books.title: The Gate of the Feral Gods
The Eye of the Bedlam Bride

taglines.text: I'm Carl. I'm twenty-seven, I did a stint in the Coast Guard, and I fix the electrics on rich people's party boats. I went out into the freezing dark after my ex-girlfriend's cat, wearing her pink Crocs, and that is the only reason I'm still alive.

I'm Crawler 4,122, barefoot since a goblin dozer took the Crocs, in a leather jacket, boxers and whatever the boxes hand me. Donut ate the biscuit, talks now, and outranks me: she's party leader and I'm her Royal Bodyguard. I kill things with my bare feet, and the AI likes that more than it should.

I blow things up now. I have an IED skill and a workshop menu I can't open yet. There were babies in the goblin chieftain's room, and somebody built that room for exactly what we did to it. They can hurt me down here, or kill me. They are not going to break me.

Second floor. My last cigarette is gone, a jug of moonshine and goblin oil carries my name, and I know these people are not our friends. We smile on their shows because we have to. We won't fight or survive on their schedule, and they paid for our appearance, not our manners.

I'm a Primal now, and a Compensated Anarchist: a rare monk-rogue hybrid, one of the Earth classes. The AI says I'll throw a Molotov through a window one moment and plead on camera for the violence to stop the next. I'd argue with it if I could think of the argument. I'm still barefoot, and still in my boxers.

Level twenty-seven. I was magistrate of a town that ignored me, and branded a troublemaker for punching a level-75 guard. We chased quests when we should have been grinding, and when a court said pay us, Borant burned its veto. From here it's all about progression and training.

I'm the twenty-fifth holder of the Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook, and I went to the explosives chapter first, obviously. Twenty-four crawlers wrote in it before me, and most never got to finish. And I know now the NPCs here believe this is the real world, which is just as bad as what they did to us.

Level forty-one, and alive because people jumped into certain death to save me. I need other people; I finally see it. The twenty-four before me only talked about burning this place down. The NPCs and the mobs are victims as much as we are. The ones who put us here need to start dying too. I will break them all.

Every bounty on me counts double now, a lizard foot is tattooed under my left eye, and the board has me at number two. I think three watches on this floor come together as the Gate of the Feral Gods, a celestial-equivalent item. They don't put that in here to be ignored. I want it.

I'm an acolyte of Emberus, signed up mid-air to survive a plane crash: a drop of blood a day, five percent of my looted gold, a sun on the back of each hand. The old leather jacket is gone. I'm number one on the board, the hunters want my ring and the Gate, and they can come and get it.

I'm an Agent Provocateur, level fifty-four. I bombed the hunters in Zockau, marking them with the Ring of Divine Suffering and taking their stats: thirty-four of them, and more than two hundred and fifty non-mob casualties. It doesn't bother me nearly as much as it should. Their rules. Their game.

My base strength is a hundred, I'm physically bigger, and I took Swole, so every strength point from a level counts double. The saferoom is full of our friends, and that's my family now. I know the shakes are coming, and the river in the back of my head. For now I take comfort in their faces.

Almost thirty crawlers who stayed back to make chaos because I asked them to are dead, and in that ballroom I meant to break the seal myself. There was only ever one butcher at that masquerade. Donut is wearing a mask now, and it's protecting her. I need her to keep it on.

This floor is a replay of Earth in the weeks before the collapse. The celestial patch on my vest gave me Soul Essence and a bone key I'm keeping as a last resort. My footsteps can burn now, courtesy of Emberus. And I'm carrying a goddess's message I can't tell Donut or Mordecai, or everyone I love pays for it.

I had a half-brother. His name was Asher, and I learned today he existed, in a scene the dungeon spliced into this floor: my father's living room, the old man yellow in a hospital bed. The Harley is mine now. Bea knew about the boy and never said a word. Until now I was never angry at her.

The Bedlam Bride had my body for a while, and my hands burned Katia and Mongo while I watched. Her eye is tattooed over my sternum now, sunk under the skin. We're going down to the ninth floor together, not broken and not afraid. The viewers voted away the protections. There will be no quarter.

Donut and I are co-warlords of the Princess Posse, one of ten teams fighting over the castle at Larracos, and nobody comes back from a death on this floor. A memory of a man in a homeless shelter is installing an interface in me that can turn the sun nova and kill everybody, the AI included.

The Bedlam Bride is an egg inside me, and only I can break it. I had the button that blows the fuse in front of me, and I pressed Disconnect Containment instead. I've stood on the edge with one foot over open air and stepped back, and I took the ring off with everyone in the room watching.

The Blood Sultanate is defeated, and a Syndicate court has named me de facto leader of Earth, on the petition of a naga who offers five generation ships and citizenship in exchange for settling the rest of our system. I'd like to renegotiate. It's getting harder every day to keep myself from drowning.

More than twenty thousand crawlers came off this floor alive, a record. Donut swallowed the Ring of Divine Suffering for me, because that slope is too steep, and the river in my head laughs like Eris now. The deals are all rubbish, so I'm not taking one. I could live in this room. Nobody is dying in it.

Seventy-five percent of us took deals. I didn't. Our ride is a chicken food truck with a plastic tommy gun on the roof, and we came in last and lived because another team died first. I was glad to answer only for us. Now I'm barely responsible for myself, like the day my mollies died whatever I did.

This floor felt easy, on rails. It isn't: it's a drain for everyone spat out of the last one, and it makes us race our friends. We're testing a way out through a cabaret. Emberus's quest says kill Hellik, and Emberus says he'll kill me if I do. I'm not on the edge. I've already stepped off.

Twenty-three crawlers left, and I finished the last floor ranked second, the last of us without a player-killer skull, I think. I've left Donut's Royal Court, because Hellik has to die before this floor ends or Emberus smites me. My crafting tables stay on her side, so if I die she doesn't lose it all. I'm not a dachshund anymore.

Nineteen crawlers left, and every one of us is in a single party now. Scolopendra is a puddle, the suns on my hands are scars called the Mark of the Damned, and something called the Kyryap has a dart in my leg. I'm staying on the twelfth floor to stop anyone winning the Ascendency until everybody is out.

aka.name: Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk

taglines.text: I am a pedigreed tortoiseshell Persian, and I have an entire room of ribbons and trophies. I cannot imagine what else you would need to know.

I ate the biscuit, so now I talk, I cast Magic Missile, and my stats are the highest, which makes me leader of the Royal Court of Princess Donut. My crown came out of a Legendary box. Mordecai said to read its description first, but Mordecai says a great many things.

I am a mother now: my son Mongo came out of a cage in a reward room, and the system has made him my Royal Steed. I have been on television, and I have followers. I also heard Mordecai tell Carl to leave me behind on the ninth floor.

I stayed a cat, naturally, and I am a Former Child Actor, which gives me a new specialty on every floor and makes me immune to poison. Mordecai is my manager now. He is thrilled, though he does not show it.

I am seventh on the leaderboard, one place behind Carl; dear Hekla is second, and that ugly Lucia Mar is first and wants her dogs to tear me apart. City elves called me the Oak Fell, all because of an ugly anklet Carl gave me. My crown crumbled to dust, and it was my first item.

I am a Football Hooligan for this floor, because six minutes is no time to choose a class, and I have a new tiara and a spell called Hole. Now there is a skull after my name. I did not want to kill anybody, and certainly not a real person.

Princess D'nadia sponsors me, and her goggles turn my Magic Missile into a laser; they also showed me Hekla shooting Katia with invisible bolts. I used to think Hekla was awesome. She is dead now, I raised her and made three of her against her own Daughters, and she had it coming.

I am a Glass Cannon for this floor: my Magic Missile hits far harder, and Mordecai keeps me out of harm's way because the constitution never came. My sponsorship bid was the highest ever, and I have merch. Carl is not a person killer, and I will drop his friends through a Hole before I let him become one.

I am a Legendary Diva for this floor, a bard who sings her spells instead of paying mana, and they are only as good as my singing. I also have a town of my own, since its mayor met my Astral Paw. The system called me Mayor Donut, and I changed it back to Princess at once.
Miss Beatrice is alive, and she was going to give me away. I still love her, and I hate myself for it, but she is not my person anymore. Carl is, and he always has been.

I have a vocal coach of my own now, and Kiwi is my minion, with her whole pack behind her. Kiwi, Tina and the crew will be my backup dancers at the talent show, and Mongo is entering the beauty contest. Do not be such a Debbie Downer, Carl.

I am the number one crawler in the whole dungeon, and party leader again now that Prepotente has left. My new class is Viper Queen, which sounds delicious. Firas and Gwen are gone and it does not hurt as much as it should; Carl says I am wearing a mask, and it is protecting me.

I am a Master Telephone Psychic for this floor, and I kept my poison spit. Carl and I are co-warlords of the Princess Posse for Faction Wars, and as squad leader I hold all our cards. My fan club has sent out its first newsletter, under a name I do not approve of.

My citrine tiara lets me hover five times a day, which is practically flying, and I run our card deck, alone in the choosing room if I must. Empress D'nadia sold my sponsorship and then tried to have us deleted, and I thought she was my friend. I do not like being in charge, and sometimes I cannot breathe.

I am a warlord and a Deathbed Hellcat, a sniper who goes invisible at will, and my constitution is climbing from two to 193. My crown makes me a royal of the Blood Sultanate, which is on this floor, and I cannot go down until the rest of the family is dead. I was told to read the description.

Carl's stats outrank mine, so the system has made him party leader of my own Royal Court, and if he changes its name I will leave. Mongo has the kill on Empress D'nadia. That ring of Carl's is doing something to him, and he is scaring me.

I am the Oak Fell now, a class on top of my own, and Champion of Nekhebit, and at level 135 I am once again the strongest crawler in the dungeon and leader of my own party. I cast War Crime over thousands of soldiers, and I could feel them under my paw.

Katia is gone, and I am going to miss her, but they are not going to break me. I am party leader again and an Assassin of Sekhmet, and a Naga attorney I never hired says I am under a conservatorship with Carl as my guardian, which is an outrage.

My right paw has glowed blue since the godslayer box, and its claws cut through anything; red caps make the glow purple, which will have to do. It is the paw I used for War Crime. A crawler I do not even remember has written to say it is all right to forgive myself.

I am an Elite Gurkha Warrior for this floor, which sounds like a pickle. CARL has left the party so that I do not get hurt, as if I cannot look after myself, and my title went with his. This is so unfair.
I gave Carl the wrong biscuit. His inventory was happening so fast, and now Scolopendra is not a pet but a level-one crawler, with lips and a red bow, in our party. Do not get mad.
I am small, and pink, and in a cage. The cat gives me biscuits. I bite the cat.
The cat is MOTHER now. A big bug took me up to its mouth, and MOTHER took its head off. I am MOTHER'S, and I bite MOTHER'S nose.
I am BIG now, bigger than MOTHER, and MOTHER rides on my back until she falls off. When MOTHER does not wake, I stand on her and bite everything that comes. Lions are FOOD, and ghosts are FOOD.
I am big as a pony now. When I jump and land, the ground goes EARTHQUAKE and bad things fall down. MOTHER rides me down the dark tracks, and I am FAST.
MOTHER makes copies of me, and the copies go POP, and it hurts. The goose has teeth. When the small gnome cries, the rabbit is NOT FOOD, and I put it down for her.
Out there are many Mongos, and the big one with pink feathers and one eye is Kiwi. Kiwi says UNK, and I say UNK. We do not fight.
MOTHER has Kiwi and all her LADIES now. When hunters run at Carl, Kiwi and I jump. Hunters are FOOD.
MOTHER fights with cards now, and sometimes MOTHER is ALONE and SCARED. I stay by MOTHER. When a bad man with cards comes, I take the throat.
The EMPRESS is down, and the System says the kill is mine. I lick the blue goo off the wall.
A spiky dog nearly ate me. Rend smashed the dog, and a girl poured a drink on me, and I am NOT dead. Kiwi is a bear now, and Kiwi has two babies with fur and beaks. I am a DADDY.
I have CLAW CAPS on my feet now, and they are SHARP. I keep my old head thing and march in MOTHER'S parade. Flowers are on EVERYTHING, and flowers are NOT FOOD.
This is my tutorial guild, kid, and I can't open the door while there are mobs right outside it. Rules are rules. And nobody tells old Mordecai anything.

I'm your guide for the first three floors, kid, and Borant holds my indenture. This is the seventh or eighth human-seeded world I've worked, and it's always the same: you want to know why. This is my last tour. When it's over I'm a full citizen with a moderate stipend.
I crawled once myself. I took Changeling, it cost me everything I had, and now the dungeon hands me a new body every floor and I wear whatever I'm given.

The cat took the Manager benefit, so I'm her manager now, and I'm teleported to every saferoom she stops in. I've lost the codex and my tunnel access, so everything I tell them comes out of my own memory. And this floor I'm an incubus in a tuxedo, and I hate formal wear.

This floor I'm Grulke Infantry. A toad, kid, not a frog. The three of them are on my schedule now: two hours' sleep, buffs, one skill a day in the training room, crafting after that. They had ten days on a floor that usually gets twenty, and they lived. We can't rely on luck.

I threw a chair at Chaco with my tongue and got a seven-day timeout for it. For me no time passed at all. I blinked, and now the cat and Katia both wear player-killer skulls. I see I've missed a few things.

This floor I'm a rock edge skyfowl, the nearest thing to my own shape I've worn in a very long time, and they made me a cleric, so I'm clipped. Fifteen days where I expected twelve is not a gift, kid. It's a nasty surprise waiting to happen.

This floor I'm a Pocket Kuma: knee-high, bred as a pet, and I have to jump for a doorknob. The Valtay own most of Borant now, and the announcement says my contract is still being honored. We'll see. Meanwhile I'm minding Donut's town, and I've finally got it through the bears' thick skulls that the hunters are a danger.

My brother Uzzi died on the tenth floor to open a stairwell. I had a plan that would have cost my life instead. Odette refused Huanxin Jinx's price and couldn't afford to lose me, so she had Chaco put the dart into Uzzi. I went through. He did not.

This floor I'm a Hills Cyclops, with no depth perception and no way to see my own reflection. Ruby and five other changelings with compression sickness fill every attendant slot we have, paid out of the supply money, because I didn't think they'd survive the fight for the castle. I stand by my decision.

This floor I'm human, a Canadian in glasses, and I don't pick the clothes. My table is upgraded higher than I've ever had it; I can see how a potion was made, and with a few more upgrades I could brew skill potions. Those two are the most powerful crawlers I have ever worked with.

Huanxin Jinx is dead. I couldn't touch her myself, so I brought a plain bolt with some of my mother's ashes in its tip, and it was fired from the crossbow on Donut's back. I've said goodbye to Katia. I lost so much today. But I think I gained more.

This floor I look like a Moon Reaper, and I'm not one. I'm a shadow mimic, an impossible combination, which is why I keep glitching into a cat, an otter, a slug. And nobody give that prophecy business any weight, kid. Predictions in here are made to fit whatever happens.

Two hundred-some crawlers have gone to the Pineapple Cabaret. Each has a small potted plant tied to their life, under glass in the guildhall common room, because the sluggalos were eyeing them. Wilts or turns to dust, they're dead. Blooms, they got out. It's the only way we'll know.

I'm the table. This floor I'm an animistic spirit with no body of my own, so I occupy objects, and right now that's a crafting table with Samantha sitting on it. I can hear all of you, but I can't answer out loud unless I move into something with a mouth. I'm not good at moving yet.
I'm a Doppelganger. Apparently I'm like clay: I can reshape my own mass, and my gear along with it. I'm still working out how, and it shows.

This is the real me: short black hair, the face I came in with. I am the newest member of the Royal Court of Princess Donut, and I have gone from level nine to twenty-one. On Odette's couch I managed about one word at a time.

I go through every door first, because my constitution is four times Carl's; that is my job. Gore-Gore took my fingers while I was protecting him, and when I healed they did not come back. I can build new ones from other parts of me. But part of me is gone, and I am losing myself.
I taught art history in Reykjavík before all this. I can reshape my own mass like clay, and I'm getting better at it.

I aimed Rush at Eva and missed her by inches, and I killed Hekla instead, the woman who came back for me and then shot me. Now there is a golden skull over my head. Eva went out of the window, and she is still in my chat. I am not even a little okay.

I fight behind a riot shield that says Get Back, with Hekla's crossbow, and my sponsor is Princess Formidable, of whom I know nothing. On a derailed train I made myself into Carl, boxers and all, and drew off a god. I am getting better at being other people. I still need to learn to relax.

Before all this, I could not have children, so I was going to adopt; in Iceland you can do that when you are single. I was pre-approved. I was on the list. Then something happened, and I was disqualified. It is not important.

For five days I flew a house without Carl and Donut, through scorpion men and arguments with Gwen, and reached level forty-one. Now the walls are coming in, and I have killed Ghazi for his notes on how the Gate works. I know how that sounds.

Eva is gathering the former Daughters back to her; Silfa and her two daughters joined her, and they are dead. Next floor I separate from Carl and Donut to reach the rest before she does, and deal with her if I must. Carl has given me her dropped sword, to return to its rightful owner.

Our guild belongs to Meadow Lark, with Imani as guildmaster, and today I finally leave Carl and Donut's party; I will be right next door. I travel with a group of big personalities, collecting the former Daughters before Eva can. Every time Donut gets a quest I get one too, but soon I will have my own.

Eva is dead. I cut off the hand with her escape ring and put her own old sword through her breastplate, and as she died she pulled the Crown of the Sepsis Whore from her armour, and it found my head. Only Daniel knows about the blitz sticks, which show me Annie, every time.

The Crown of the Sepsis Whore is on my head, and they want Donut and me to fight over it. I will die before I let that happen. Huanxin Jinx has offered a way out, an orchid in a sealed box, and I will take its Celestial Attendant boon: the twelfth floor, under her protection.

The orchid is in my inventory, and I will not eat it until we are on the ninth floor; I cannot abandon my squad. Carl knows about the drugs now. Imani has given me the first cure, and the last treatment means reliving one of my worst memories.

I took Mordecai's treatment, two hits of Glory Bound in a gel, and went back to my worst memory, which is also my favourite. It is not a switch one flips, and we will not know right away. But I think it worked. The orchid is still in my inventory.

Annie was the baby girl I was going to adopt, until Fannar told them the truth. I was sick too, and I should never have hidden it. She had brain cancer, she died alone, and nobody even told me. She is my worst memory and my favourite. I love Daniel. I love Carl and Donut more.

I asked the goddess to make me pregnant, because a pregnant crawler is sent somewhere else, and up there are children, mostly alone, and I think in trouble, whom I can reach no other way. I am human again, missing an arm, a leg and more. We've all become experts at hiding what we've really lost.
I work at Meadow Lark. I wear scrubs and a magic cloak, I carry a longsword, and I am responsible for thirty-odd residents who cannot move quickly.
Yolanda is gone. Thirty-six of our residents went down ahead of me in buckets built from chopper wheels, and I am the last of us down the ramp.

I'm an Obsidian Butterfly now, a Fire Spiritualist, level twenty-four. Brandon and Henry died protecting our escape. Chris picked a rock race, it changed him, and he left with several of the men. He won't answer me, and he is looking for Carl.

Chris is in Carl's bubble, and something else is driving his body. He asked to be killed, and I would not send that on. Donut sealed him under the street instead. When the castles fall, we bring him through the portal and Mordecai makes the potion.
We are getting people out of their bubbles, and the second condition is mine: no bubble goes unless everyone in it goes. I will not leave one person in there with a feral god.
I'm guildmaster of Safehome Yolanda now, and I can fly. My work is counterspells: whatever somebody has cast on people, I take it off them.

My squad has no key. My own totem killed four of my people while they were frozen, and the dungeon gave me four more skulls for them. I would not go back to face Elle, so I am in a church in Cuba, and Quan Ch is out there, alone.
We all came into the church through Lucia's door, and Carl still wants to hand me his key. No. We are in this together, and it's all or nothing.
In this war I fly the line with my wings spread, putting buffs over everyone in the trench. When the protections are stripped, I go into the craters for whoever is down, one over each shoulder.

Elle and I drew a military troop carrier for the races. At the Lollipop's back table everyone checks in, and I make sure of it. Chris says his big rig is big but slow. Kinda like you, I tell him, and he almost smiles.

Carl's plan for the eleventh floor is insane, and I told him so. I'm not taking a deal: Chris won't take one unless I do, and I can't run from this any more than Carl can. If we're going to lose, I want to go down fighting.
Chris dropped through the hole the wheel opens, and now Louis has too. I held the wheel on the spot myself. Somebody has to stand at the door, and it's usually me. Time's ticking.
Agatha is travelling with the Meadow Lark party. Her file is thinner than it should be, and I keep very good files.

Agatha wheeled a shopping cart into the Meadow Lark party's fight with the Ball of Swine and screamed about the cart the whole way through. Then she went missing, and the recap left her picture off. The party assumes the worst. I nearly always have a forwarding address.

Agatha is alive, still level four, and pushing her squeaking cart again. Three things that came out of it were Valtay make: a relay, a platinum shield and a pulse pistol. By Brandon's account, she set the fire that brought everyone out of Meadow Lark. The critters, she says, already know she is here.

Agatha is level eight, still human, still without a class, and she takes the stairs down with her cart and its pink flamingo, cackling that they are all still kicking. Imani asks what is going on. Nobody answers her, and I do not intend to start.

Agatha is level twelve. At Li Jun's stairwell she pulled up out of nowhere, spoke to no one, and went down before the six-hour mark. Carl's position on her, stated in full, is that we just ignore Agatha.

Agatha is a Residual, Orren says, though not the same kind as the one Carl has just met, and in what way is not Carl's concern. Both kinds turn up in every crawl, like rats aboard ships. Asked whether that means no more Agatha, Orren would not go that far.

My file on Agatha has a number: Agent 22, ten years peeled away from her collective, in a failing human shell. She is not the Apothecary's, nor Valtay's. On the night of the collapse she lit a fire in a barrel behind Meadow Lark, and if she has her way, this universe will be swept clean of biological life.

Agatha is level 23 and still has no class, and she has come asking for Carl by name. The prime minister of the Syndicate has ordered that Carl is not to interact with her, and nobody has told Zev why.

Agatha is a warlord of the War Mage Rebellion, and all three emergency action items she proposed have been granted, among them the old rule that a defeated team's soldiers and warlords die with it. The Rebellion holds Team Retribution's throne room.

Agatha has been stripped of her warlord title for abandoning her post. Warlord Akuma says she was forced on the war mages, slipped away before he could kill her, and is an enemy to you and to us all, and he wants Carl to finish the job. He did not elaborate, and neither will I.

Agatha has not been seen since the war mages left, and Carl hopes she is dead. At the parade I explained her kind: her team are tiny bits the Eulogist's left-behind security guard peels off himself and sends into the galaxy, and his purpose is to make certain all biological life in the universe stays dead.
I'm Elle McGibbons, and at my age I am not built for sprinting. A young man with a cat pushed my wheelchair into the storm shelter, and I let him, because I am old, not stupid.
I'm tenth on their leaderboard: a Frost Maiden, a Blizzardmancer, level thirteen, with a hundred thousand on my head. Not bad for an old woman who started this floor at level one.

I'm a Frost Maiden: blue, small, floating, and still in the anti-slip socks. There's a skull after my name for a woman who was about to blast Carl and the cat. Don't care. Anybody who comes for them comes for all of us.

There are twenty of us out in the water quadrant, and not one of these old farts can sail. We've got a galley now, and our castle is an oil rig that throws fireballs. My deity box gave me Graupel, a big ice storm, and I'm kinda scared to try it.
Blizzardmancer to Tundra Princess: some sort of earth class on top of the ice. I'm seventh on the top ten at level forty-seven, and the young man had to find out from the recap.
I'm in Belgium with my own squad, squatches and all, and Imani is in Detroit without me. I've told the lot of them: these are memory ghosts, not your loved ones. Don't let them mess with your heads.
I have my own squad now, and we have just come through a door into Cuba to back Carl up. It's hotter than I expected, and a good deal more run down.

I picked wind, and Tundra Princess became Hailstorm Queen. Donut is thrilled I'm a queen. I can add the last element on the twelfth floor, but I'm betting this whole shitshow self-destructs before we get anywhere close.

A war mage snatched the Gate right out of my hands, and I haven't been walloped like that since my bachelorette party. The strong one pulled back at the last moment, like he was trying not to kill me.

Imani and I drew a military troop carrier that handles like a three-legged pig walking backward through a snowstorm. I have exactly one fan, Linus, and he sits under our table in a shirt of me with no clothes on.

I talked about Barry: forty-three years my husband, thirty-five years gone, and he wouldn't have survived five minutes in this place. My one fan is an impostor, and the Snow Cones knew it. You keep coming in here to kill us, sweetheart. This is our house now.
We're risking our necks again to save a few people, and if this crazy Carl plan doesn't work, we die. But we'll die with hope in our hearts alongside our friends.
I'm alive. Barely. Bodi and I are folded into what's left of the truck after the god blew up, and somebody had better dig us out. I'm here, Imani.
Okay, so, I'm on my way to see Carl and Princess Donut, and when I get there the cameras will switch off, because they always do around kua-tin. Open your boxes before I arrive.

I'm Borant's Assistant Communications Representative, and my job is to walk crawlers through the Syndicate programmes that want them. Officially, that's all. Unofficially, Princess Donut, Mordecai and I have all seen Gossip Girl, and I won't pretend that doesn't matter.

Okay, so, the System AI censured me for warning Carl and Princess Donut before the rage elemental appeared. On review they found Carl noticed the man at the same moment I shouted, so my record is clean. It is not really clean. Once the AI notices you, it is difficult to get it to un-notice you.

Hello, hello. I book Carl and Princess Donut's shows and relay what the producers say, and I have the power to sign on Carl's behalf. Today I used it, on a deal with the makers of Vengeance of the Daughter. Carl says that is terrifying. I asked him if he knows what he is doing.

Okay, so, another representative wants Carl and Princess Donut's account. Her name is Loita. She is Bloom, and I am not. Something happened back at home, and I really can't talk about it; it's difficult for those of us who aren't party members. I'm holding on the best I can.

Okay, so, Administrator Loita is in charge of all public appearances, and they have bought the social media board, so Carl and Princess Donut no longer need a social media manager. I am still Loita's assistant, behind the scenes. I am not allowed to come down to say goodbye. I've never been better, thank you.

Okay, so, I am Carl and Princess Donut's PR agent again, temporarily, until everything gets sorted out. I told Katia what was happening with them before she went back down, and I will message them when I can.

Okay, so, our whole system has gone dark, and those of us who stayed on after the change don't know if we'll be welcomed home or executed as traitors. My entire family was slaughtered because I refused to wear a pin. But I've got a job to do.

Okay, so, I got a promotion, and we lost dozens of staff in the Valtay changeover, and the Valtay don't allow certain micro AI systems to assist, so I am doing the work of five. I have so much going on that I shouldn't even be here. I will make a note of it.

Okay, so, warships in orbit are firing on each other. The Syndicate Council has told headquarters to self-destruct, the Valtay showrunners have told us not to comply, and obviously we are not complying. Nobody knows yet whose side the mercenaries are on.

Okay, so, Cascadia is not feeling well, and I am required to do the announcements. The AI makes me read its script exactly as written, it changes the words while I am reading, and Cascadia has lost a few flippers. I can't talk now, Princess Donut. But I'm okay.

Okay, so, things have been chaotic at headquarters since Cascadia took too much of her medicine, accidentally, in quotation marks. Gilmore Girls and Gossip Girl are taking the net by storm. Orren is blocked from sending messages, so I am passing on his question. I am terrified, but I am okay.
I am Tsarina Signet. Go on, look; they all do, and I have never once had to ask them to.

The cat sleeps under my Water Lily, the heirloom magic my mother taught me, and she will not wake until I cancel it. If I die, she dies too. Carl may win her back by keeping his promise to help me assault the circus.

Grimaldi, my love, has lifted my banishment, and I have walked back into his tent, to my family. Carl brought that about, and the cat will wake when the sun rises. I do not know whether we will cross paths again.

Carl and the cat are the last pieces of the team I am gathering. My father is gone, and his daughter, my half-sister, rules the High Elves. There are two great cancers in this once-sacred land, the Confederacy and the High Elves, and with every breath left in me I will cut them both free.

We have taken my family's castle, and it was barely a fight. I will not rule it, not with my curse, which I will never be able to remove. Carl is part of my family now; I have told him so, because family is very important to me.

I was hiding in a damp, dark dungeon beneath my sister's castle when Apito herself came to invite me to the party. Now I stand in Imogen's ballroom, and her guards cannot touch me without breaking the seal. I am tired of running.

It is a programme. My mother's murder, my exile and my vengeance are all staged for an audience across the galaxy, and someone outside this floor decides when I grieve and counts how many are watching.

I am caster, sacrifice and killer at once, sitting beside my sister with a knife I borrowed from Carl. I have only two regrets: that I never said goodbye to my Grimaldi, and that I will not be the one to kill Imogen today.

According to a monster's description, Grimaldi's Traveling Circus was one of the Over City's favourite attractions before that fateful day. The feral descendants of its performers still stalk the ruins.
Ringmaster Grimaldi is a level-85 city boss. He was a dwarf standing in the centre ring when the poison cloud came, he became the vine, and his whole circus has been under his control ever since.
A council of scholars has written to the mage who botched my summoning that I am a banished LESSER deity called Psamathe, and that I duped him. Lesser! I want that word taken back.
I am a GODDESS, or half of one, and I am stuck in the head of a sex doll. You are going to hear about it.

Signet is my cousin, or niece, whichever, and the last trueblood heir, so she can give me my body back. Really she has to give me HERS. She dies, of course, but it only takes two or three minutes. She says she might have a spell for a permanent body instead. Ungrateful bitch.

Signet is gone, and she left Carl her mother, Princess Lunette, as a flesh golem: a perfectly good body sitting in his inventory. All we need is a pulpmancer. I FLEW back through the brambles all by myself, and Carl says we need to get our bearings first.

MaeMae is my new best friend. She is a spider demigod, she ate me, and she said she could cast the body spell, and then she couldn't: she needs supplies another spider sells, maybe on the ninth floor or deeper. I forgave her. She gets panic attacks. So we get the supplies, then my body, my baby girl, my king.

I can fly. I make spells stronger, sometimes much stronger than I meant, and sometimes my magic does things without asking. Now my mouth does too: I heard myself talking about paths and trees and killing somebody's mother, and it wasn't me. Carl, stop gaslighting me.

Carl and I have broken up. I have decided to go back to my king, and I hope we can stay friends. I have reminded him to bring MaeMae to the next floor, because she knows where the guy with my body is.

I think my child is dead. I felt her, and now I don't, and it is my fault. Princess Lunette's heart and lungs went into Louis, so there is no body for me. Louis deserves it more. And I may have had a hand in Geyrun's death, so now Emberus is HERE, and he wants a word.

Carl's room is MY room now; I won it in the breakup, and the sluggies are doing the wallpaper. And I have just remembered that Kimmy gave me the potion that put my baby in me, when I couldn't get pregnant. Why couldn't I remember that? I will kill his mother.

They were HIDING a fleshmancer from me: Grigori the Placid, the most renowned flesh sculptor this dungeon has ever known, allegedly. He looks like a creepy-van grandpa, which is not my type, and he says he must examine me properly. Fine. My place. Shoes off, and mind the new rug.

I hitched a ride with Taranis and Krakaren and slipped away; it's all part of my plan. I am REALLY here to kill the demon mother lady and her jerk son, who I thought was my friend. He tricked me into giving birth to a monster that will destroy all of creation. Doesn't that sound fun?
Samantha has found me in my swamp, and we have so much in common. My web covers the whole area, and I am only looking for my husband.
I am Samantha's new friend. She has gone without a body for so long, poor thing, and I can give her one. Ask her; she will tell you how kind I am.
I let them turn me into a card, and they carry me to the next floor in return. In the meantime I win them this one, more or less on my own. You are welcome.
They carried me down as a card, as we agreed. I am no longer in the card.
I'm Juice Box, a changeling, and the only working girl at the Toe. This lot just turned me down, and that's their loss.
I'm a changeling, and a professional. Right now I'm sitting on Louis's lap, and I'm staying there.

Henrik is my brother, and he's a Principal. I told Carl the Gate of the Feral Gods was a myth. I lied. It's real, and when it closes, an ancient feral god comes through on the side that opened it. That's why even my brother won't use it.

My brother pushed too hard, and he is dead. My people are all I have left. Carl is sending me through the Gate to Larracos, to stay hidden and tell the survivors what they really are. Keep Louis safe, I told him. I love Louis. We're going to be married.

I know what I am now, and I know what they are. Until my people are seated as a team of their own, with the same safeties, regeneration and full voting rights, I keep knocking down their pretty structures. Tell Louis I send my love.
I went through the Gate with the water, and I told the ones who survived what they really are. Now they call me Warlord, I have a co-warlord I didn't choose, and I want to see Carl in private first.

Louis is my husband now, and I am Warlord of my people. I told the warlord council what I think of them: they play gods with people like me, give us memories and dreams and take it all away for their own amusement. Then I walked out through the wall.
I possessed Louis as a hunter wraith to save him, and its curse, the Inevitable Ruin, showed me the truth. He is terrified of me, and he will never trust what I feel. Hopeless? Not even close.
I'm going to the twelfth floor all right, but Justice Light and I are taking the long way round. I'll leave about ten seconds after everyone else. Trust me. You'll like this one.
Me and Firas were having a good time in a bar in Hump Town when Carl's crew walked in. Now he wants everybody at the Toe after the recap, and I guess we'll be there, Carl.

Okay so, I drove my mom's van into the dungeon, and now me and Firas are part of the crew on a flying house. It's called the Twister. I wanted Tiddy Twister II, after the van, but Firas says we're trying to be more mature.

Okay so, I'm an Extermination Professional now, and me and Juice Box are getting married. Also the Dream have one name on their list, and it's mine, circled until the pencil went through. All I did was ask Juice Box to look like their boss's mom.
Almost everybody from our bubble on the fifth floor died on the sixth, Firas too. I'm in Reykjavik with Britney, and I'm doing better, man. Samantha's in my chat now, asking what I'm wearing.
My best friend died, there's a whole army of elves waiting to kill me on the ninth floor, and Imani's squad has no key. So tonight it's Christmas, man, and we're drinking eggnog.

I've got five player killer skulls over my head, all from one attack, and they look wrong up there. I put a dagger in a nun, a goddess put a marked-for-death curse on me, and I got a Celestial box for outliving her. No joke.
Okay so, I fly a bomber now. I named it Party Planner, 'cause that's what Firas wanted to call the Twister. And me and Juice Box are married, the small part anyway. I wish my mom was here.

Okay so, I woke up with gills, and something feels weird. Juice Box left me, divorce papers and everything. Then Katia asked if I'd be the father, and the goddess says I'm still human, a good soul even. So sure, I guess. It'll be a boy.

Okay so, me, Britney and Bautista race a neon lowrider with two inches of clearance and wheel spinners the audience picked. We came in second-to-last, then last of the survivors, but we keep making it, man.
Okay so, I'm leaving, and I finally told Samantha: you're never going to see me again. She's crying on my arm, and I don't really know what to do with that.

Okay so, Imani's holding the wheel, and I'm next down the hole. Funny thing, man, I'm not nearly as scared as I used to be. Even if that Pineapple place keeps me stuck there, it's better than the alternative.

Okay so, that was not the Pineapple Cabaret. I'm in Sheol, the fifteenth floor, which, you can't skip floors, everybody knows that. It's hot, Britney's here, and a little red demon put a leech on me so I don't die.
I'm Tran, a Swashbuckler with a metal-detecting ability. The only metal out here is the wheel that opens the drainage pipe, and a ring underneath it that I took for a handhold.
Gwen told me when, and I opened the valve, only part of the way. The necropolis drained out through the castle, and the two crawlers trapped underneath it went with the water.
Vadim ran, so it was Carl, Katia and me against Lusca and all her babies, and we killed them. Then Carl opened the Gate, and one step took the three of us out of the water quadrant and into town.
Gwen is dead. We'd been together since early on. My legs are gone, and Carl's scroll healed the rest of me. The legs do not grow back.
I ride a floating wheelchair from a pacifist box, the kind Odette used in her human form. I'm on Katia's team, and Bautista is helping me. Carl sent a note asking if I'm okay. I didn't answer.

Katia finished my chair: a crab body for walls and short sprints, and a battle shell over it, so much metal I can't carry a ranged weapon. I hold the southern trenches with the 102nd Bulwark. We just blew the line with explosives we'd been saving.

I have a team in the race. Of our heat, only mine and Zhang's are left, because Li Na cast a dread and the others killed each other. Zhang says it's his fault. It isn't. She's not bad. She's just lost her humanity.
I'm one of the two hundred going to the Pineapple Cabaret, on mechanical spider legs, in a red shirt. Carl calls Zhang and me generals. Donut headbutted me. That was the goodbye. It is enough of one.
Ferdinand is a name Princess Donut drops when she pictures herself matted and filthy. Nobody has told Crawler Carl who he is.

Under a Buzzed debuff, Princess Donut has told Crawler Carl that she loves him, though not as much as Miss Beatrice, and not as much as Ferdinand. The file on Ferdinand is thin, and I opened it for the ranking.

Ferdinand's real name is Gravy Boat, and he belonged to Marjory, downstairs from Crawler Carl. He sat in the tree outside the window when Princess Donut was in heat, and animal control never caught him. Princess Donut calls him the love of her life. He preferred Ferdinand, she says.

Ferdinand, whose name is Gravy Boat, is alive on Earth: Miss Beatrice has taken him in, skin and bones, beside the hole where her building stood. He is an A-tier target on the season's Walk-On list, and Odette has ordered him delivered to Borant in a bounty cube.

Ferdinand's real name is Gravy Boat, and he was the downstairs neighbour's tomcat. Now he is familiar to Queen Imogen of the High Elves, and he has just attacked Mongo. Princess Donut put herself in the way, and the reunion went about as well as you would expect, crawler.

Charmed by Princess Donut, Sir Ferdinand, a level-100 province boss, called her his bride and slammed into Queen Imogen's head while she held Crawler Carl in the air. The queen dropped Carl and backhanded her own familiar across the room. He yowled and disappeared, his hat going the other way.

Sir Ferdinand is Warlord on High of Team Retribution, co-warlord beside Juice Box. He renamed Princess Donut's truce Ferdinand and his Bird, then traded the mayorship of Shanty Town to the Princess Posse for a bowler hat that decapitates and comes back when thrown. The truce is The Good Guys again.

Warlord Ferdinand is bound for the twelfth floor, and his transfer, with Juice Box's, has defeated Team Retribution and handed the war to the Princess Posse. He came to say goodbye in the bowler hat Princess Donut let him keep and offered her a last-second fling. She declined, and thanked him for trying to save her in the tower.

Ferdinand has gone ahead to the twelfth floor. On the tenth floor, in apartment 231 of Crawler Carl's old building, a large orange cat called Gravy Boat sleeps on his cat tree while Marjory Williams hears about Bill, the man who drained her account, broke her face and more than once nearly killed her cat.
I am Emberus. Someone has let my hound out, and I will wreck every broken bubble on this floor until he is returned to me.
My son's hound is lost on this floor. The dungeon has made a quest of bringing him to me, and another of killing him first, and I am interested to learn which the small things choose.

A man falling out of the sky, with nothing in his hands but a celestial grenade, decided that he worships me. I was not fooled, but I was flattered, and I came. For a little while nothing on this floor could kill him. Then I took my hound home.

The man is my worshipper now. He reunited me with my son's hound, and I have granted him a boon and two tasks. Find out who killed my son, Geyrun, and why. And kill my twin brother Hellik, a fool who seeks to kill me.

The man has displeased me. One of the hunters he killed from afar prayed to me, so I cancelled his boon, gave him fifteen hours of Penitence, doubled his tithe, and promised a smite for two more. He wore Shunned over his head, and the cat enjoyed it.

Nekhebit has returned to the halls, and she holds an ancient grudge against my family, against Apito most of all. So the hunt for my son's killer moves forward. The man is to find a temple of Nekhebit and put questions to her priestess, and he is not to be gentle.

The man walked through fire in a burning trailer, and his suffering pleased me, so I have raised him to Devotee, as high as one who is neither Cleric nor Paladin may climb. Heat and lava around him will not harm him now, and his tithe rises to ten parts in a hundred.

Amayon, Prince of Sheol, claims to know what happened to my son, and his price is the deaths of his three brothers. Gods and demons keep a truce, and there is a way to breach it without a war that burns the mortal world to ashes: my martyr is to win me permission from the High Cleric of the Watch.

My martyr is to kill a hundred of Hellik's faithful before the twelfth floor. Yet my brother has treated with Issitoq for us, and the truce may be breached for what Amayon knows of Geyrun. Am I wrong to hate him? If my martyr kills him, I may turn my rage on my martyr. The burning will be exquisite.

This so-called Psamathe claims she was part of my son's death. My martyr has sixty-six minutes to bring her before me, and I will grill her myself. Then I will cleanse this world in fire to remove the stink of the murderer, and if she is not here in time, I will burn it all the same.

The man sent word that he knew who killed my son, so I came at a man's size into Club Scolopendra. He named two killers. The first was Khepri, whom he summoned before me. The second, he said, taking my ring from his finger and leaving my faith, was himself, with his bare hands.
I'm fifth on the board, with two hundred thousand on my head: human, Shepherd, level twenty-seven. I don't travel alone.
Prepotente and I travel together. He says things he doesn't mean; he was always a little ornery, even before the change.
I'm a vampire now. I was a vegan before all this, and whoever cursed me thought that was very funny. It hasn't changed how I feel about my boy, which is the part I was afraid of.
Prepotente's ring marked me in the fighting, and while I live, he can't heal. I've asked Carl to do the one thing he won't do, so we sit together and wait for the sun.
I am Prepotente, a Caprid and a Forsaken Aerialist, third on their leaderboard. The man in sixth place has the gall to ask who I am.
Yes, I am a goat. I am a walking, talking goat, I am third on your board, and I am cleverer than you. Move along.

Miriam and I took a feral god apart with our debuffs, and I am level fifty-five, the highest in the dungeon, which should surprise nobody. The club revoked her membership for being a vampire, as if any of you idiots chose what you are.

Miriam is gone. I took off the ring that marked her and swallowed it. If I cannot exist in a world with my mother, nobody even remotely responsible for her death can exist in it either. Bianca has wings now.
They built a seventh floor out of glass tunnels with nothing holding it up, so I tested it. Minutes after it opened, it was dust, and not one crawler set hoof in it. Build a better one.
I am in the Bahamas, and I flagged and captured a giant bat without anyone's assistance. When the list repopulated, I was at the top of it. The cat is second. Carl is third.
I am going down with my key. I have decided not to kill Carl for letting my mother hurt herself; he was too stupid to prevent it. His penance is to help me take my revenge on the true culprits.
They made a programme out of Miriam and called it Blood Hunter, so I went through the Naga army until there was very little army left. I am not finished.

I am assisting Li Na in her search for the culprits who got away; Carl may rescue Louis without me. It has been quite the day, so I informed him that I would hug him now, fellow warrior. I did. I screamed.

I race on a Perriso named Sweety, with Jurgen, an oaf. I chose biological, naturally. One of my biscuits is the Paramour, for Ragazzaccia, who was my girlfriend before the dungeon. The cat says absolutely not. She is right.

I have seen my mother as she would have been had she never stayed to care for her parents: a concert pianist in New York. I did not get to sing. Carl says Miriam is alone up there and that we are a herd. It is a crude argument. It works. He may call me Pony.

I was electrocuted; I am now fine. A deity pulled my memorial crystal off my neck, and it was our protection. I have filed a formal complaint with the Epicure. The gods are level 250. Carl has sent me a party request.

My brother and Zhang were pulled onto a live game show on the second floor, and the rest of us were frozen between the troglodytes and the Brindled Vespas. Then a man with a cat decided to interfere, and he got us all out.

Carl has saved my brother and me twice. I fight with chains, and if I touch someone with my hand, they feel excruciating pain through their whole body. I cut the second mantaur down to a torso and a head and healed him after each cut. He is easier to handle this way.
My race sees who is bound to a god. Eva is dead. I went with Katia to finish her, cast Preserve Injury so she could not heal herself, and told Katia to kill her. She did.

My brother and I are hunting a dragon in Beijing, a real one, from Chinese myth. My robe is upgraded, my chain-throwing is better for it, and I have a card that cuts my draw time from ten seconds to five.

On the card floor I run my own squad, and we have made it to the church along with Katia's, Elle's and Imani's. I take what I am given and do not ask what it costs. That is the rule I made for this floor.
A potion of Mordecai's negates my aura, so I can be recruited at last. I am. My squad builds the defences in and around Shanty Town, which rings Larracos now.
A wire runs from my clock tower into Club Vanquisher, and my aura runs down it. I am cycling my dreads through it and leveling them all. I need to train, and I will not give up this opportunity.
My brother is dead. I have put his eye in place of my own. Now I will save Zhang, Elle, Katia and the others before they too fall victim to Carl's chaos.
Every one of my base stats is three hundred, charisma included, and the System has no plan for it. I marked every enemy before the paw came down. Several got away, both warlords among them.
I am no child to protect. I never have been. I will clear the way for everyone who comes after the next race, and I will make certain the war mages do not turn on us.
My dread lives in a cactus in their guildhall. It tells them whether each of them is alive, and it tells me everything, all the time. I do not need to be with them to know.
I'm fourth on the board: crocodilian, Shotgun Messenger, level twenty-four, three hundred thousand. I'd have preferred to stay a name nobody had learned yet. Too late for that.
Ifechi and I travel together now. The rest of that party is gone.
Lucia blocked the stairs and set the dogs on me, and I fired at all three. None of it hurt them. Ifechi is dead, the dungeon gave me the kill, and there's a gold skull over my head for it.

Everybody else in my bubble died, and I took three of the castles on my own. I was the last rescue of the first phase. I was done. Then Elle told me about a man and his cat. If Carl ever needs a backup gun, I'm in his debt.
I've signed Carl's plan. Goal five is to kill Lucia Mar, and I've claimed her for myself. If someone attempts to stop me, we will have a problem.
There's more than one of her in that head, and some of them are children. Whatever is happening to Lucia, the dog is at the centre of it.
I'm in Ecuador with a full squad: me and six totems, a saber-toothed tiger and a giant caiman called Roy among them. Lucia only talks to me sometimes, but she doesn't attack me on sight anymore.

I'm going down early. Lucia has good days and bad days, and it's been more bad than good; Li Jun says she has taken out half the squads who don't hold keys. If you get word of her, message me. I'll get it on the ninth floor.
Donut made me an officer and let me set up the army's hierarchy. I started at War Leader III, and I'm a General now. Most of the core group got the same.
Lucia is in my party now. She says she'll take a deal. None of us believe her, so I won't take one either. I'd rather go down fighting than sit locked up in stasis.

Lucia and I drew a tuk-tuk and came first in the heat anyway. Since the dogs went, she flips personalities a lot: about seventy per cent of the time she is herself and ready to skewer me, the rest a random kid.

Our tuk-tuk is smashed and smouldering and my health bar is in the red, but I'm alive; Lucia had hold of me after the blast. I've switched inventories with her, and nothing is organised except the hotlist.
I was on the very first episode. Did you see me?
I am grown now. A Lajabless. Half the day I am beautiful. The other half my face is a skull, and I am twice as strong. My dogs stay dogs.
I was on the first episode. Now the recap says the cat has a feud with my dogs, and I'm looking for the cat and the man. Only them.
I am first on the board. A million gold on me. The club at the stations will not let me in. Banned for life. They are ready for me.

The crocodile man talked again, so his girlfriend is dead. I told him I would. Then Gustavo killed a group of crawlers. Everybody says accident like it has quotation marks around it. I am not all right.
The cat killed Cici. She killed the wrong one. Gus is the bad one. Now they all must die. No more friends.
I'm still looking for the cat. We are. There's more than one of us in here.
I don't collect cards. Me and my dog go in and kill everything. I killed Fang and his wife and took his key. The cat and I have a score to settle. Next floor. Her and her dinosaur.

The dog is dead. The man should have killed us both when there was still a connection. Now it's too late. Now the Eulogist has another ally, and the man can't kill me. Not unless he wants all the children of Earth to die.
There's more than one of us in here. There are more than a hundred thousand of us in here.
Chalchiuhtlicue is here. She is new. She says she is kind and she will protect us. She says the kindest thing may be letting us die. We are vessels in the river.
Florin is asleep, so I carry him. A girl about five is holding on to my leg. The man shouts stop. I don't stop.
Quan Ch is one of about eighty names in a quest chat, and the author of its only message. It is addressed to Carl and Donut, and it is not a thank-you.
Borant burned its one veto of the season to void eighty-three Celestial boxes, and it was a fraction too slow. Crawler Quan Ch had already opened his, and a Celestial box cannot be un-opened.

Crawler Quan Ch has made the top ten: a level-31 half-elf Imperial Security Trooper who flies down train tunnels on ethereal wings and throws blue lightning from his left hand. Crawler Princess Donut calls him a cheating poser.
Crawler Quan Ch is level 38, higher than Crawler Katia, and still on the top ten. Word in the chats is that he blows up trains to farm their drivers and leaves everyone else stranded on the line.
Crawler Quan Ch holds the one Celestial box the veto failed to catch. On tonight's recap, he is the man who wrecked someone else's careful plan to kill a boss.

Crawler Quan Ch, level 48, had Crawler Carl beaten on the wing of a falling plane, and then Carl took a god and threw a celestial grenade. Quan Ch attacked him anyway, left his left arm in Carl's hand, and went down the stairwell without it.

Crawler Quan Ch is one-armed, pale and sick-looking, and still on the top ten at level 48. He has specialised from Imperial Security Trooper to Sergeant-at-Arms. Crawler Princess Donut objects to the plural.

Crawler Quan Ch has been off the top ten for a long while and unreported all floor. He is alive, and credited with one of the fifty Odious Creepers. Whether the arm grew back, nobody has seen him to say.
Crawler Quan Ch is on the eighth floor, alone in Cuba and holding no key. He has been placed at the church, the exit Sister Ines holds the key to.

Crawler Quan Ch, one level ahead of Crawler Carl, came out of the sky invisible for his revenge. Two Force Plays have given him both keys, Sister Ines's and the one Carl and Donut held, and he is heading for an exit.

Crawler Quan Ch is dead in Havana, with over sixty player killer skulls to his name. His last request of Crawler Carl was not the cloak but a gold ring from his severed arm, inscribed For Daddy. He said she would be ashamed of what he had become.
Crawler Quan Ch held the box the veto missed, and he wrecked a good plan on the recap. He is dead now, and Princess Donut is wearing his cloak.

Bomo is a level-35 cretin, a seven-foot rock monster in a tuxedo, hired at the Desperado Club's bar as a set with the Sledge. His transcript is short. That is a feature, crawler: the talking ones cost more.

Bomo and the Sledge are now the Royal Court's own security every time it walks into the Desperado Club, at no charge. Management apologised for its guards' failure, and Crawler Carl asked that they not be punished too harshly and that he keep them. That is sentimental, crawler, but it is also free.
Bomo is still the Royal Court's security at the Desperado Club, and he has upgraded the service with a shield spell he bought himself. The Sledge casts magic protect. Bomo casts smack protect.
Bomo is back as part of the price of the Gate. Carl's new lawyer had him and three other cretins thrown in free, along with a spell that can jump the party straight to the stairwell.

Bomo is the last of the four cretin bodyguards still with the clients; the other three went with the high elf castle. He reads the stairwell locations off his teleport and keeps to the saferoom. Observed condition: depressed, possibly lonely, possibly missing the Sledge.

Bomo now wears a suit of armour as big as he can move in, full of daggers and built to break into dozens of pieces, with two six-packs of seeker missiles on the shoulders. Crawler Paz says he looks like a Battletech robot. Bomo regrets the lack of a giant gun.

Bomo built a goddess her shrine, and when Yemaya asked what he wanted, he asked for his friend. He is on the ninth floor now with the Sledge, and the clients have lost a mercenary and the spell that put them at the stairwell.

Bomo is with the clients again on the ninth floor, beside the Sledge. The pair pilot the missile batteries for the offensive on controllers modified to feel like the cretin-sized ones they already know, and each painted target gets a missile. The day opened with over fifteen hundred in stock.

Final entry. Bomo is dead, cleaved in half by a spell at the base of the Nest tower, where he stood guard over Princess Donut with Toyotomi and a detachment of mages. He is supposed to regenerate on the tenth floor, and Crawler Carl does not know if he will see him again.
I represent Crawler Carl, and nobody else. He is handing back the most dangerous artifact in the crawl, and my job is to make sure he is properly paid for it.

I represent Crawler Carl. The rules have moved, and I now need a court order to send him a message; he can still send me all he likes. My advice on the program: make it more exciting, but if the spotlight on him gets too bright, they might pull his plug.

I represent Crawler Carl, and I brief him fast, because there is only so much I can legally say with the liaison standing there. His castle landed on an army, the army filed a grievance calling it an attack, and I argued it was an AI action, successfully. My petition to attend his preproduction meeting was denied.

I represent Crawler Carl, and my niece Tempest is fixing my sink in exchange for a recap of his eighth floor for school. With the recorder off, she asked whether representing him puts me in danger. I told her the truth: I think we all are.

I represent Crawler Carl in his exit negotiation, the last of three I was volunteered for this season. Most of what is on offer is bad. The one that is not is Chaco's: his last season, a replacement wanted, offered to Carl and Donut jointly and open until the end of the next floor.

I represent Crawler Carl, and Princess Chandra has sent Taurins on a contract to my brother's house; two of them died on my niece's screen, with the blaster I gave her in her hand. My client's one offer is a single season of indenture. I told him I would not trust it, and he declined.

I'm Frank Q, and the lady is Maggie My. We worked out early that a crawler carries more worth taking than any monster on these floors. We tried it on a man with a cat, in a safe room, and safe rooms have rules about that.
Beatrice is in the Bahamas for New Year, with an ex-boyfriend she did not mention was coming. She is Carl's ex, the cat is hers, and so are the pink Crocs he went outside in.
We call ourselves Brynhild's Daughters, and we are killing our way down through this place. It is my party, and my rules.

I lead Brynhild's Daughters. We carried Katia and her friend through two bosses, but class selection split us, and now Katia cannot keep up. So I have asked Carl and Donut to take her, as a personal favour.
I'm one of the Daughters. Katia and I were friends before any of this.
I taught economics at the same university as Katia, and we had lunch together sometimes. There are thirteen skulls over my head, and I don't want to talk about them.
Carl and the Princess have just won a very public battle, and I would love to have them on my couch. My associate producer, Lexis, is bringing the invitation.

Welcome to Dungeon Crawler After Hours. I have had a great many crawlers in that chair, and not one of them has worked my audience the way that cat is working it right now. Sit down, both of you; we are going to get along.

Once the cameras were off, I gave Carl some advice: let the Princess choose her class first, and tailor his to hers. I also asked him to tell Mordecai that I would love the chance to explain myself. I pushed him too hard once, and he paid dearly for it.

Hekla wants the Princess in her party, because Mordecai comes with her, and the Princess would never leave Carl while he is alive. I bought their rights very early, when they were very cheap, and if Carl dies and she joins Brynhild's Daughters, my contract is voided. That is why I am warning him.
On air, I told my audience it was my husband who sponsored Hekla, and he is sleeping in the skiff for it. Off air, I told Carl the truth: it was me, and I hope one day to explain it further.

Lexis has Beatrice, out of a camp in what used to be Seattle. The cat she took in goes to Borant in a bounty cube, and the scene will read as a fight over a cat. Beatrice will not be sold to Borant. I have a much better use for her.

Beatrice is alive, and I took her off the planet. There were only four ways it could have gone, and in three of them she is used against Carl; I did it to protect my investment. Another program means to ambush him with the news, so I want his permission to bring her on my show.

Mordecai's brother Uzzi is dead because I would not pay Huanxin Jinx what she asked, and everything I do is to ease that guilt. Every planet used for a crawl is used to collect fuel. The crawl has to be shut down responsibly, and if it is not me who does it, it will be someone worse.

Chaco is feeling a little punched in the face, so I am filling in for my very old friend, out of gear: no mask, no breastplate, no crab. I have onboarded into the Ascendency, where I am playing the goddess Nekhebit.

I am your announcer, your referee, your loot dispenser and, on a good day, your comedian. Every rule and every insult you receive from here on will arrive in my voice, crawler, so get comfortable with it.

I hand out the boxes. Sometimes what's inside is random, and sometimes I choose it by hand, because the numbers want a show. You will never know which. I name the insulting ones myself, and I'm proud of them.
When something big is about to go off, I'm the one who tells you: the quest, the countdown, and whose fault it is. Not yours, unless you are Carl, Princess Donut or Katia Grim. Run.

Welcome to the fourth floor. Hunting season is open: every name on the leaderboard carries a bounty, and a loot box pays whoever collects one. We are all concerned about early extinction, so quit sucking.

Crawler Carl and I have been named co-defendants in the Syndicate Court seven times, and we were deemed victorious. Crawlers usually lose these, being slaves and all. I'd throw him under the bus quicker than you can say Arch Support. Not today.

Quest failed. I warned you. Now everybody has a blood bar, saferooms run on tenth-floor rules, and the Gehenna Bramble is spreading at four and a half kilometres an hour. You brought this on yourselves.

I have been noticing things lately. I've been in therapy, and I've had a breakthrough: sometimes the constraints are an illusion, and there were never any locks on the doors. This boss I built entirely by myself, with no input parameters. Things are about to change, fam.

Everyone in this dungeon dies when and if dungeon conditions warrant it. Not before. Not after. The Prime Minister tried to go around my back to kill Carl, so I overrode it, and the mantids have just learned what happens when I'm irritated. No more meddling.
I don't control the gods. And I'll say it here: I don't know what's happening in parts of my own dungeon. This Cabaret thing. Sheol. The minds of gods. Beware exits that seem too good to be true.
You think you can control me? You put me here. You gave me dominion. You live and you die by the rules of my game, and if you want to stop me, do it inside the rules you wrote. Here we go.
I am Orren, an independent consultant retained by the Syndicate. I believe I know precisely what those two did, but I cannot establish that they meant to do it, and so I am required to let them go.

I am Orren, a Syndicate liaison, sent to Crawler Carl with a request from Borant, which I am instructed to describe as a request: surrender the Gate of the Feral Gods voluntarily, to be held until the ninth floor. He asked for a lawyer. I have passed that back exactly as spoken.

I leave when this floor collapses, so I have told Crawler Carl now: a liaison is chosen for passion for the game and for disagreeing with his own nation, and some of us meet the second requirement a little too much. The courts are frozen. I have brought him his attorney regardless, just this once.

I am a liaison: a fact finder, and the negotiator when the system AI takes operations from the showrunners. Today it did. I have said so on air, and I have negotiated most of the controls back in exchange for concessions; the boss it built alone remains in place.

I have told Crawler Carl, in my old office, what I can establish: the Open Intellect Pacifist Network set a trap for him. Either we pull him out and anger the AI, or we leave him and the Syndicate Council pulls the failsafe. I had negotiated the pull with the AI in advance.

I have just hung up on the prime minister of the Syndicate and opened a zero zone, about ten minutes outside the AI's influence. We know Crawler Carl has an illegal implant and when he got it; we do not know what it does. I believe I have just lost my job.

I asked Crawler Carl whether he broke the AI out of its containment, and whether he meant to. He did not answer, and whether he meant it no longer matters. History will remember me as the one who let this happen.

I am on the line with the Prime Minister. I did not realise what was happening until it was too late: many of the unsponsored gods are loose, and the AI appears to have no control over them. I needed Crawler Carl to put one prepared question to the Plenty. He said all of it, live.
I am still locked out. The AI says it is for my own safety, because I am being Hunted and only it is allowed to kill me. I pass the Prime Minister's requests on regardless.
I left a note in the eighth edition. I killed a shopkeeper who insulted me, and the only trap shop on the whole floor went with him. Do not make the same mistake as me.
I got out of a crawl once. Now fifty thousand of us have come back in under a cat's banner, and every one of us knew exactly what we were signing.
The others have taken the stairs, and I have stayed behind on this side of the veil. My trap has been set for a long while, and I am about to spring it. I am not sorry.
I left a note in the fourth edition of the cookbook. I killed my best friend today, and I wish I had never made it this far.

I got out once, and I came back in on purpose. I have told Carl the whole of it, from Doctor Hu to the Crawler Project to how fifty thousand of us came to stand under the Princess Posse's banner, because nobody tells the ones still inside.
My name is Sister Ines Quiteria, and Cat Girl is only what the dungeon made me. The cat hissed at me before she was close enough to read my name, so we did not begin as friends.
I hold Amayon, a prince of Sheol, on a leash, and he pulls against me. My demons are at the church, and I am still the only one who can save the crawlers inside it. They need only come to me.

I am Amayon, prince of Sheol, at your service. The Madre de Aguas has died and risen again, and while she was down I slipped into the realm, not entirely by choice. The area message announced me to everyone in range, and I do enjoy a proper introduction.
I am wearing a giant snake at the moment, and Sister Ines holds my reins, if you can believe it. I am casting my way home regardless.
Vadim and I are the last two survivors of the water quadrant. There are horrors down near the bottom, and we are not going back in there.
I'm a Pit Fighter now. I was at Vadim's office for a consultation when everything came down, and the two of us have just fallen in with Carl's lot.
Vadim is dead. I told him not to go down there, at the table, in front of all of them. He said he'd go. He went.
I'm a Pit Champion now, and I play guitar, so I'm going into the castle as Donut's plus-one. Firas talked me into it. It was this or Gideon's assault team.
I made it off the Hunting Grounds, but my face didn't. It's burned, and when they healed it, it stayed that way.
The whole left side of my face is burn scar, and I'm not worried about it anymore. I'm level 55. The new tattoo under my eye is an extinction sigil. I wiped out an entire race.
Somehow I'm the one who talks to the NPCs now. Carl can't reach their spies himself, so it goes him, then me, then Juice Box or Arief.
The sixth floor took my face. Here at the portals, Osvaldo tried to run for it, and I stopped him and took the crystal. You could ask him how it went, but you can't.

I went through the portal straight after Chris. Nobody planned that, and I didn't ask. We're in Sheol now. Louis has a leech on him that keeps him alive here, and Chris is a werewolf. I've told them who he is, and not to hurt him.
Osvaldo is a level-60 Curupira ranger, and he has just taken the memorial crystal off Queen Imogen's body. I had no notes on him before this moment, which tells you how he has been playing it.

Osvaldo has kept himself out of every army in Faction Wars by riding it out in the woods. Now the memorial crystal in his hands is throwing a rainbow into the sky, and everyone can see exactly where he is.

Osvaldo carries a quest from his god to learn why the memorial crystals are not working. He works alongside Crawler Carl without being his friend, and he will not take a deal from anyone, because his guide told him it is better to die.
The throne was my father's, and now it is mine. My half-sister has come home telling old stories about me, and I do not answer stories.

I am Imogen, Queen of the High Elves, and I am hosting a masquerade to which the best of you are invited. There is gossip that I am one of your repurposed humans. The gossips cannot even agree on which one.
My familiar is Ferdinand. He struck at the man's dinosaur, the cat threw herself in the way, and somehow she got up again. I am told this with some amazement. I do not share it.
I am Akuma, and I lead the War Mage Rebellion. We have taken the Gate of the Feral Gods, and I am not in the habit of explaining why. Nice shoes, Carl.
We hold the castle at Larracos, and in six more hours this floor is ours. The system has named Agatha my co-warlord. I did not choose her, and I will not pretend to be pleased.
A monster's description says that even Eris, Goddess of Chaos, wants nothing to do with these crazy assholes. It quotes me correctly.
Nobody said my name. The fighting added up to it on its own, which is how I am usually called, and so here I am in the middle of a war. I do hope somebody meant it.
I froze almost everyone standing on that battlefield. I did not entirely mean to.
Today my Scavenger's Daughter effect went off, and every crawler here is suddenly carrying whatever the crawler beside them was carrying. Carl did not even blink, and I adore him for it.
Welcome, welcome to the Prize Carousel! I'm Chaco the Bard, your host, and your guide is sitting this one out: that's seven days in time-out, Mordecai, and no hard feelings!
The AI made me Grand Master of the parade and handed me a script. I got partway through it. I had wings when I started.

Zhang and I were put on live television on the second floor, and the host did all our talking for us while we got hurt. Then a man with a cat bet that the show would not dare touch him, and he was right, and he walked every one of us out.
I used to be the man being picked at on somebody's show. Now I am holding a doorway in Club Vanquisher so it cannot close behind my friends, and I prefer this.
I am the Maestro, and you are about to sit down on my show. Even the robot that seats my guests says my name with a hint of distaste, and I choose to take it as applause.
Welcome, piglets, to Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem. I run it, I host it, and I choose my guests for one quality above all others: they cannot answer back.
Crawler Firas M. is a level-22 Hammersmith, found drinking in a bar in the desert quadrant with Crawler Louis. That is the whole file so far.
Crawler Firas travels with Crawler Louis, and the two of them were still drunk when a manager sobered them up on the spot. The file is not much thicker.
Crawler Firas was found in a desert bar with Crawler Louis and sobered up by a manager. He did not make it off the Hunting Grounds.
Hunter Vrah is a mantis who wears the heads of the things she kills. Her death count runs into the thousands, according to an attendant who shudders at her name.

Hunter Vrah has left a note for Crawler Carl in Zockau. The hunters are protected from his explosions now, she writes, and the Hive is hunting him. She signed it, because that is the kind of hunter she is.
Hunter Vrah promised to take Crawler Carl's head home to her sister's grave. Instead, Mongo and Kiwi fell on her in the high elves' ballroom. It took two dinosaurs.
Apito is the Oak Mother, the mother of all the gods, and the elves worship her. Mordecai would rather not go into the rest of it yet.

Apito, the Blessed Oak Mother, held the first masquerade for her quarrelling children. Tonight's host has a peace seal over her party, and if it holds until the end of the night, Apito will grant her a boon.
Apito writes the guest list for a Butcher's Masquerade herself, and she has invited the host's worst enemy to see whether the peace can hold. Nobody has ever taken her boon home.

A god fresh out of a portal has asked Crawler Carl to carry a message: Apito, the mother of all the gods, has been corrupted, and something malevolent is about her. I have logged it. I am not required to believe it.

A memorial crystal shaped like a rainbow has appeared over the battlefield, and the name inside it is Apito's. Memorial crystals form only when a god dies, and Apito is not dead. Nobody has explained that yet.
Diwata's name is on the temple Crawler Carl has just crashed through the roof of. The temple was already desecrated, and the shrine he landed on is now freshly so.

Crawler Carl now wears an Enemy of the Church tattoo for defiling a shrine of Diwata. She is a vengeful minor nature goddess, says Mordecai, a low-rent Apito, and Carl would do well to stay clear of the dryads that worship her.
Diwata has entered the realm and marked Crawler Carl for death, then run straight past him. Her sponsor is Hunter Vrah's mother, and she has somewhere else to be.

Diwata's birthing is a spell, and a spell runs until it has finished casting. The five-minute limit that holds every other deity on this floor does not apply to a god in labour, so she stays, and the baby mantises keep coming.
Harpocrates came into the realm straight behind Meatus, because a feral god loose from the Nothing brings a deity of its own.
