Toyotomi is a sergeant in the Princess Posse, leading Li Na's builder squad, and his next job is the tall synergy tower they are calling the Nest.
Toyotomi died defending the Nest's door against a crawler with a dog, cleaved in half by a spell. Bomo will regenerate. Toyotomi will not.

Kandy "Bigs" Newton is a level-29 sluggalette of the Princess Posse who burst out of Carl's slugpox and planted a hatchet between Vinata's eyes. The System credits her with the kill on the Sepsis Whore.
Bigs rides in uninvited on other people's mounts, asking who she gets to chop, and she has to be told not to kill the prisoners.

Bigs has come down to the tenth floor with the Royal Court, where she counts as a mercenary and not a pet, so the enchanted hats are not for her. She has had girl talk with Samantha, got orange goo all over the borrowed carpet, and been invited to the bachelorette party.
The sluggalo code is unity, support, family, and kneecapping bitches. Bigs calls Carl daddy-o, and she holds him to all four.

Bigs is no longer the only sluggalo to come out of Carl's slugpox: Lil' Mello Haze has burst from his back as well, a level above her. At the parade the sluggalos rained from the airship onto the masked crowd in the stands, and Bigs has never been so proud.

Bigs and the sluggalos took the chicken truck's wheel from Tipid and made it the Sluggalo Chick-Chick Express, deep fryer on against orders. About ten of them are still in it when the killing stops, and they have lost Hedy.
Burcu is new to the top ten: a level-59 Porsuk swashbuckler with the head of a badger. She fought Osvaldo and Prepotente after Imogen's death at the close of the last floor.

Burcu is Turkish and very serious, and she was one of the three who fought over the memorial crystal. Tonight her drunk, jealous teammate punched Carl and promised that his Burcu is going to kill him.
Burcu's whole team seems to have been taken in by the Madness, and nobody can reach them. That most likely means conscription.
Architect Houston cut out Burcu's tongue and voice box, and he murdered her mother in front of her. She died in his theatre when the traps fired, looking at Carl with accusation in her eyes.

entries.name: Pater Coal
entries.role: High Cleric Supreme of Emberus · Club Vanquisher

taglines.text: Pater Coal is a level-101 Hobbledehoy, the High Cleric Supreme of Emberus at Club Vanquisher and one of the few mortals in constant contact with the god. He washes Carl's feet in boiling water, because Carl is a martyr of Emberus, and he does not always do his own talking.
Pater Coal arranged a loan from the church for Carl's new ring: 990,000 gold, interest-free for martyrs, with an asterisk. While he owes it, Carl may not renounce his religion.
Pater Coal was the first body Carl watched the AI wear. Now it is wearing Growler Gary.

Raul is a level-70 red Maníseros land crab and a Sun-Kissed Cloud Rank warrior, meditating on top of a crashed box truck on the eve of the Chowder War. After years of cultivation, he is on the verge of a breakthrough.
Raul the crab is a totem card in Princess Donut's deck. He fights well, chants his slow spells and grovels to everybody, and he and Geraldo come to blows on sight.
Raul has been summoned onto a beach full of corpses and told that his people are dead, that he is the last of them, and that he must fertilise the eggs right now, in front of everyone.
Raul has ascended to level 110, and his card is mythic now: ten minutes per summoning, and a much deeper voice. He still calls Carl Daddy.
Jola is a mythic totem card from Iceland, one of Katia's spares, and Princess Donut was delighted to put him in her deck.

Jola the Yule Cat is a fat, dirty-brown Persian the size of a house, with a candle as big as a garbage can burning on his head that reveals anything hidden. He speaks only Icelandic, which nobody present understands.
Jola's Fashion Critic blew every stitch of clothing off Quan Ch, and the cat meant to eat the lot. When Carl took Quan's cloak, Jola hissed at him and crouched to pounce.

People call him Paulie, but his real name is Goff. He is a Residual living in a homeless man's body at a shelter, and he gives the same speech over breakfast every day, in case a crawler is ever standing there to hear it.

In frozen time, Paulie told Carl the rest: when crawlers die, what is inside them is harvested to feed the centre system, and a drink of his coffee installs a menu that can blow the star. Then the Paulie part of him asked Carl to be sure.

entries.name: War Leader Arief
entries.role: Semeru war leader · Larracos Defense Force

taglines.text: War Leader Arief is a young, level-80 Semeru dwarf with a long thin moustache, wearing his great-great-grandfather's hat. He is the first NPC Carl has heard call himself an NPC out loud.

War Leader Arief guides the party down the rings of Larracos, which are numbered from the bottom. He means to take revenge on Architect Houston, who caught his brother sabotaging the Madness fortifications.
War Leader Arief stands guard at Juice Box's door, relays messages to the NPC spies, and runs the dwarven diggers whenever she is away.

entries.name: Dante
entries.role: Former crawler · Trap Master guild instructor

taglines.text: Dante was a crocodilian former crawler, a guild instructor fourteen seasons short of freedom, who wrote a single entry in the cookbook's third edition. He was reassigned to guard an ice castle, refused to follow orders, and is dead.
Dante was ordered twice to kill the ice elves he guarded, and he refused twice. There was no third warning: a beam came from the sky and erased him.
Volteeg's only note in the seventh edition of the cookbook says he misses her so much, and asks whether surviving this place is worth it with her gone. He does not think it is.

Volteeg was a pet songbird who became a gargoyle crawler, and then a Weeper commander for the Operatic Collective. He filled his tank with humming energy balls, put on Mozart, and drove it into his own warlord's caravan.
Rectrix is a sponsor whom Baroness Victory has reminded, along with the Maestro, that making a deity act outside its nature is against the rules.
Rectrix is the Open Intellect's agent and is driving the goddess Theia this season, which is why Samantha found a male skyfowl in her mother's temple.
Nami is a model and influencer who outbid the Priory to drive the goddess Eris. She had surgery to look and sound just like Hekla, and now she wants out.
Someone stripped Eris's soul armour and threw Nami out of the goddess. She landed in the grass outside the ball of flesh, and the fleshers took her.

entries.name: Fopsy
entries.role: Adjutant for the Dream · former Prime Minister

taglines.text: Former Prime Minister Fopsy is the Dream's adjutant: a tripod, a round body covered in black dots on three long, jointed legs. He observes, and keeps his theories to himself.
Fopsy says he had no idea that his own client was a robot, and if the vote goes a certain way, he may be Prime Minister again.
Fopsy was passed over for the vacant office of Prime Minister, because nobody was certain of his relationship to the Dream. Victory has the job instead, for now.
Quemada is a level-96 fire fairy, the protection in team Helix, a three-for-one mercenary squad. She speaks with a thick Spanish accent, and she has just tripled her price.
Since the elf mage spoke, Quemada no longer knows what is real, and her panic heats the cab by the moment. Finley has had to put her to sleep.
Quemada never woke. Finley was carrying her to a temple, so that she would not wake alone, when an APV hit him in the street, and Olga and Quemada died with him.

entries.name: Minus
entries.role: Syndicate security soldier · the tourist who was not Linus

taglines.text: Minus is a soother and a soldier of Syndicate security, sent into the crawl under the name of his dead brother, Linus. He has a primary target, a secondary target, and orders to act the pervert for a while.
Minus, the tourist who was not really Linus, was outed at the crawlers' farewell gathering by the fan club he had been imitating. His first target was Imani, and his second was Louis.
The AI has told the whole dungeon that Linus was replaced by his brother, a soldier sent to kill two crawlers and break what the rest have built. Princess Donut's only question: his name was Minus?

Tempest is Quasar's niece, a young Nullian with a school report due on the crawl, and she has been assigned Carl and Donut. Her uncle makes her pay for his recap by fixing a sink she knows nothing about.
When Taurins came to the house on a contract and hurt her father, Tempest fired the very illegal blaster her uncle had given her, and she was the one left standing.

entries.name: The Gate of the Feral Gods

taglines.text: The Gate of the Feral Gods is said to be buried in the long-lost Necropolis of Anser. A bugbear submarine captain spent close to twenty years looking for it, and an artifact of this grade has no business turning up this early.

Carl's Doomsday Scenario is a soul crystal going off inside a Sheol Glass Reaper Case, big enough to flatten forty-five square kilometres. It can no longer be stabilized, and it will explode the instant it leaves his inventory.

entries.name: Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore

taglines.text: The Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore is a tiara with a clouded purple stone at its centre. Putting it on places the wearer permanently in the line of succession for the Blood Sultanate on the ninth floor, and Donut put it on before Mordecai could finish warning her.
The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook came off a prize carousel looking like a joke book of chicken and goblin recipes, each with a story from its anonymous author.
The Cookbook has been passed from crawl to crawl since the fifteenth season. Carl holds the twenty-fourth edition, and whatever he writes in it goes into the twenty-fifth.

An Enhanced Pet Biscuit has over a hundred possible effects, half of them good and the rest neutral or worse. The cat snatched this one out of Carl's hand, melted into a heap of furry goo, and got up talking.

entries.name: Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering

taglines.text: Frank Q gave Carl this ring as a curse: while one of its marks lives, the wearer cannot be healed. Carl wears it anyway, for the five percent it adds to every stat.
The ring marks a target, and when the target dies, the wearer keeps a point of its best stat. Mordecai says it is addictive, and Donut does not want Carl picking up a new habit.
Eat the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace and you spend an hour unconscious at one percent health, with healing blocked. Survive it, and the goddess decides which of her boons you receive.
According to Mordecai, the Guild of Suffering keeps something called a memorial crystal, which is like a soul crystal, except that nobody has ever established what it does.

A memorial crystal is what a fallen god or demigod leaves behind. This one is the most expensive prize on Chaco's counter, at a hundred hunter hands: the queen usually wears it around her neck, and nobody knows which dead god made it.
The Tiara of a Thousand Lights came out of a celestial box from a waste-management company, on the eve of a war. Donut wears it with Quan Ch's cloak, though nothing has been charged into it yet.
The Scavenger's Daughter is a divine back patch for Carl's jacket: a pile of skulls, stacked nice and neat. What it does depends on which gods, and certain demons, happen to be nearby.
The Scavenger's Daughter is also a person. The war mages came to the castle looking for her, found her, and have left with her.

Nothing! is a double-width space on the Desperado Club's wheel of fortune. At the roulette table, a player who lands on its twin falls through the floor, and a ghostly clawed arm rises out of the dark after him.
The Nothing is where gods are banished, as Samantha's own father banished her. Her first escape split her in two, and every time a Gate portal closes, one of those inside gets through.
The fans voted Carl a xistera: a scoop that looks like wicker, strapped to his forearm and reaching two and a half feet past his hand, which hurls whatever he pulls from his inventory into it.
An emergency box has sent Carl an extension slot for his xistera, made for throwing Samantha's head. With the slot on, the scoop will not retract.
A Skill Potion from a gold box raises one named skill by a single level.

Not every skill potion is worth a single level. On his show, the Maestro gave Frank and Maggie a legendary one that takes Find Crawler to level fifteen, and there is exactly one crawler Maggie wants found.

entries.name: The Filthy Little Crawler's Book of Voodoo

taglines.text: The Filthy Little Crawler's Book of Voodoo came out of a Gold Prepotente Box, and Carl cannot trade it, destroy it or throw it away. It is named after the message boards at old conventions, and the System goes out of its way to say that this is the only reason.
The System has dropped Carl a heavy hint, in the name of a box, that the Voodoo book can be used together with his ability tattoo, and then declined to say how.
A Fan Box holds items voted for by the crawler's followers. Once you receive one, you cannot open it for thirty hours while the fans vote.
A Fan Box is the prize for being watched: the audience votes on what goes inside, and the crawler carries it around for thirty hours, knowing that strangers are arguing about what they deserve.
Only a patron can send a Benefactor Box, and they hold the rarest items. According to Mordecai, even a bronze Benefactor Box is better than a plain gold Adventurer Box.
A Benefactor Box is bought for you by somebody out there who wants you to keep going, and it may hold things from the patron's home world that the dungeon itself would never give you.

The Royal Chariot is a tracked contraption that Carl and Katia built by hand around a magical train-cart engine. Donut named it before it was finished, and the System's description of it is mostly abuse.
A Cleaner Bot is one of the cheapest personal-space upgrades, at twenty-five thousand gold. Katia bought one without a word, because the room was swimming in ghoul blood.
Party Planner is a silver tilt-rotor airship that came out of the celestial box Louis earned by outliving a goddess's mark for death. He gave it the name Firas once suggested for another vehicle.

The Goblin Copper Chopper is a steam-driven goblin motorcycle with a sidecar: a single wheel on a huge spring and a fur-lined orc skull for a seat, which Donut began demanding changes to the moment she sat in it.

Carl's Jug O' Boom is a clay jug of Rev-Up moonshine with a splash of goblin oil and a short torch jammed in like a cork. It throws blue flames up to the ceiling, and the dungeon has named it after him.
The Jug O' Boom is now in the Dungeon Codex under Carl's name, and he earns a gold coin for every kill another crawler makes with it, for the rest of his life.
The moonshine the Jug O' Boom needs is no longer being made, and Carl's royalties stopped after the first few coins.

The Bolt of Ophiotaurus is a single crossbow bolt from Princess Formidable. It is an ordinary bolt unless it goes straight into a god's eye, and then the god's invulnerability pauses for fifteen seconds.
The Bolt of Ophiotaurus opened a goddess to a killing blow. Magical bolts can be used again as long as they don't break, and Katia still has this one.
Princess Donut fired Katia's bolt straight into Emberus's eye, and for fifteen seconds the god had no invulnerability. Taranis used them.
A Celestial Grenade summons its thrower's god for sixty seconds. This one was Maggie My's, bought by the Skull Empire to bring the god of pain down on Carl, and Carl dived for it and has it now.
Carl took Emberus as his god in mid-air and threw Maggie's grenade at Quan Ch. Emberus arrived, and for sixty seconds of Divine Intervention nothing could hurt Carl.

entries.name: Enchanted War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull

taglines.text: The Enchanted War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull is a wrist bracer that becomes a spiked gauntlet of orcish steel when Carl makes a fist. It warns that striking Grull's adherents may transform them into the god himself, and according to Mordecai, those adherents include horses.
Every punch Carl lands on one of Grull's adherents has a 1.5 percent chance of summoning the god. The description never said the chance was cumulative. It is.
A platinum sharpening stone has given Carl's gauntlet longer spikes, a point more strength and dexterity when he makes a fist, and a slightly oilier, meaner look.
Hob-lobbers are round hobgoblin bombs with an eighth of the yield of a hobgoblin stick, in fused and impact-detonated versions. Pustule has only one case of the fused ones tonight.
A fused hob-lobber is the perfect size for Carl's xistera, which sends it out like a cannonball. The fuse runs six or seven seconds, so he pre-lights them to cut it short.
Hob-lobbers are Carl's staple ammunition, fused or impact-detonated, and he cuts them down at the bench to half, quarter and eighth strength for close work.
Carl makes sticky hob-lobbers as well now, but the dungeon has learned to fight back: in one room, heat lamps threaten to set a bomb off while it is still in his hand.

entries.name: Spunky Jefferson
entries.role: Sapient nickel-sock flail · Dong Quixote's weapon

aka.name: Spunky Jefferson the Enchanted Nickel Sock of the Elderly Miser

taglines.text: Spunky Jefferson is a crusty tube sock full of nickels, cursed to hold the life force of an elderly miser. It is sapient, it grows stronger as it kills, and Dong Quixote has taken it as his flail.
Dong's sock grows bigger every day, and it seems to be keeping him alive just by being near him. Imani does not like the look of that.
The sock was torn in a bar fight, shrank back to its original size, and stopped talking to Dong. Then it left him, cursed with Negative ROI, and told him he was a bad investment.

The pink Crocs belong to Bea, Carl's ex-girlfriend, and they are too small for him. He squeezed into them to fetch her cat out of a tree on a freezing night, because his boots were in the dryer in the basement.
Both of the pink Crocs went flying when Carl turned and ran from a goblin murder dozer down the main tunnel.

The Goblin Murder Dozer is a goblin-built, steam-powered machine the size of a tractor, on treads like a tank, with a spinning, spike-covered wheel across its front. It waits in a dark alley, three goblins aboard, for a crawler to walk into an obvious trap.
Carl kills all three of the dozer's goblins and gets behind the guild door before its boiler breaches. Mordecai has never seen anything shake that door so hard.
The Enchanted Nightgaunt Cloak of Stoutness came out of a gold apparel box together with a trollskin shirt, and Mordecai gasped at the sight of the pair.

Carl's nightgaunt cloak is black, leathery and hooded, the wing of some demon creature: four Constitution, resistance to poison and ice, and anti-piercing for all his worn armour. A Nightgaunt that sees him in it will not be happy.

Carl's black, hooded cloak, worth four Constitution and resistance to poison and ice, is made from the flesh of a Nightgaunt, a semi-intelligent species the dungeon dresses up as a demon. The sight of it drove one so mad it never played a single card.

entries.name: Enchanted Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk

aka.name: Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk

taglines.text: A toe ring is what the gold shoe box gives Carl, at a time when what he needs is shoes.

The Enchanted Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk gives Carl three Strength and three levels of Powerful Strike, which multiplies his damage when he fights without a weapon. It sits on the index toe of his right foot, and it is uncomfortable, as promised.
Upgraded once by a scroll, Carl's toe ring now gives ten Strength and five levels of Powerful Strike.
The Enchanted Trollskin Shirt of Pummeling comes out of a gold apparel box beside a nightgaunt cloak, and Mordecai gasps the moment the two appear.

The trollskin shirt gives Carl seven levels of Regeneration and negates melee debuffs such as Stun, Knockback, Disarm and Out-of-Breath. Mordecai calls it one of the best under-armour garments for tanking, the sort of thing found in a Platinum or Legendary box.
A Scroll of Upgrade has added three Dexterity to Carl's trollskin shirt, a decent upgrade if not a great one.
The Goblin Pass comes out of a silver goblin box as a goblin-shaped skull that flies at Carl's left inner forearm and brands itself there, showing through his jacket as well.

The Goblin Pass is a tattoo that removes goblin hostility and grants free passage through goblin territory. The catch is that fairy-class creatures, the goblins' natural enemies, deal twenty percent more damage to whoever carries it.
A Standard Healing Potion comes in a small red glass bottle with a cork and raises the drinker's health by at least half. Put on the hotlist, it is drunk without actually drinking.
A healing potion comes with a timer: drink a second before the first one's fifteen seconds are up, and the drinker is poisoned.
Healing potions hurt the dead: a note in the Cookbook says a smoke curtain soaked in one and left to dry mass-kills undead.
Healing potions come in grades, standard, fine and gold standard among them, and Carl keeps a gold-standard one loaded in his new toe ring, set to trigger on its own at two percent health.
A Pet Biscuit is dry pet food that feeds a pet-based class for a full day. Pets find them delicious and will gobble them on smell, so they come out of an inventory one at a time.
A pet biscuit tossed into a cage turns a beaten danger dingo's dot from red to white. Donut, who still eats them, calls feeding hers to a dingo a betrayal most foul.
Pet biscuits are how Mongo is trained, because he is very food motivated.
The Poker is the second weapon the dungeon hands Carl, out of a Bronze Weapon Box. It is literally a fireplace poker, a wrought-iron stick with a screw-on point at the end.
Tried against a level-four cockroach, the Poker is knocked out of Carl's hand at the first stab, and he shoves the useless thing into his inventory.

entries.name: Scroll of Heal Critter
entries.role: A pet heal, good for one reading

taglines.text: A Scroll of Heal Critter came out of Carl's very first box, a bronze pet box, with ten pet biscuits: a single rolled-up piece of paper.
Read on Donut, a Scroll of Heal Critter does nothing and evaporates with an error message: No Valid Target Available.
A Heal Critter scroll fizzles out where something blocks magic, and Mongo, bleeding, has to heal on his own.
The Toad Cudgel is the first weapon out of Carl's boxes, from a Bronze Weapon Box: a stick shaped like a three-quarter-length baseball bat by someone with only a vague idea of what baseball is.
Carl likes the Toad Cudgel better than the poker, but its rounded end bounces off a giant cockroach without doing much damage, and he has to bend awkwardly to use it.

The Tome of Magic Missile came out of Donut's silver adventurer box with a pile of pet biscuits, and she had taught herself the spell by the time Mordecai noticed. A tome teaches a spell for good; a scroll casts it once.
In the first safe room, a silver Adventurer Box gives Carl a silver ring worth a point of Constitution, which brings the stat up to ten.
A boss box has added a second ring of constitution, worth two points, which Carl wears on his left ring finger. His Constitution score comes up to twelve.

The Talisman of the Slate Butterfly is a little silver butterfly that jingles on Donut's collar. It makes her a better jumper and a little smarter, and winged fairies are no longer automatically hostile to her.

Donut has worn the butterfly charm since the first floor, but to order the guards of Point Mongo around she has to wear a settlement charm on her collar instead; the butterfly can go back on if fairy-class mobs turn up.
Goblin Dynamite is a red stick that sweats, so volatile that a loud noise might set it off without the wick. The System advises keeping it in inventory until it is wanted.
Goblin dynamite wears down as it is handled: every stick in Carl's pile reads out of fifty, and all of them are already at Detonation Imminent or Danger.
Pustule sells goblin dynamite by the case, twenty-five sticks for five hundred gold, beside hobgoblin sticks at twenty for two thousand.

entries.name: Enchanted Spiked Kneepads of the Shade Gnoll Riot Forces

aka.name: Spiked Kneepads of the Shade Gnoll Riot Forces

taglines.text: Carl's kneepads slip on like knee bracers, made of skin and fur, with needle-thin spikes about eight inches long that pop out only when they are needed. They add ten percent Damage Reflect to all his equipped armour and cancel momentum-based attacks.
A Neighborhood Map is the scrap of paper a neighborhood boss drops, persistent loot any crawler can take. Touched, it fills in about a square mile of the minimap, red dots and all.
A neighborhood map fills in the minimap round where it was dropped, and the one Carl looted from a dead goose shows him where a living boss sits as well.
A Potion of Iron Skin raises the drinker's physical armour by a hundred percent for five minutes. Carl has five, from a gold crowd control box.
A Scroll of Confusing Fog fills a room with a mist that only the mobs can see. Carl has three, out of a gold crowd control box.
How long Confusing Fog lasts depends on the reader's intelligence. With Carl's intelligence of three it gave fifteen seconds; Donut reading the same scroll would get a hundred and twenty.

The Tome of Wisp Armor comes out of Carl's boss box, a magic protection spell he cannot cast yet on three mana. Mordecai calls it quite valuable and says to hold onto it, or give it to the princess, who wants it before she knows what it is.
Carl has read the Tome of Wisp Armor rather than sell it. The spell wraps him in tendrils of light that turn aside most magic damage and, for a few minutes, anything trying to take over his mind.

The Torch tome is a spell book out of Donut's Bronze Boss Box, and she applies it before Carl has time to read the description. It teaches her Torch, a curl of light that follows her around and grows stronger with use, and she thinks it is a stupid spell.

entries.name: Desperado Pass
entries.role: The tattoo that opens the Desperado Club

taglines.text: The Desperado Pass is a tattoo out of an Asshole's Box that brands itself on: a gold splotch glowing through the fur over Donut's right shoulder blade, and a dagger dripping blood on Carl's neck. It grants access to the Desperado Club and rules out a Vanquisher pass.
The Desperado Pass also precludes several classes for Carl and Donut, among them the Cleric and Paladin classes.
The Desperado Pass is what gets Carl and Donut past Clarabelle and into the members-only room of the Desperado Club.
Katia has a Desperado Pass now as well, a dagger tattoo that formed on her neck out of a loot box.

entries.name: Enchanted Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet

aka.name: Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet

taglines.text: The Enchanted Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet is Donut's first armour: silver fae-steel scale draped over her back half like a skirt, with a slot for her tail and two points of Dexterity. Not the best protection, its description admits, but it makes her backside look oh so pretty.
Donut's old crupper has made way for a chain mail one, the Crupper of the Benevolent Champion. Its two points of Dexterity were great on the first floor and are laughably weak now.
A Sapper's Table is a workbench sold in safe room stores, and Carl's new Demolitions Workshop menu will not open unless he is standing in front of one.

Carl has a Sapper's Table of his own now, out of a Gold Sapper's Box: a crafting table like his engineering and alchemy tables, where the explosives and traps he makes don't lose stability or go off early.
Carl's Sapper's Table stands in his crafting space, where he expects to spend most of his time, and he spends two upgrade coupons to take it to level three.
At level five, Carl's sapper's table is still better for building explosives from scratch than the bench in his new bomber's studio.
The Tome of Minion Army comes to Donut in a Beguiler Box. Its spell makes hostile enemies fight for her, but it costs fifty spell points, she has twenty-four, and the book will not let her read it.

Donut has read the Tome of Minion Army. The spell takes five minutes to cast and roots her in place while it does, and at level one each intelligent mob in its circle has a two percent chance to turn on its friends.
Donut has cast Minion Army at last, rooted for four minutes, and the demon birds caught low in its circle turned on each other.

Agatha leans on a shopping cart heaped with blankets and odds and ends, a plastic pink flamingo with an arrow in its head among them. Her spray paint lives in it, in a blue IKEA bag, and she insists the paint is hers.

Carl's inventory history still lists everything that was in Agatha's cart while he held it: blankets, clothes, IKEA bags, spray paint, and three pieces of Valtay Corporation technology that sort to the very top by value.

Agatha already had this cart on Earth before the collapse. With the countdown running, she took her supplies out of her dimensional space, put them in the IKEA bag and shoved it to the bottom of the cart. Carl's inventory history still lists the three Valtay devices it carried.
A bracelet out of a silver Adventurer box adds two points to Donut's Dexterity, bringing it to twelve. It wraps snugly round her front leg.
Donut wears bracelets on all four legs now, and the plus-two Dexterity one is on a back leg.

The Enchanted Shuriken of Bloodlust are a hundred small, low-damage black throwing stars. Every monster hurt by one makes the set hit that monster type eight percent harder, compounded, but the stars are very fragile.
A star that takes a single chip loses its red enchantment. Fifty of Carl's shuriken became the spikes on the front of the redoubt for the borough boss, and only about twenty of those stayed unbroken.

entries.name: Heal scroll
entries.role: A heal for whoever it is read on

taglines.text: A Heal scroll heals whoever it is read on, and there is no countdown between one scroll and the next, as there is with potions. Donut won a dozen from a Silver Survivor's Box, and Carl's bronze one brought five more.
A Heal scroll works on Donut, but read on Mongo it does nothing.

The Puddle Jumper tome is a spell book out of Donut's Bronze Boss Box, and she reads it before Carl can ask what it is. It teaches her Puddle Jumper, which teleports her and up to three others anywhere in her line of sight, for 20 mana, on a ten-second delay and a five-hour cooldown.

The Speedbump is Brandon's name for the portable fortress he, his brother and Carl built from goblin tables and gym equipment: angled, four feet high, drilled to go up in less than twenty seconds and come together in twenty more, and meant to wedge a rolling boss against the ceiling.
What survives of the Speedbump travels in pieces in Carl's inventory, and an angled section that is still intact serves him as a shield in a boss fight.

A Borough Field Guide is looted from a dead borough boss, and Donut gets one of her own. It outlines the quadrants of the map round it, and hovering over one gives the levels and types of the mobs inside, though only for a limited area.
The field guide from the bowl's borough boss shows the level and description of every mob in the area, and it covers the entire bowl.

entries.name: Cheat Code Potion
entries.role: A skill boost that will not keep

taglines.text: A Cheat Code Potion raises one recently-used combat or magic skill by three, chosen at random and permanent. It expires shortly after it is generated, so it has to be drunk on the spot.

entries.name: Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph

taglines.text: The Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph is a little zippered folder of twelve tools. Used nightly in a safe room, it gives Carl's bare feet extra damage, three levels of Smush, bones that will not break and a five-second warning before any trap set off by a footfall, all for thirty hours.
The Goo-Inator 3000 is a shaping tool from a silver mechanics box, an oversized silver lollipop with a button on the handle. It only works at a workbench, so for now it waits in Carl's inventory.
At his engineering table, the Goo-Inator lets Carl work metal like dough: flatten it into a sheet, or bend it freehand.

The Second Chance tome arrives by mail: a boss box has made Donut a member of the Dungeon Book of the Floor Club, one spellbook a level. It teaches Second Chance, which raises a lower-level dead monster to fight for the party for as many minutes as the spell's level.

Rev-Up Toilet-Grade Moonshine is a 180-proof accelerant made by Krakaren's operation from grub slime and a secret source, and carried by her clurichaun consultants in clay jugs. Carl and Donut take twenty-five of them, and Carl wants torches.
No more Rev-Up Moonshine is being made this season, and Mordecai tells a shopkeeper that Carl and Donut are the reason. Three of the bottles they kept buy a pharmaceutical starter kit.

The Rev-Up Immunity Smoothie is a recipe left in a dusty box beside a bicycle-powered blender. It takes two ingredients, and Carl reckons it is how a crawler is meant to get immunity from the Taint before fighting the boss.

The Rev-Up Immunity Smoothie is one part moonshine and one part fairy, blended pink on a child-sized bike. It gives ten doses of temporary immunity to health-seeping debuffs and disease, with the Buzzed debuff thrown in.
What is left of the smoothie from the second floor goes into Carl's infusion experiments, and mixed with a smoke curtain it is a dud.

The Enchanted BigBoi Boxers are white, covered in little red hearts and self-sizing, because a were-creature's underwear has to survive the transformation. They give two Constitution and let the wearer cast a level-fifteen Protective Shell once every thirty hours.

An upgrade has made Carl's boxers probably his most valuable item, Mordecai reckons: five more Dexterity, five more Intelligence, three more Constitution, and the Freeballing benefit. It adds a hundred percent damage bonus to every attack from below the waist and allows only a single layer over the crotch, so with the boxers on, no trousers.

entries.name: Enchanted Fur Brush of the Ecclesiastic

taglines.text: The Enchanted Fur Brush of the Ecclesiastic gives Donut two extra points of Constitution for thirty hours, as long as someone brushes her with it for ten minutes every night. It works much as Carl's pedicure kit does.
An upgrade out of a Scab box has the brush adding a further ten percent to Donut's Constitution, on top of its two points for a brushing.

entries.name: Residents' wheelchair train
entries.role: Meadow Lark's ride through the hallways

taglines.text: The residents' train is ten wooden cars on wheels from wheelchairs whose owners are gone, four riders to a car, linked by one glowing magic chain and pulled by Imani and Chris in pig harnesses. It was Imani's idea, and Brandon designed it.
Out in the scorched hallway there is no sign of the wheelchair train's cars, or of the wheelchairs and walkers left behind. Only its chain, which Carl grabbed earlier, has survived.

Yog's Special Chain is a scroll out of a Gold box that makes a magic chain, any length up to something like a thousand feet, light as a feather and gone in thirty hours. Imani's runs about three hundred feet through ten cars of residents.
Imani's chain outlasts the train it pulled, and dropped from a bomb launcher with weights at either end, it snares a rage elemental by the leg.
Imani uses the few chain scrolls she still has, and the chain they make hangs a whole interdiction cart from a crane without breaking.

Dungeon Gold Rush is a scratch-off lottery ticket with six spots. One spot can be scratched each hour, and the symbol revealed decides what happens to Donut's next attack on a mob: five thousand coins, say, or double damage, or a mob that splits in two.

Fireball or Custard is a scratch-off lottery ticket with five spots. Each scratch in battle casts a spell at the nearest red-tagged mob, an even chance of a level-15 fireball or a glob of healing strawberry custard, with thirty minutes between scratches.
Carl's first scratch comes up custard. It heals the bear he is fighting, and the healing kills the worms that have been controlling her.
Carl has scratched two of the ticket's five spots: custard first, then a fireball that half collapsed the room it hit.

The Mother of All Bombs is not a bomb but a launcher Carl built on the chopper's trailer, a ski-jump ramp down which Donut rolls wheeled bombs, its babies, out behind them. Brandon says the name is wrong and calls it the Bomb Chicken, and Donut agrees with him.
The Gorgon Marital Aid is a spatula-shaped workbench tool that hardens and softens rigid materials, and the System says intergalactic porn stars are fond of it.
Carl has built the plungers of his first landmines with the Gorgon Marital Aid.
Mana Toast comes out of a plain metal toaster in a safe room, one burned triangle per crawler. It refills mana, and the System says that is all it does.
Donut keeps two slices of mana toast for an emergency, because they top off her spell points without counting as a potion.

A Proximity Trigger is a trap part, a black box the size of a dime on a long wire, that sets the conditions for a trap to go off. Carl gets ten in a Gold Sapper's Box, and his inventory ranks them near the top for value.

On his show, the Maestro gives Carl a brand-new pair of Bates zip-up tactical boots in his size, identical to the service boots he wore on active duty, with socks in the box. It is a troll: Carl's barefoot buffs and skills stop working in shoes, and the orc knows it.
An Alarm Module is a ready-to-go trap, no tinkering required. Donut's gold sapper's box gives her one, along with a Spike Module.
An Alarm Module blasts a very loud song when something sets it off, or adds an alarm to a trap someone builds. On the train its first song tells the party the babies are through the door.
At his sapper's table Carl now seals alarm traps inside hollow banger spheres so they can be thrown, and because he puts them together there, he picks the songs, from memory.
A Spike Module is one of two ready-to-go trap modules out of Donut's gold sapper's box, no tinkering required. Changing one needs a sapper's table.

A Spike Module is a cube the size of a pair of dice that pushes fifty-centimetre spikes out of a one-metre square every two seconds, forever once something hostile triggers it. Carl has found that it will stand on a door.
The Master Pen Key opens the cages of the fighters and the bait animals in the kobold fighting pits. It is attuned to kobolds, and in anyone else's hand it works once and breaks.
Donut 'coincidentally' receives a spell book of Heal Critter from the boss boxes in the kobold pits, just after she and Carl have won a baby dinosaur.
Heal Critter is on Donut's spell list now, at level one.
Donut's Heal Critter is level fifteen, though like every pet spell it will not work on a special mount.

The Valtay Perso-Shield Platinum Edition is a tech-based personal shield made by the Valtay Corporation. One was in Agatha's shopping cart, and Carl only learns it from his inventory's history, after he has given the cart back.

Carl has a Perso-Shield of his own now, a pinback button like the planet Saturn, unlocked from the hunters' tech loot. Switched on, it wraps him in an inch-thick buffer against physical blows, and somewhat against corporeal spells, for about two minutes, then takes about an hour to charge.
A magical pet carrier is the dungeon's equivalent of a pokeball: supposedly expensive, Odette says, and a way to put a bonded pet into inventory without harming it.
Mongo's carrier cost 15,000 gold: a square brown box the size of a Rubik's Cube with a fire hydrant etched on it. He sleeps and recovers inside it, and comes back out at the press of a button.
A pet carrier is how Ren hands Carl her pet, unconscious and level one now.
Carl carries Ren's pet in a pet carrier in his inventory, and as long as he stays boxed up, Mordecai says, he will be fine.
A Big Top Ticket is one of the things a dead clown was carrying, along with a hunk of Clown Meat and 35 gold. Carl loots all of it with a mass of red dots fifteen seconds away.

A Big Top Ticket admits one adult into Grimaldi's Traveling Circus Big Top Show, with Safe Passage through the public areas only. Signet says that means anywhere in the tent except the three rings, which is exactly where the three poles are.

entries.name: Carl's cactus
entries.role: A gift from the Earth box

taglines.text: Carl's Silver Earth box held a small cactus in a clay pot, three inches tall and covered in yellow spikes, with a $3.99 Home Depot price tag still on it. He cannot think why they chose it for him.

Li Na has cast a dread trap on Carl's cactus and then gone into a cleaner bot that is meant to carry her out of the dungeon. Its glow, its blooms and its dust will say whether she is alive, gone or dead, and a single flower will mean the way is safe.
A single flower has bloomed on Carl's cactus. Li Na reached the Pineapple Cabaret, and it is safe to send the others after her.

An Earth Hobby Potion is a reward the Syndicate Government requires for every crawler with a domestic class: drink it for level three in a random Earth hobby. Donut's is Scutelliphily, which nobody can explain, and Carl's is Cesta Punta, which he wonders might be a martial art.

What an Earth Hobby Potion teaches arrives all at once. Carl's Cesta Punta is jai-alai, the sport of the scoop his fans have just voted him, and Katia's has made her a gear head who has never actually fixed an engine.
Donut's Scutelliphily, Britney explains, is the love of small shields. Her hobby is patches.
Mongo's collar is black and magical, out of Donut's gold pet box, and it puts his orange dot on the map wherever he is. He does not care for it.

entries.name: Enchanted Anklet of the Fallen Oak

taglines.text: The Enchanted Anklet of the Fallen Oak is a simple wooden anklet off a dead crawler, with three little beads that click like seed pods. Its description calls anklets garish, so Carl gives it to Donut for the constitution, and she wears it on a back leg where nobody will see it.
To the city elves, the anklet on Donut's back leg is the forbidden oak, and they take its bearer for the Oak Fell, Apito's version of the antichrist.
Nica's strength rings are two rings, each +2 to strength, that Carl takes off a dead crawler named Nica. They bring his strength back to an acceptable level.

Mordecai mixed a double healing potion that he insisted would cure a parasitic infestation. Carl drinks it in Grimaldi's big top with a mouthful of worms, and throws up a never-ending stream of them, dead and dying.
The double healing potion also works on a brain parasite, Mordecai says, if it is drunk before the parasite reaches the brain.

Carl's Lucky Bastard box, for surviving Signet's attack, holds a single comp chip worth 100,000 gold at the Desperado Club casino. It cannot be sold, traded or cashed in for gold, only played at the High Roller's Roulette Table or the Wheel of Fortune.
Carl played the chip on the Wheel of Fortune, where a comp chip leaves only two bad spots, and it won him a Scroll of Upgrade.

entries.name: Enchanted Fang Caps of the Expectorating Tizheruk

aka.name: Fang Caps of the Expectorating Tizheruk

taglines.text: The Enchanted Fang Caps of the Expectorating Tizheruk are a pair of metal caps like loose vampire teeth, out of Donut's Platinum Quest Box. They add half again to a bite, with a chance to poison or paralyze, and Donut decides at once that Mongo is getting them.
Mongo wears the fang caps now, and every time he snaps his teeth, little tendrils of electricity burst from his mouth.

Hobgoblin dynamite comes in white sticks instead of goblin red, with a larger yield and far more stability. Carl's first whole box of it came with three globs of hobgoblin pus, remote-controlled detonators.
A stick of hobgoblin dynamite is practically a mini nuke: thrown half a block, it knocks Carl off his feet and brings down a building's front. It is utterly impractical in a regular fight.
Hobgoblin dynamite is much more stable than the goblin kind and should survive several impacts, so Carl builds it into his bigger bombs.
Carl cuts hobgoblin sticks down at need, carefully slicing one into twenty pieces.

A Scroll of Upgrade improves one random item a crawler has equipped, a little or a lot, and its short shelf life means it must be read at once. Carl's first makes his BigBoi Boxers probably his most valuable item, with the catch that he can no longer wear trousers.
Scrolls of Upgrade have been good to Carl. One won on the Wheel of Fortune takes his toe ring from +3 Strength to +10.
Not every Scroll of Upgrade is a great one: the third Carl reads only adds three Dexterity to his Trollskin Shirt.

Blitz sticks are what the Desperado Club's pharmacists sell in place of earth tobacco: eat one for five points of Intelligence for a while, or smoke it for a fifteen percent chance at a permanent point, with a side effect or two. Mordecai says they are magically addictive.
Katia smokes blitz sticks she found on one of Eva's victims, and they show her what she asks them to. Only Daniel knows.
A blitz stick is like weed plus a hallucinogen that shows you memories that do not exist, which is why it is so damn addictive. The cure is a patch worn on the skin.

Quint's starter kit is a suitcase that is really a large chest, filled to the brim with chemicals and herbs: everything you need for a pharmaceutical empire, he says. Mordecai got it for three bottles of Rev-Up Moonshine, a potion for Donut thrown in.
The starter kit's supplies sit on the alchemy table in the crafting room now, for Mordecai to work with.

entries.name: Framed photograph of Bea and Brad

taglines.text: Donut's first gold fan box holds a small, framed photograph of Miss Beatrice, lifted from her Instagram: Bea in a bikini, laughing, on her ex-boyfriend Brad's lap. It is the photo that made Carl break up with her, and Donut loves it.
Donut keeps the framed photograph of Bea on a small table beside the bed, which is where she makes Carl put it.

The Gate Pass is a slip of paper from GumGum's inventory, signed by Magistrate Featherfall: the holder is doing this on his orders. It keeps the Over City's swordsmen off a crawler carrying a corpse, inside the township that issued it.

The Mysterious Letter is a folded, blood-soaked paper from GumGum's inventory, written in squiggles and triangles nobody can read. Mordecai recognises necroscript, something an undead magic user would write, and suspects a lich.
The letter is a used Suppurating Eye scroll, and Mordecai thinks the blood on it is the caster's own. Whenever it is out of Carl's inventory, whoever cast it can see and hear what happens around it.
The Scroll of Meat Hooks came off a dead city elf who used the spell to lure Mongo away into an alley. Cast, it draws every nearby carnivorous pet-class monster to the source of a burning stench.

Read from a plane, with Donut's charisma giving it a range of almost three kilometres, the Scroll of Meat Hooks trails a stench behind them like a blown engine, and draws a giant two-headed puppy out of the water after it.
Hundreds of swordsmen guards stand in stasis in a warehouse, their yellow aura all leading to one point in the ceiling, and Carl reckons a soul crystal is up there somewhere.

A soul crystal is elf technology, a charger that runs on the souls of everything killed nearby. The one over the swordsmen's warehouse is overloading, and the map puts it at the epicentre of an explosion with a blast radius of forty-five square kilometres.
The guard depot's soul crystal went off inside a Sheol Glass Reaper Case, and the two together are Carl's Doomsday Scenario now.
Soul crystals power the fourth floor's ghoul generators too, and the generators do not take kindly to being blown up.

The soul crystals elves use are mined from Scolopendra's lair, made when certain kinds of people die and their souls are filtered through the centipede. Once installed as a power source they are worth nothing, except as an explosive.

A Sheol Glass Reaper Case is a small, expensive protective case forged in the fires of Sheol and sold by travelling Spider Reaper Minions. Carl's is one of Miss Quill's, pulled from the debris of her building with Kimaris inside, and every time it opens there is a 1.5 percent chance of Sheol Fire.
The case Carl closed round an overloading soul crystal is half of Carl's Doomsday Scenario now, a caged explosion sitting in his inventory.
A Red Line Engineer's Key is what the magically locked service plate under a red line car's gangway floor asks for, and the System is happy to point out that Carl does not have one.
The keys are colour coded, Carl says, so each one works only on its own line's trains, and it takes one to get into the engine car at the front.
Carl holds two now: the Ochre Line Engineer's Key from a dead engineer, and a large bronze Steam Engineer's Key from the Nightmare's cab, good for all four hundred of the Tangle's steam trains.
An engineer's key is a pass as well. Equipped or held outside inventory, it lets a crawler through the gated portals over the abyss, which lead to a trainyard.

Keys are rescue gear now: crawlers trapped at the abyss need a hat or a key to get through the portals, and at station 75 Carl collects fifteen coloured-line keys from his fellow crawlers along with more than seven hundred hats.

The moment the floor begins, the System hands out one each for an achievement: a blue and white toddler's hat embroidered with I rode the Iron Tangle. Carl examines his. It is not magical. It is junk.
The souvenir hat is a key. Equipped, it carries a crawler through the gated portals over the abyss, and some crawlers have already sold theirs, for five thousand gold apiece.
With the Kravyad's portal closed and the trains stopped, a crawler without a hat may have no way off the line, and more than a hundred and fifty of Bautista's group have none.
Carl is carrying more than seven hundred of them, given up by crawlers who heard what they were for, to hand out to the people trapped at the abyss.
The hats have done their work. The crawlers Carl brought through give theirs to Donut, one by one, in tribute, and she gathers every one into her inventory.
Nobody is buying the hats any more, not even for a single gold, and Carl has not had the heart to tell Donut.

The Bang Bro tome comes out of the bronze boss box Carl earned for killing Miss Quill. Read, it teaches a five-mana spell that adds fire and electrical damage to whatever he has equipped, and Mordecai says it will work on his gauntlet.
Mordecai says the personal space's second tier will offer something called a Bomber's Studio, which would let Carl practise blowing things up.

Carl's Advanced Bomber's Studio is a room ten feet wide and as long as a bowling lane. It holds a virtual range where any explosive he copies can be set off and paused mid-blast, and at the back a bench for taking real bombs apart.
When Carl leaves Donut's party, the bomber's studio stays on her side with most of his crafting tables, so that if he dies she does not lose it all.

entries.name: Enchanted Necklace of the Haute Bourgeoisie

taglines.text: The Enchanted Necklace of the Haute Bourgeoisie is the second smallest of the chains of leadership, and Carl has it for becoming magistrate of a Skyfowl town. Its one gem, a poor sapphire, gives him dexterity, the Talon Strike skill and 432 gold in taxes every ten days.

The Enchanted Tiara of Mana Genita is a crystal tiara like the one Donut lost, with white jewels instead of purple. It adds intelligence, helps her spot mobs on the map, and keeps the worshippers of an obscure goddess from attacking on sight.
Donut wears the Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly now. The Tiara of Mana Genita is kept, in case it is useful one day.

The Hole spellbook is Donut's Book of the Floor Club prize, waiting in a saferoom mailbox, and reading it teaches her Hole: a temporary hole in any surface she chooses. At level one it is not deep enough to get through most doors.

entries.name: Upgrade coupon
entries.role: Slips of paper worth an upgrade

taglines.text: The AI's special box paid out seven slips of paper each: a coupon for a free level-three personal space, two for tier-one environmental upgrades, two for free tier-one crafting tables and two for table upgrades. Each is worth up to 250,000 gold, and two cannot be combined on one item.
Mordecai wanted everyone's table upgrade coupons for his alchemy table, but Carl spent his on the sapper's table and Katia hers on a makeup table.
Coupons keep coming in boxes: Carl now has three third-tier personal space upgrade coupons and a town upgrade for a castle, on top of the lower-tier town upgrade from the Tina quest.

The Battery Fabricator sits in a dusty corner of Limp Richard's general store at 75,000 gold, price not negotiable. Pour in mana potions, add a brick-sized metal block, and a charged battery is supposed to come out the other side.

Carl owns the Battery Fabricator now, traded for the rest of his westerns and a jug of moonshine. Four full mana potions and five minutes charge one dwarven battery, and the powered railway carts at this station can run on them.

The Gangway Chock is Carl's own name for a sheet of metal, a swordsman's breastplate thinned and stretched, that wedges into the gangway between two train cars. With wedge-shaped door blocks on the outer doors, it lets the party keep a cleared car to itself.
One leftover door block from the Iron Tangle has been coated by Mordecai with a holy protection oil, which makes it a repellent against the undead.
An Invisibility Potion does what it says. Carl's first is in the pocket of somebody's suitcase on a train, next to two mana potions.
Invisibility potions keep turning up in Carl's boxes, and he makes sure Donut always has a few. Smashed against someone, one works on them too.

entries.name: 1965 Harley Davidson FLH Panhead Electra Glide

taglines.text: Prize four on Chaco's carousel is a red and beige 1965 Harley Davidson with a small dent in the gas tank, and Carl knows that dent: he made it as a boy, knocking his father's motorcycle over. He does not pick it.

The Harley stands in the yard of Carl's father's trailer, which the dungeon has spliced into the floor from an earlier time, maybe a summer. Carl takes it into his inventory, and it files itself with his vehicles, not the temporary loot, so he thinks it is his to keep.
Carl's father's Harley starts at the first try, its gas tank full, and Carl rides off on it.
Carl rides his father's Harley across the arena at Scolopendra with Donut on his shoulder, and lays it down to make the throw.

The Enchanted Mongoliensis Saddle comes from Donut's fans: a garish blue-and-red seat with a pommel and a great many tassels, no straps and no reins, that clicks onto Mongo's back by itself. It boosts the rider's spells and the dinosaur's constitution, and his melee damage while someone is in it.
Mongo's saddle has an upgrade called Legendary Steed, which lets Donut hitch a cart to him without adding weight, and he can still jump.

A Fragmenting Potion Ball is a hard rubber ball that holds one full potion vial, made at Mordecai's alchemy table to be thrown. A potion works on a mob that is hit with one, and as far as Mordecai can tell, mobs do not get potion sickness.

Mordecai's Special Brew is his own potion: thirty seconds of nonstop healing and rapid regeneration that keeps a crawler's health topped up, though nothing in it saves anyone from an instant death. The price is about ten more hours of potion sickness, and no one can take more than two before they stop working.
Carl has drunk one under Grull's axe, and spent thirty seconds being broken and healed over and over.
The brew works thrown, too. Loaded into a potion ball and fired from Carl's xistera, it heals a giant puppy in one hit.
Thirty seconds of the brew is the window Edgar's surgery on Louis is built around.

The Superb Constitution Buff Potion is a stat potion of Mordecai's making, orange and bubbly, that permanently adds one to four points of Constitution. No one may drink more than two, whatever their quality, so Mordecai says to drink nothing like it they find unless it is labelled Superb.

A Jelly Bomb is Carl's landmine for taking a train off its rails: a tire-shaped, oblong metal tube stuffed with hob-lobbers and a stick of hobgoblin dynamite, set off when a train presses one of its spikes. The System named it, presumably after a jelly donut, and gave him no credit for inventing it.
Two Jelly Bombs on the ochre line are enough. The train comes off the track, and Carl gets an achievement for manufacturing a derailment.

Katia's Makeup Table is a crafting table Mordecai told her about. At level three, paid for with her table upgrade coupons, it lays the face of anyone she has met onto its glass to sculpt from, sitting at it does not hurt, and it stores three designs to call up on demand.
Katia can shape nearly anything on the fly now, but faces still come out best at her Makeup Table.
A bottle of Rev-Up Magic Hair Restoration comes off the corpse of Gore-Gore, along with an engineer's key and a neighborhood map.
Carl's hair has burned off, eyebrows and all, and he means to grow it back with the Rev-up hair tonic, though he has heard the results are a little overenthusiastic.
The tonic adds length for as long as it stays on, and Carl's head went wrong at the last step: his hair now reaches his waist, grows back when cut, and will keep doing so for about two weeks.
Carl had meant to cut his hair once the tonic wore off, but a hairbrush too good to give up means it stays long.

The Armorer's Table is the crafting table Carl buys with a free table coupon at station 281. Metal shaped at the engineering table is only metal, but picked through the Armorer's Workshop tab it becomes armour the system lets someone equip, Katia included.

entries.name: Ugly Ass Backpack With a Completely Useless Design that Only an Idiot Would Wear

taglines.text: Carl built Katia a way to carry her own mass: an open-topped metal basket on dingo-hide straps, which the System calls an Ugly Ass Backpack. Loaded with metal poles and equipped, it vanishes into her, and she grows by what is inside it.
Katia has widened the backpack herself on Carl's engineering table, packed more metal into it, and added rubber to layer between the metal and her flesh.

Katia has a better one now, out of a boss box: the same idea, but adjustable, so she can carry even more, and it will not break. It gives her a stability enhancement while she wears it, and retractable stilts make loading much easier.

Valtay Corporation Neural Enhancer #544 is a blue and yellow capsule from a bronze benefactor box stamped with the Valtay Corporation's symbol, and it permanently installs one upgrade in a crawler's interface: Identify and Analyze Subspace Portals. Carl has swallowed it. A doorway that is a portal now glows purple for him, and he can read it and see a still picture of the other side.
Portal sight is how Carl reads the gated portals over the abyss: who may pass, which keys count, and a picture of the trainyard waiting on the other side.
Carl's implant still reads portals, but in incompatibility mode since the changes to his body, with limited details and no picture.

A Sheol Brick is what a Lesser Demon's young become: of the thousands born in a litter almost none live, and the rest shrivel and harden into black chunks that burn far hotter and longer than coal. The Nightmare Express runs on them, and Carl has taken a box of about fifty out of its cab.
Mordecai wants as many Sheol Bricks as Carl can get, and Fire Brandy has let him take several hundred, most of them still burning.

entries.name: Prism Industries Capacitating and Focusing Goggles

taglines.text: The Prism Industries Capacitating and Focusing Goggles are big round sunglasses, a signed gift to Donut from Princess D'Nadia, that seem to be magically fixed to her face. They see in the dark and by heat, guard her eyes, and turn her Magic Missile into a laser she can split four ways.
An empty benefactor box has upgraded Donut's sunglasses instead: they now read the surface and subsurface temperature of anything she looks at, in precise detail.
Donut's sunglasses are locked to her, as Louis found when he tried them on. A rare scroll called Cracker Jack could free them, and nobody they know has one.

Seize the Day Toothpaste is a tiny travel tube of cherry-flavored toothpaste, five applications, from a Platinum Big Daddy Box. Brushed with in a safe room, it gives thirty hours of three times damage to bosses, four times against province, country and floor bosses. Carl is keeping it for a day he knows he will meet one.
Its bonus is part of what puts Donut's effective charm over three hundred when she goes to work on Ferdinand.

Banger Spheres are Carl's xistera ammunition: baseball-sized balls of dwarven robot scrap he made by the few hundred at his engineering table. The system gives the name only to the ones made at that size.
Banger Spheres are still Carl's everyday ammunition, plain or spiked, and he has made hollow ones too, with an alarm trap sealed inside.

A PVP Coupon is a black ticket with a gold-leaf skull that pays out a stack of boxes and a player level for killing the crawler named on its back. According to Hekla, a crawler in a party who earns a player-killer skull gets them in a Savage box, one for every member, and Katia has found the one with Carl's name on it where Donut hid it under a train track.
Donut says she got rid of both of hers, Carl's under a train track and Katia's in the garbage at a Hotdog on a Stick. The one with Carl's name on it is in Carl's inventory.

A Dirty Little Phased Bolt is ammunition for a crossbow assassin: invisible, hiding its own wound, it drains its victim to a tenth of their health with amnesia and a bleed, and a second takes them to one percent. A death that follows is put down to something else, so the shooter gets no credit and no skull. Two of them were in Katia, and Donut says she saw Hekla shoot them.
Carl keeps a broken one in his inventory. Dipped in blood it shows its shape for a moment, and it is his proof of what Hekla did.

entries.name: Enchanted Repeating Crossbow of the Scavenger Mother of Mothers

aka.name: Repeating Crossbow of the Scavenger Mother of Mothers

taglines.text: The Enchanted Repeating Crossbow of the Scavenger Mother of Mothers was Hekla's, and Katia, who killed her, looted it. It never runs out of basic bolts, only a woman may wield it, and its damage and speed climb with every woman in the party.
Katia's crossbow rides on Donut's back now, clipped to the Scorpion's Bite weapon mount and bigger than the cat herself. Donut admits it is weaker than it could be, with no women in her party.

entries.name: Enchanted Wrestling Belt of the Great Gorgo

aka.name: Wrestling Belt of the Great Gorgo

taglines.text: The Enchanted Wrestling Belt of the Great Gorgo is a gold champion's belt from Katia's Platinum Slam Master box. It adds strength and constitution, and when her whole body is moving, whatever she hits takes the force of twice the mass.

entries.name: Growler Gary's left hands
entries.role: The keys to the rapid-response carts

taglines.text: The rapid-response carts start only with a gnoll's left hand on each of two key consoles, so Carl collects fourteen left hands from Growler Gary, who regenerates every time. Take a hand off, and the cart shuts down.
Carl took one spare pair of Gary's hands, and he is still a pair short.

entries.name: Interdiction Rapid-Response Railway Repair Cart
entries.role: Railway cart with a mobile portal

taglines.text: The Interdiction Rapid-Response Railway Repair Cart is the hobgoblins' wreck-clearing vehicle, with a mobile portal across its front that sends everything on the track to a trainyard or into the abyss. It runs on batteries, and only a pair of gnolls can start it.
One interdiction cart hangs nose-down from a crane over the hole in the station, its portal facing the floor and tuned to the abyss, swallowing whatever comes up.

entries.name: Teleport Trap
entries.role: Two-part trap and a way to travel

taglines.text: In a note by Crawler Milk in the Cookbook's chapter on portals, teleport traps are simply the worst.

A teleport trap can be set inside a saferoom, because the real trap module sits outside, at the destination. Lucia Mar has set at least two, one just inside a saferoom door and one just outside the guildhall's.

A two-part teleport trap needs both halves set by the same trapper, but nothing says the anchor has to stay put. Carl mounts anchors on the backs of little spider automatons and sends them where he wants to go.

entries.name: The Left Fang of the Green Sultan

taglines.text: The Left Fang of the Green Sultan is one of Eva's two sabers, dropped in a train's engine car and picked out of the gore by Carl. It is half of a set and only magical with its brother, so on its own it gives nothing, and Eva has lost her main weapon.
Carl has given the saber to Katia as she prepares to go her own way, and told her to return it to its rightful owner.
Katia has returned the saber to Eva. She cut off Eva's escape-ring hand with it, then drove it through her breastplate.

entries.name: Enchanted Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit

aka.name: Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit

taglines.text: The Enchanted Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit is a wrist bracer that pops a small metal shield into place with a twist. Katia gives it to Carl once her new riot shield will not let her wear both, and a hit on it has a small chance to disarm the attacker.
Carl has swapped the Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit for a better shield bracer, and it has gone onto the pile of gear for the Faction Wars team.

entries.name: Enchanted Shade Gnoll Riot Forces Crowd Control Shield

taglines.text: Katia's fan box gave her a riot shield of the Shade Gnoll Riot Forces: tall, curved and absurdly light, with Get Back on the front. It adds constitution and Rooted in Place, and it upgrades her Rush to Crowd Blast, which hits a whole cone in front of her and can be used every five minutes instead of once a day.

entries.name: Enchanted Shade Gnoll Riot Forces Telescoping Crowd Control Baton

taglines.text: The baseball bat in Katia's fan box is a police baton, faintly glowing with enchantment, that telescopes from twenty-five centimetres to three metres and casts a Cone of Knockback when swung at a group of ten or more.

The Stuffed Grulke Infantry Figure is a beanbag toad in a spiked helmet, the commonest of its line, one of more than a thousand stuffed monsters from Miss Quill's apartment. Pull the tag and throw it, and a real grulke fights for fifteen to thirty seconds.

Astral Paw is the spellbook Donut pulls from the mailbox as her spellbook-of-the-floor club prize, and she reads it before anyone can talk her out of it. Mordecai calls it a good utility spell: a paw that handles things at a distance as if she were touching them, with more force than Astral Hand and claws to come at level five.
Donut picks Astral Paw as one of the two spells her War Crime combines, and over the hole of Larracos it becomes a glowing paw big enough to pin an army under it.
A gift from the gods has pushed Donut's Claw skill to 17, and Mordecai tells her that her Astral Paw spell can now cut through almost anything. She stiffens at the name.

The Enchanted Gnome FarSeerer is a dirigible gnome bomb sight, a white telescope covered in pipes and gears, that lets its user inspect things at a distance. Skarn keeps one to watch the patrols, and every gnome it targets is told they are being watched.
Donut has stolen the FarSeerer off Skarn's roof in ten seconds flat, and she says she forgot the thirty gold she was told to leave for it.

entries.name: Enchanted Toe Ring of the Leprous Bandit

aka.name: Toe Ring of the Leprous Bandit

taglines.text: The Toe Ring of the Leprous Bandit, on Carl's left foot, carries two benefits. Sticky Feet lets him walk on walls and ceilings barefoot once every six hours, and Super Spreader passes his active debuffs to a target once an hour.
The Gnomish Knock-Knock is a refrigerator-sized fuel-air bomb, barely stable, slung under the gnomes' patrol ships. Only a few are left, and they are kept now as a standoff weapon.

The last few Knock-Knocks hang under the Wasteland itself on the morning it comes to bomb Hump Town. Carl's second volley of missiles goes at its gun battery and three bombs on its underside, and the sky to the north goes up in white fire.
Carl counts the Knock-Knocks under the Wasteland as one quadrant's "cheat", a quick way to kill everything, like the drain hidden in the side of the sandcastle.

Pawna's Tears is the potion in Carl's Legendary Deity's Box, named for Pawna, the goddess of peace and Grull's sister and arch enemy. It adds five to any spell or skill its drinker chooses and can be saved, and Mordecai calls it the single best item of loot Carl has had.
Carl has spent Pawna's Tears on Donut, to bring her Laundry Day to fifteen against Circe Took. His sponsor says he will replace it.

entries.name: Scroll of Water Breathing
entries.role: Breathing underwater, a scroll at a time

taglines.text: A Scroll of Water Breathing lets a crawler breathe underwater for three seconds per point of intelligence. They turn up in box after box on this floor, which Mordecai reads as a hint about what the floor holds, and Donut announces that cats do not swim.
Water-breathing scrolls have to be chained one after another, and when one runs out, the water in a crawler's lungs comes back up.
A Water Breathing scroll grows gills, and in surgery Mordecai uses one to give Louis gills that stay.
A Surefire is a crafting part the size of a bottle cap that gives any projectile the Guided status: an arrow, a bolt or a rocket seeks the target it is given. Carl has a case of twenty-five.
Surefires are what turn Carl's rockets into guided missiles. He had used ten when Ruckus's boss box sent a case of twenty-five more.
A launcher of twenty-five surefire missiles brings down a fleeing hunter, and Carl has used the last of the parts.
Out of the seeking-missile attachments for some time, Carl gets a group of surefires from a gold box and can build more missiles.

The Wall of Fire tome, from Donut's platinum box, teaches a fifteen-mana escape spell: a wall of flame ten metres wide and two high, for fifteen seconds at first level. Mordecai warns that fire spreads. Donut wanted Fireball.
Donut's Wall of Fire crackles bigger than ever, thanks to her new nipple ring.
Wall of Fire is one of the spells Donut's new cloak is raising to level 15 over the coming week, and Mordecai expects her to be a terror on the battlefield.
Powered up to level 16, Donut's Wall of Fire runs a mile along the road and a hundred feet into the air.

The Gnomish Drop Bear is one of the dirigible gnomes' earliest fast-attack planes, an open-air, twin-engine biplane with famously underpowered engines and a quick-escape balloon. It does not drop bombs; its payload is something the System calls much more entertaining.
Carl now has a Drop Bear of his own, an abandoned biplane named Death Trap, which he sprays over and renames Nightmare II.

Rapid Detox clears its drinker of alcohol and most drugs, and for a single floor makes them violently ill if they drink. Mordecai gives it to Louis and Firas disguised, so neither can read what it is.

aka.name: Veriluxx RealPet Dungeon Crawl Special Edition Exclusive

taglines.text: Veriluxx RealPet Companions is Donut's new sponsor, and its first benefactor box is a product sample she is to play with on camera before she, Carl and Mongo go on a program about it.
The product is a toy robot Donut, three-quarters her size, with fur like rat hair, bootleg Garfield lines and a creepy streak. Donut is thrilled to have merch. Mongo bites its head off.
The newest robot Donut is three times heavier and survives Mongo, but a cheap tab holds shut a panel at the back of its head, and opening it starts a five-second self-destruct warning.
Loita is dead, blown up by the last robot Donut, and Carl had made sure its panel would fall off.

entries.name: Mairmei Mushroom
entries.role: An alchemy material, and a drug

taglines.text: Mairmei Mushroom is an alchemy material, and all its description says is that these little guys are quite the trip. Carl took a batch from the town hall in Hump Town, and Mordecai has never seen the strain before.
The camels have been feeding a mushroom to their gnome prisoner to keep him compliant, and eaten raw, Mordecai says, the mushrooms help get people to do what you want, if not reliably.

The Toraline Root Vegetable is a rare tuber that grows only in dirt once covered by lava, and by the System's account it tastes like dogshit. It came in a silver benefactor box from the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network, and nobody, Mordecai included, knows what it is for.

Mordecai, with Samantha's help, has worked out the toraline's uses: a special ink for scrolls, or lava-themed potions at about an eighth of the yam each. One of them, a phase potion, has got Maggie out of Chris's head.
More than half of the toraline is gone, and the sponsors who sent it have sent a note: Save the toraline.
A sliver of the toraline, brewed in a beaker by Shi Maria with Carl's own hands, has become the black ink of a tattoo on his chest. Mordecai still has the biggest piece.
Toraline ink mixed with Carl's blood makes a permanent tattoo that lends a spell to someone else, and the yam potion renews it. There is barely any of the vegetable left.
With some ink tips from Milk, Rosetta says, they no longer need the toraline to do what they need.
The Valtay Corporation's Neural Enhancer #275 is the second pill the brain-parasite corporation has sent Carl. Swallowed, it adds his current elevation and airspeed to his interface, permanently.
Ruckus, the giant cyborg buzz-ard, carries a twenty-five-foot stick of ten spinning buzzsaws, each blade the size of a truck tire, hung under her on a pair of thick cables.
Ruckus is dead and her buzzsaw is in Katia's inventory. It runs on the same dwarfish battery as the Chariot, seems to work without the bird, and is lighter than it looks.
The buzzsaw is gone, broken apart on the ocean floor after it cut through Lusca's head.
Carl wants a parachute in a hurry, and Feather Fall is a potion for it, but Mordecai has none of the materials: the seed pods it needs, he says, are scarce until the sixth floor.
Carl buys a case of twenty-four Feather Fall potions at the Masquerade's prize counter, because Eva's thievery has left the group seven fall-protection potions short.
Carl hands out Feather Fall potions once the escape plan is live, and when the last five seconds come he drinks one himself rather than trust his nipple ring.

entries.name: Enchanted Roll of Never-ending Duct Tape

taglines.text: Carl asked the viewers for duct tape, and a silver fan box has sent him the universe's greatest: fifty metres of extra-durable fabric tape that grows back at a metre an hour until the roll is full again.
The duct tape has bound a gnome prisoner, sealed a bomb into a submarine's minifridge and patched a flying house's net of ropes, and Louis has just used up the whole roll.

entries.name: Jellyfish Salve
entries.role: For a Pain Amplifier Jelly's sting

taglines.text: Jellyfish Salve comes in what Donut calls a lotion bottle, five applications, and takes the pain out of a Pain Amplifier Jelly's sting, though not the minute of blocked healing. It came out of Carl's silver boss box for killing Ruckus.
Carl has given Katia some of the Jellyfish Salve, and he tells her to keep it in her hotlist outside the Akula.

The Vahana is a Gnomish Legate Balloon, perhaps the oldest vehicle left aboard the Wasteland, black and gold striped from the days when such balloons meant ambassadors and perhaps peace. It brings the gnomes' negotiator down to the sand.
Carl hijacks the Vahana with Donut and Katia and fires his missiles at the Wasteland from its basket. All three jump as the airship's gun battery smashes into it.
Dolores Doesn't Splat is a potion for anyone falling faster than two hundred kilometers an hour. It speeds the fall, softens the ground at impact, and slams the drinker into it five times in a row.
Dolores Doesn't Splat is no pleasure, but Mordecai calls it genius: Carl's health was still at a hundred percent when he landed.

The Coffee Shop Author Kit is a magical sheet of paper with a quill and a jar of ink. Whatever Carl writes in a new tab of his scratchpad appears on the paper, and whatever is written on the paper appears in the scratchpad.
Clipped to the wall of the bathroom stall in the personal space, the Coffee Shop Author Kit is how Carl and Katia trade messages nobody else can see.
Half Splat is a potion against falling: with it the ground cannot kill you, but you land at five percent of your health. Carl, Donut and Katia each have three, from the same Silver Skydiver's box.
At the Butcher's Masquerade Carl has half-splat potions to spare, and he leaves a bathroom counter covered with them, and a note, for the crawlers who come in after him.

A Live Ammo Ball is a dirigible gnome grenade: a fist-sized clamshell sphere holding a living creature in stasis, which bursts out when the ball hits. The five on a dead sniper's bandolier each hold a level-11 frenzied gerbil, and the many more that fell with the Wasteland loose thousands of gerbils on Hump Town.

A big, broken live ammo ball is the casing of the largest bomb Carl has built on purpose: filled with explosives and Nitro Sludge, welded shut, and named by the System Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home.

entries.name: Mongo's speed and strength fang caps

taglines.text: Mongo's second pair of fang caps came out of Donut's platinum quest box, like the first, and adds fifteen percent to the dinosaur's movement speed and fifteen percent to his strength.

The Platinum Sharpening Stone is a little black rock from the quest box for saving Hump Town, made for any spiked weapon and too short-lived to keep. Carl rubs it along his gauntlet's spikes at once, and they grow a little longer.

Princess Formidable's emergency box gives Katia a set of ten crossbow bolts of Petrify Rock Class. Each one leaves its target Petrified, conscious but unable to move, for sixty seconds, and Mordecai says they cost more than regular bolts.

The Nightmare II is a gnomish Drop Bear biplane the other crawlers found intact, renamed by Carl over its stencilled Death Trap. It runs on gasoline, has a rear-facing gun, and carries an emergency balloon that lifts it to the top of the bubble.
The Nightmare II came down slowly on its emergency balloon after the boss fight, and it lives in the flying house's garage.
Carl has flown the Nightmare II once, against Quan Ch over Orthrus, and it went spiralling into the nose of Emberus and exploded.

Bonnie's necklace looks like a walnut and holds a little purple soul crystal, the power for the balloon that keeps her house afloat. How far its clamshell is open decides how much power the balloon gets, and Carl keeps it open just a fraction.
