Katia says that if Carl had not left the controller with Louis, they never could have flown the house to the land quadrant. Louis and Firas have turned into quite the pilots.

A Hobgoblin Disco Ball is a hobgoblin smoke curtain soaked in an invisibility potion. Its rainbow smoke hides everything inside it, bounces to the beat and blinds whoever threw it as well, and Carl's first one goes off on his crafting-room floor.

Orren credits the dust a disco ball leaves behind with Administrator Loita's death, and calls it one of the most brilliant assassinations he has seen a crawler execute. Carl had only wanted the toy too filthy to take into the studio.
Carl throws disco balls in fights now: from the wing of a biplane at Quan Ch, and by hand at Queen Imogen, whose goop-covered face, by Donut's account, never saw Prepotente coming.
The Belt of Buoyancy is a simple belt that wraps around Donut's stomach and keeps her from sinking, though it only works in the water. She spends a good three minutes complaining about it.

A Potion of Bloodlust doubles its drinker's strength and speed for as many seconds as their constitution, and leaves them not knowing where they are or why they are fighting. Carl has two, and Mordecai tells him not to use them.
Carl does not drink his Potions of Bloodlust. One, taped to a hob-lobber and set off on the flooding bridge of a submarine, spreads through the water and drives Lusca's babies into a feeding frenzy.
Carl's last Potion of Bloodlust goes into a potion ball. Beamed at a flying mantis warrior, it enrages her, and she pulls the head off her own sister.

Drakea's Enchanted Kerchief of Disorder looks like an ordinary black bandana with a white paisley pattern. It gives Carl +5 to Detect Traps, a level-15 Tripper spell once every five hours, and the Remote Detonator benefit.

Carl's black paisley bandana still gives him a level-15 Tripper. Neither Imani nor Elle can wear it, so Imani carries its Tripper spell as a tattoo from Katia, and Carl feels a jolt in his chest when she casts it.

The earth patch is a tiny round patch, the size of a half-dollar, depicting the planet Earth. Sewn onto an eligible garment it gives +5% Strength and immunity from cloud-based attacks, and Donut dismisses it as a screen print.
The earth patch was the first patch on Carl's jacket, sewn on by Katia, and a patch of flaming arrows now sits beside it on his shoulder.

The Enchanted Anarchist's Battle Rattle is a black, sleeveless canvas jacket that gives +1 to all Carl's base stats, a point more for every patch sewn onto it, double that with a back patch. It also adds half again to the range and accuracy of every explosive he throws.
Carl's Battle Rattle now carries three patches, the planet earth, a fistful of flaming arrows and a hand-stitched bomb, and each one adds a point to all his stats.
Carl's Battle Rattle carries five patches now, and on its back the Scavenger's Daughter, a divine back patch that doubles the stat boost they give him.
A Potion of Dinosaur Repellent promises that a pack of dinosaurs will eat its drinker last, for a full thirty hours. Mordecai's "uh-oh" when Carl draws one does not help.
Carl has received ten of these potions and drunk one, though the description is vague about what it actually does. Donut refuses hers, afraid it will make Mongo shy away from her.
Carl leaves a counter covered in these potions for the crawlers on their way into the ballroom, so that loose dinosaurs will go for the hunters and not for them.

A Ring of Water Breathing is a glowing blue ring that lets its wearer breathe underwater as well as on land, for a point of charisma. Carl, Katia and Tran each get one, and Mordecai warns that it grows gills and makes the skin slimy.
Carl slips the ring on to go into the water after Samantha, and the gills form on his neck at once. Donut is appalled that it costs him only one point of charisma.

Each of Carl's seven silver Summary Judgement boxes holds a gold piece, a photograph and a Stock Certificate for one share in a company from the home system of one of the plaintiffs who sued him. They are worth about ten credits each, and Mordecai says crawlers should not be getting anything with credit value at all.

King Rust tells Carl that the stock certificate he owns is losing significant value by the moment, now that his daughter has told the whole galaxy the Skull Empire builds backdoors into everything it makes.

The Twister is the flying house: a beige suburban house from Texas, cut down to its ground floor, hanging in a net under a huge glowing balloon. Louis and Firas fly it on the air currents and named it; Louis wanted Tiddy Twister II, after his van.
The Twister has gone through the portal to the sixth floor with the changeling refugees. Louis and Firas cannot pass that way, and mean to recover it once they have taken the stairs.
Louis and Firas have the Twister back, with a ballista Bonnie built on the side of its yard. The ceiling on this floor is too low for the balloon to clear the trees.
The Twister is gone. With the mantises aboard, the Sledge, who still has its controller, crashes it into the last two guard turrets still firing.

The Enchanted Handcuffs are novelty cuffs in red, fuzzy velvet, magically reinforced so that only a strength of 200 can break them. There is no key: Carl locks and unlocks them himself, and can set a safe word.

entries.name: Ping tome
entries.role: Carl's spell book from a quest box

taglines.text: The platinum quest box for saving a puppy held a magical tome, a black leather hardback warm to the touch with a skull on the cover. Opened, it taught Carl Ping.

Rockard's Ring of Sniping is an amber-stoned ring that marks on the map every creature under half health and every one wearing magical gear, which makes stealing kills simple. Carl pulls it off the arm he tore from Quan Ch and puts it on.
The Tome of Twinkle Toes, from Donut's platinum quest box, teaches a cheap spell that makes Mongo, or any other minion, run really fast for as many seconds as her intelligence.
Twinkle Toes lets Mongo outrun the dune buggy, and Donut practices it to level it up. Mongo screeches with joy whenever she casts it.
Hedy the gremlin says pet spells do not work on special mounts, so Twinkle Toes will be no help to a biological vehicle on this floor.

The Enchanted Xistera Extension Slot is a head-throwing attachment made for Carl by the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network and sent in an emergency platinum benefactor box. On the end of his xistera it throws Samantha five hundred metres for every point of his strength, and taking it off brings her back.
The extension recalls Samantha the moment it comes off Carl's hand, so he does not wear it all day, and she roams free instead.
Dropping the extension brings Samantha back, and what she holds can come with her: once it brought Sister Ines, the sea snake she rode and thousands of seals, crabs and fish, living and undead.
The Phase Lava Rock potion is one of Mordecai's brews from the toraline yam. For one minute its drinker can move through lava and lava rock, and a creature made of lava rock cannot touch him.

A gold Hunter-Killer Box is the reward for The Hand that Claws the Master, an achievement for permanently killing a non-crawler biological. The achievement may be awarded more than once, but the boxes come only on the sixth floor, and Carl's first batch is thirty-four.
Each Hunter-Killer Box holds gold and the severed hand of a hunter; Carl's thirty-four open one after another, every one with a thousand gold more than the last.
A Hunting Trophy is a hunter's severed hand, and one comes in every Hunter Killer box Carl earns for a kill. The hand is a prize ticket for a counter that opens at the Butcher's Masquerade.
At Chaco's prize counter, hunters' hands are the currency. One buys a 25-pack of potions, thirty buy a future floor boon, and Carl arrives with sixty-six.

entries.name: Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home

taglines.text: Carl's biggest bomb yet: a broken live ammo ball about five feet tall, filled with explosive and Mordecai's Nitro Sludge, welded shut, imbued with Fear and set in a cart for Bomo to pull. The simulator says it flattens everything within a third of a mile.
Kicked out of a saferoom door at Vrah's mantises, the wheeled bomb kills the last three of her mantis warriors, explosion protection and all. Vrah gets away.

entries.name: Enchanted Collar Charm of the Effete Bourgeoisie

aka.name: Collar Charm of the Effete Bourgeoisie

taglines.text: With the ursine town she renames Point Mongo comes a collar charm Donut must wear to order its guards: one tiny turquoise gem for the town, plus eight dexterity, plus four intelligence, the Snitch skill and 3,592 gold every ten days. She hates it, because it replaces her butterfly charm.
A second, red gem hangs on Donut's leadership charm now, for a small settlement: a little intelligence and dexterity, a spear skill she can never use, and only 403 gold every ten days.
A pack of twenty trap add-ons called Fail Safes, the prize in a Trapmaster box Carl earns when one of his roadside traps kills a hunter. Each one tells him if its trap is ever disabled or set off.

Carl takes nine potions of Levitation off a dead hunter. They raise the drinker into the air for twice their intelligence in seconds, though nobody says how high one can go or what happens if it runs out on the way down.

A Levitation potion moves its drinker up and down on a slider and nothing more. Mordecai calls them dangerous: they will not stop a fall that already has momentum, so treat it like standing on thin ice.
Carl drinks his last Levitation potion at a railing in Larracos and goes straight up out of Larracos.

Carl's fan box holds a postcard-sized plastic badge on a red lanyard, SPECIAL GUEST flashing round its edge. His fans have put him on the CrawlCon roster for three events, attending virtually, and Zev advises him to cooperate.
Worn round his neck at the production facility, the badge lets Carl see the names over people's heads while his menus are switched off.

Major Charlie is a potion Mordecai brews for Carl, usually called Brain Juice, though not even Mordecai can explain the name. It adds ten points of intelligence for thirty seconds, then takes ten away for five minutes.

entries.name: Enchanted Obsidian Bracelet of the Raggle Rouser

aka.name: Obsidian Bracelet of the Raggle Rouser

taglines.text: The black bracelet Carl took off the moon elf Akland is the Enchanted Obsidian Bracelet of the Raggle Rouser: ten constitution, five dexterity, fifteen percent fire resistance and a level-10 Fireball once every twenty minutes. Donut wears it on a front leg.
Donut has cast her bracelet's Fireball indoors now, into Lucia Mar in a wooden pub, and set its back wall alight.

A light-duty trebuchet the size of a windsurfing board, built from glowing, poisonous bamboo by the Dream's raiders and left spiked to the ground in a clearing. It hurls three hundred kilos and infuses whatever it throws with Poison Cloud. Carl takes it.

A little cup on the sling changes the poison: pour a potion in and the rock carries that instead. Loaded with Mordecai's weedkiller, Carl's rock chucker kills an Odious Creeper, and Donut, as spotter, gets the credit.
A card Donut finds on a dead Skull Empire hunter when she loots everything at once. It has no description and looks like a credit card, and she wants to spend it before they cancel it.
Credit chits are, as far as Carl can tell, the intergalactic equivalent of credit cards. He takes a second one off a dead dreadnought hunter.
With the right card machine, King Rust's eyeball, his family ring and a password, King Rust's money moves onto a credit chit and out of everyone's reach.
Summoning traps cover the slope below Fort Freedom alongside the alarms, and bush elves are quietly disarming a path through them to the water.

A recycled summoning trap calls two guards or minions to wherever it is set off, and it misfires if you have no minions or control no town. Carl collects ten; if they ever use one, Donut will have to set it.
Slippery Slope is a trap on the south shore of the river, across from Fort Freedom, that would have made Carl slip and fall into the water. He disarms it and keeps it.

The Automaton Table is a level-five crafting table left alone in an empty studio at the production facility after Carl's CrawlCon panel, with Dr. Ratchet's Guide to Building Automatons for Fun and Profit lying on it. Carl takes both.
The Automaton Table builds from the recipes in Dr. Ratchet's manual, and its first build is the Spider Stalker.
Carl has given Katia access to the Automaton Table, and she is building something for Tran on it, with vehicles to follow.

entries.name: Dr. Ratchet's Guide to Building Automatons for Fun and Profit

taglines.text: An autographed paperback left lying on an Automaton Table in an empty studio after Carl's CrawlCon panel. Carl takes the guide and the table into his inventory.
The guide is an instruction manual full of automaton recipes, and Carl has copied every one into his scratchpad and into the Cookbook in case it is taken back.
Katia builds from the manual too: she has repurposed one of its recipes into Tran's two-part wheelchair.

A Gold Spicy Box gives Carl a white patch with a little bomb hand-stitched on it in Spider Reaper Minion silk. It adds constitution, damage for every explosive and two levels of explosives handling, and a discount from the traveling Spider Reaper Minion merchants.
Carl's white bomb patch, in Spider Reaper Minion silk, adds constitution, explosive damage and explosives handling. An identical bomb is embroidered over the crotch of the Royal Court's capture flag.

A small square patch from a gold ranged-weapon box: a dozen flaming arrows in an eagle's claw, drawn Sailor Jerry style. Katia sews it onto Carl's jacket beside the planet earth, for five percent more dexterity and five percent more damage from every ranged projectile.

A recipe Mordecai has been chasing for fifty cycles, sent by the Apothecary with a drawing of Mongo. The potion must be brewed for a specific animal, and its special ingredient is a liter of that animal's blood, per potion.
Brewed from Mongo's blood, the potion is named Charm Mongoliensis now: it makes the closest eligible monster Donut's minion for the rest of the floor, and the one they want is the pack leader Kiwi.
A second charm potion, brewed with cat blood and drunk by Donut on stage at the masquerade, makes Sir Ferdinand her minion.

entries.name: Enchanted Silver Bracelet of the Ab-solar

taglines.text: A silver bracelet set with little purple gems shaped like bulbs of garlic, from Donut's gold Apothecary box. Under a rant about vampire novels, it protects her against vampirism and lycanthropy and adds a quarter to her magic damage against sapient undead.

A gold box from the Plenty holds a patch for Carl's jacket: a gray goat head on black, denim-like cloth, the symbol of the Midnight Epicure, a children's bogeyman grown into a ward against all night evils. It protects against vampirism and lycanthropy and adds a quarter more magical damage against sapient undead.
The goat on Carl's patch is the Midnight Epicure, the god Prepotente worships: a tale made to scare non-caprid children that grew into a symbol of hope and comfort for his kind.

Mordecai's holy water grenades: potion balls of a fine healing potion and an air-activated coagulant, dipped in the blood water of Carl's Emberus shrine. Against vampires, he says, they act like napalm.
Miriam Dom left over forty scrolls of something called Size Up in the pile of everything she owned, and Carl takes two where Prepotente cannot see.
Prepotente knows Carl took Size Up scrolls from his mother's pile, and he asks for five fine healing potions as payment.
Donut drinks a Size Up potion before the race and reads off Osvaldo's dexterity with all his buffs, his abilities and the levels of his skills.

A legendary benefactor box gives Prepotente a vintage-style spray applicator and a recipe for a herbicide. The mix of fine healing, blessed water and weedkiller only works when his new magical canister turns it into a very fine mist.

entries.name: Uncle Morty's Insta Lawn-Kill and Undead Repellant, Extra-Strength Edition

taglines.text: Uncle Morty's is Mordecai's weedkiller for the Odious Creepers, an existing weedkiller for an odious bloom with anti-undead boosts added: four moonshine jugs of it, each enough for two or three creepers. It is very flammable, and if it burns before the monster absorbs it, it does not work.
Poured into the little cup on the elven rock chucker's sling, Uncle Morty's goes out with a three-hundred-pound rock and brings a creeper down in seconds.

The smallest of the four nipple rings Carl pulled out of the hunter Iota, about the size of a nickel, worth plus ten and another five percent to constitution. Donut wears it in the top right, for a price.

Pawna's Cries adds three to any spell or skill and has a limited shelf life, so it must be taken before the end of the floor. It comes with a note telling Carl to give it to Donut in secret, and he hands it over as her price for wearing a nipple ring.
Donut drank Pawna's Cries before the Masquerade and took her Laundry Day spell from nine to twelve.
The third of the four nipple rings Carl pulled from the hunter Iota imbues its wearer with Quarter Fall, a falling speed a quarter of normal. Carl puts it through his own left nipple.
When the Sledge counts down the last five seconds, Carl does not trust his nipple ring's fall ability and drinks a Feather Fall potion as well.

entries.name: Satchel Bomb
entries.role: A bag that levels a town

taglines.text: Satchel bombs are little bags with leather handles that Carl can toss and set off with the power of three sticks of hobgoblin dynamite, enough to level a small town. An Odious Creeper's boss box gives him a bunch.
Carl has been making his own satchel bombs in his bomber's studio, safe for regular crawlers to handle, and now they go on the market.

entries.name: I Take it All Back Potion

taglines.text: A black, bubbling potion that removes any effect of Scolopendra's Transmutation spell, given to Prepotente in a benefactor box and handed on to Donut with a tag: use it when the time is right, and do not give it to Tina.
Burst over Kiwi in the middle of the castle battle, the potion turns the raptor pack leader back into an ursine, and Tina knows her mother.
Bautista has a line of about a hundred stuffed slate butterflies from his sponsor's sample box. They are harmless: summoned, one flies to the nearest light and sucks the energy out of it.
Britney's jacket is made of stuffed slate butterflies, and one pull on a tag sends one up to drain the warning light in the Masquerade's ballroom.
The lightning found the cloud of butterflies from Britney's jacket and blew it apart over everyone's heads.
Cracker Jack is a rare scroll that frees gear locked to its original owner, the usual guard on benefactor box items. Nobody Carl knows has one.
Carl has three Cracker Jack scrolls from his trade with Orren, enough to free three of the locked items taken off hunters.
Spider Stalkers are rat-sized robot spiders built from one of the recipes Carl took from Dr. Ratchet's manual. Each can be programmed with a target and armed to explode.
Carl carries fifteen spider automatons. Ten are armed with regular explosives, and the rest he can arm with a holy grenade or a healing potion against the undead.
The spider automatons carry the anchor halves of Carl's teleport traps on their flat tops, so he can teleport to wherever one of them is.
A new tiara for Donut, one of five gifts from the Apothecary laid out on a table before the Butcher's Masquerade. Unlike the hammer and the stick, its purpose is clear.
Once on Donut's head, the tiara doubles her charisma for thirty hours and then dissolves: her base of 138 becomes a god-like 276, before the saferoom buffs.
The tiara doubled Donut's charisma through the masquerade, and it is lost in the battle that ends it.

A ball peen hammer small enough to fit in Carl's hand, sent by the Apothecary through Imani with a note that it is for Donut. Its description says it is magical and does nothing magical, and a seven is pressed into its wooden handle.
In Prepotente's hand, the hammer gives the Stick of Cascadia's Screams one very tiny tap in the glass wall of the seventh floor's starting chamber, and the whole level shatters.

A ten-inch metal rod that looks like aluminium, sent by the Apothecary through Dmitri Popov for Donut. It is not a wand, its description says, but used correctly it can do something truly magical, and a seven is pressed into one end.

Pushed halfway into the glass wall of the seventh floor's starting chamber and tapped with the hammer, the stick cracks the wall, and the whole level shatters while Cascadia screams over the announcement system.

Of everyone the Apothecary sponsors, only Katia got a benefactor box not meant for Donut. It held a small knit beanie that raises all her stats by three percent and gives her a spell, I Need My Personal Space, which knocks everyone around her back with a powerful blow, her own party included.
In the fight in the pit where the castle stood, Katia takes the beanie off her own head and puts it on Carl's, so that he can clear a way through the nymphs and get Donut close to the god.

entries.name: Wand Recharge scroll
entries.role: A scroll that brings a wand back

taglines.text: A recharge wand scroll is one of five Apothecary gifts that arrive in sponsorship boxes given to other crawlers, each with a note saying it is meant for Donut. Carl understands what this one is for.
On the Masquerade stage, Donut casts the recharge scroll on the dead wand in Big Tina's hand, and the wand glows back to life.
Carl gets another wand recharge scroll from Orren, in a trade that also brings him three Cracker Jack scrolls.
Carl keeps his rare Wand Recharge scroll in his inventory, in case the shrink wand ever runs out of charges.

A sheet of bard music in Chaco's prize case at the Butcher's Masquerade, priced at ten hunter hands. Chaco offers it when Mordecai asks for something like his own escape spell, though it is not quite as good, and Carl buys it for Donut.
Skedaddle is Donut's second way out of a fight after Puddle Jumper. With both, the party can jump twice, as long as she sings it in key.

aka.name: Book of Lore – Commonwealth of the Bahamas

taglines.text: One of two Future Floor Boons in Chaco's prize case, thirty hunter hands apiece and one to a customer: a book of lore for the eighth floor, whose random starting location and full title reveal themselves on purchase. Carl buys it.

Its full title is Book of Lore – Commonwealth of the Bahamas: a thin hardback under the Bahamas flag, full of the monsters there and their stats. Carl tells only Prepotente the title, and Donut picks somewhere else.
Donut chose Cuba, but the Bahamas book still earns its place on the eighth floor. Its index runs from Common to Unique, and Shi Maria is in it, among the uniques.
A shrink wand with ten charges, like the one Zhang used to have, is in the Masquerade's prize case, and Carl buys it with his hunter hands.
The shrink wand cannot be used on living flesh, so Carl uses it on a steel collar locked round a neck.
Carl's shrink wand has seven charges left after Zhang borrows it to bring down a church.

entries.name: All Eyes on Me sheet music
entries.role: Donut's song for the talent show

taglines.text: Among the Apothecary's gifts for Donut was sheet music. On the Masquerade stage she sings All Eyes on Me, the song her mother used to sing to her, without taking her sheet music out, and the whole room falls under its charm.
All Eyes on Me normally takes a song, but Donut's charisma is now so high that she can cast it with spoken words.

entries.name: Princess Lunette
entries.role: Signet's mother, as a body in Carl's inventory

taglines.text: Princess Lunette is an incomplete flesh golem: Signet's mother, or the memory of her given flesh, with the memory itself gone. Signet wants Carl to take the body, help Samantha and find a pulpmancer.
The body was a tattoo of a fish before Signet's final spell. Carl carries it in his inventory, waiting for a caster who can put Samantha into it.
Princess Lunette's heart and lungs are in Louis now. The body that was supposed to house Samantha went to save him instead.

The Dart of Ophiotaurus is a priceless artifact Odette's crawlers spent half of the tenth floor hunting. Worship a god and use it on someone else, never yourself, and the god is summoned through them; the god's immunity does not start until five units after it forms.

Every squad leader on the eighth floor gets twenty flags bearing a logo the system designed. Plant one in a living thing below five percent health and it becomes a T'Ghee totem; a lost flag is not replaced.
A flag only works in the hand. It has to be touching whoever shoves it in, so a flag tied to a crossbow bolt is simply lost.
A flag does not check what it goes into. It has turned a dying city boss into a card, and a dying crawler too.

entries.name: Enchanted Nipple Ring of the Superior Fire Demon's Hand Maiden

aka.name: Nipple Ring of the Superior Fire Demon's Hand Maiden

taglines.text: The Enchanted Nipple Ring of the Superior Fire Demon's Hand Maiden is a glowing red ring from Princess Donut's Beguiler's box. It makes her impervious to natural fire and lava, strengthens her fire spells, and lets her cast a berserking spell called Bitch, What? once every thirty hours.

entries.name: Tome of Legionnaires of the Damned

taglines.text: The Tome of Legionnaires of the Damned is a summoning spellbook from Princess Donut's De-Sleeving box, chained shut and wriggling. Its spell fills recently unequipped armour and weapons with wailing spirits that fight for the caster, and Donut learned it the moment she had it; the tome screamed as it went.
Legionnaires of the Damned is the second half of Donut's Phantasm move: Laundry Day blasts the armour off Bomo, and the spell fills every scrap of it with a screaming ghost.

entries.name: Enchanted Nipple Ring of the Defiler

taglines.text: The Nipple Ring of the Defiler is a silver ring with an eyeball hanging from it, wearable only by a crawler a god has marked for death, which Carl is. It reads the religion of everyone nearby, lets him break shrines without divine fallout, adds a quarter to his damage against clerics and casts Black Nimbus once an hour.
Black Nimbus strips a worshipper of their god's blessing for a while. It takes away the god's protection, not the god's wrath.
The Prison Tattoo Kit is the same stick-and-poke gear Edgar the tortoise used on Tsarina Signet. Tattoos can carry all sorts of magical buffs and upgrades, and everything depends on the artist.
Katia has used the kit to tap a Desperado Club pass onto Samantha's neck, and the ink is already starting to fade.
Shi Maria has used the kit through Carl's own hands: its stick took Li Jun's eye, then tattooed an eye into Carl's chest.
With the right ink, the kit can put a skill into a crawler's skin. Katia is using it to tattoo a skill from Li Na's blood onto Carl's right arm.

entries.name: Enchanted Right Back Atcha Personal Shield

taglines.text: The Right Back Atcha Personal Shield is a short black forearm bracer covered in little buckles that throws out an overeager small buckler. It catches physical attacks on Carl's dexterity and magic bolts on his intelligence, and sends three in four of them back at the attacker, sometimes doubled.

The peace symbol patch is a small upgrade patch from Carl's gold pacifist's box. It makes neutral mobs less likely to aggro and adds ten per cent to his Dexterity and to his skill at the bongos, and it is sewn to the bottom of his jacket, beside the bomb symbol.

The Combo card is a very rare, consumable T'Ghee utility card. It fuses two monster cards into one creature for the shorter of their two summoning times, and afterwards both are out for the rest of the combat.
Donut has spent the Combo card, fusing two problem totems into one, and the Glow-Up card has made the result permanent.
The red beret came off the head of the Experience, a mob with an angry bearded face like Che Guevara's. It glows because it is magical, and Donut gasped when she read its stats.
The red beret gives Donut only a small boost to all her stats, but she wears it now and then because it is appropriate for the location.
The Flee card is an uncommon, one-use T'Ghee special card that teleports a whole squad out of combat, without saying how far or where to.
In the final phase a Flee card has a price: a keyholder who flees loses a key to the opponent. It is also the only way to hand a key to someone else.
Stout is a common T'Ghee utility card that adds 25% to a mob's health for the length of a combat. It is not a one-time consumable, and Carl and Donut collect one after a fight with the duendes.
Carl and Donut hold two Stout cards now. Carl takes the second from a pile of spare cards Katia's team brings over.
Time Extend is a common T'Ghee utility card that doubles how long a summoned totem lasts. It is not consumable, and Carl and Donut have two.
Time Extend can be made permanent: a totem buffed with one and then hit with a Glow-Up card keeps the doubled summoning time in future battles.

A Spirit Box is a set trap that roots whoever steps on it for sixty seconds, lowers their spirit resistance and summons a random non-corporeal entity to possess them. A haunted town in the fog is littered with them.
Greased Lightning is a T'Ghee utility card that increases a mob's speed by 25%. Carl takes one from the spare cards Katia's team brings over, and thinks it would make Geraldo ridiculously fast.
Greased Lightning is a speed card Donut plays on her totems fight after fight, and her active deck now holds two of them.

Hobbled is a very rare, consumable snare card, the first snare card Carl and Donut own, out of Donut's gold T'Ghee box. Played on an enemy totem, it cuts the monster's summoning time by ninety per cent, and the cut stays with it for the rest of the combat.

The Bard's Golden Throat is a golden, amethyst-encrusted headset microphone, voted to Princess Donut by her Princess Posse. It keeps her songs within a step and a half of the note, helps her form bard songs and spells, amplifies her voice two to five times, and adds five per cent to her Charisma.
The Thief is a mythic mystic card, black-bordered, that steals a card from an opponent. It is not consumable. The goddess Yemaya gave it to Princess Donut, and it gives her all five kinds of card.
Force Discard is a rare T'Ghee mystic card. It picks a random card from the opponent's hand and tosses it onto the discard pile.
Hole in the Bag is a snare card that drains a totem's mana. Unlike Hobbled, it is not consumable, so it can be played fight after fight.

entries.name: Enchanted Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly

taglines.text: The Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly is a simple silver-coloured tiara from the gnome jeweller at the Desperado, set with Donut's citrine for 25,000 gold. It halves her potion cooldown, adds ten intelligence, cancels the dexterity debuff when she is drunk, and gives her a level-10 Hover five times a day.
Donut has set the dragonfly tiara on a charging pillow, which drains an item of all its magic and stores it for a like item.

Liquid Therapy is a protection potion Mordecai brews against Shi Maria's Unending Insanity and Lights Out, which nothing short of divine intervention can cure. One dose a day lasts until the drinker sleeps, and it covers a host of other fear-based debuffs besides.
Damnation is an uncommon T'Ghee snare card. It does not kill an enemy totem; it makes sure the totem goes to the discard pile when its time runs out, dead or not.
Glow-Up is a mythic, one-use T'Ghee special card that fixes a card as it stands at that moment, buffs and all, so a totem stretched by a Time Extend keeps the longer summoning in every fight after.
Ren has handed Carl a second Glow-Up along with all of her cards but her totems.

Glory Bound is the worst of the drugs Katia has been taking and by far the most addictive: it puts her in a coma to relive a memory. She has taken it once. The cure, Mordecai says, is a bad trip of the same drug.

Mordecai's modified Glory Bound is a fizzing green gel: two hits of the drug compounded with a subdermal gel and a potion called Tough Love. Under it Katia must relive her worst memory, and Carl, with Removal Order added to his dose, is meant to enter the spider's.
The treatment has worked, for Katia as far as Carl can tell, and for him sort of: Shi Maria is trapped, though the eye on his chest remains.
The sailor hat belonged to Robert the Human, a hunched old man in a white sailor's outfit much too small for him, until Mongo took his throat. It is the first thing Donut collects.
Donut's white sailor hat cuts two seconds off her card-draw countdown, at the price of her Hover skill and ten points of intelligence, so it goes on when the deck comes out.

A Scroll of Build Trench lays down a permanent trench two point three metres deep and two wide, as long as its user's intelligence plus strength allows. Scrolls can be combined to add sleeping quarters and other front-line accessories.
Build Trench scrolls keep turning up in crawlers' inventories. Carl has about fifty, and Louis likens them to the bandages and torches of the first floor.
Thousands of Build Trench scrolls carried down from the eighth floor have become a labyrinth of trenches on the front, with bunkers, hospitals and fall-back positions.
A Build Trench line laid across an enemy trench can be enjoined to it. It is a long-standing exploit: the scroll is craft magic and ignores most protections.
Lamp is a consumable snare card that paralyses a totem for ten seconds and makes it glow brightly. Carl and Donut take ten of them from the deck of one deckmaster, a Nightgaunt.

The Sentient Necro Staff, the Worm Fulcrum, is what the ogre deckmaster Sharp Elbows summons from a mystic Necro card combined with a Walking Stick totem: a living tree of a staff that raises the dead turkeys around her as zombies. It is both a totem and a mystic card, Donut protests.

The staff card is Princess Donut's now. It is not consumable and takes no totem slot; before a fight she imbues it with one of her own spells, to cast once, and the staff looks different depending on the spell it holds.
The Golden Combo is a unique T'Ghee card that works like the Combo, fusing two totems for a time, but it is not consumable, so it can be played over and over.
When a Golden Combo's intended target dies mid-play, it proceeds to the next available minion target, and that is how Carl has been combined with Shi Maria.
Carl's father's Glock is a 9mm pistol, the only gun his father had, and Carl takes it, along with two boxes of ammo, from his father's bedroom in the floor's recording of the trailer.
The Glock came from outside the dungeon, so Carl cannot fire it as it is: once he handles them the rounds are overpowered, and the gun would probably explode.
Carl keeps his father's Glock in his inventory and has no intention of wearing it or using it, even after a fan box sends him ammunition and a shoulder holster with his name on it.
A folder filled with court documents is one of the things Carl takes from his father's bedroom in the floor's recording of the trailer. He takes it without looking at it.

Carl has left his father's papers on the table in Donut's room, unread. Donut has read them: money Carl's grandparents set aside for him that his father tried to get at, a marriage certificate, and court documents from several arrests.

The Champion Pack goes only to a squad that has defeated the keymaster. Its leather bag, in the squad's own boxer pattern, holds a backup slot for two more totems, a champion trophy, a cooler of yellow Gatorade and two Flee cards.
The Champion Pack's backup slot is where Donut keeps the card of Paz, which Katia let her take after the goddess died.

The Book Burner patch is an embroidered upgrade patch of a burning book, out of a Gold Talk of the Town box. Fixed to a garment, it adds fifteen percent to Intelligence and the Book Burner benefit: once a day, an opponent forgets a spell for thirty hours.

The Wand of Nighty-Night is a gnarled wooden wand with ten charges. Each casts a level-10 Sleep on a single non-boss target for five minutes, broken by physical damage, and more casts compound the effect.

entries.name: The Bull Rush, Bespoke Personal Shield

taglines.text: The Bull Rush is a bespoke tech shield from Hereford War Machines, a Taurine-owned company that outfits elite mercenary squads, taken off a hunter. Unlocked with a Cracker Jack scroll and pinned to Donut's collar, it wraps her in a bubble that moves with her and can stretch, more weakly, over a mount or a whole vehicle.

entries.name: Enchanted Pauper's Ring of the Steadfast Emberus

aka.name: Pauper's Ring of the Steadfast Emberus

taglines.text: The Pauper's Ring of the Steadfast Emberus is Carl's old strength ring, his first in the dungeon, re-forged by the Temple of Emberus against a loan of 990,000 gold. It holds back most disease and health-seeping debuffs for a worshipper of Emberus, and to everyone else it still looks like a strength ring.
Too many debuffs at once overload the ring, and then the slugpox it holds back breaks through.
Carl has taken the ring off and left the faith of Emberus, standing in front of the god himself.

The Knife of Frozen Tears is a small knife of Sylvan crystal that looks like a butter knife and glints with red light. It is not very sharp and not worth much, but it can kill Garret, because Sylvan crystal is one of his weaknesses, and Ren uses it on him herself.
The Midnight Express is a consumable special card with two large men in tights on its face. Tserendolgor never got to use it, and she gives it to Carl with the rest of her cards.
Played, the Midnight Express makes a teammate the deckmaster for three minutes, which leaves the squad leader free to cast spells and use inventory. Princess Donut has spent it.

Velma is Tserendolgor's enchanted flamethrower, part breastplate and part weapon. She did not name it. Sitting on the floor of a building about to collapse, she unsnaps it and gives it to Carl with the rest of her gear.
Rosetta's team in the crafting room has refitted Velma to Jamal's harness. The flamethrower hangs under the hammerhead's belly now, and little tendrils of flame keep leaking from it.

The Tier 3 Doggie Door is a personal space upgrade that lets a crawler leave their space by any door they have already used on the floor, a fast-travel network shared with guests and party members. Lucia Mar dropped five of them, and Mordecai thinks she stole them when she went on a show.
A Doggie Door is installed in Carl and Donut's room and in Katia's, and the plan is to fast travel by it between the city and the guild's headquarters.
A doggie door works for anyone who has one, and off-world sponsors can buy the upgrade too: an enemy who ever came in through the bait shop can come back the same way.

Annie – Útburður is one of Katia's T'Ghee totem cards: a level 80 raven the size of a cat whose head is the skull of a human infant, the little holes in it filled with teeth. Katia plays a Timeless card on it so it stays summoned.
Annie is the card Katia brought down from the floor before, and the skull-headed crow rides on her shoulder even inside her dream. It shares its name with Annie, the baby girl in that memory.
Katia left the card on a table when she went, and Donut took it.

entries.name: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride

taglines.text: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride is an eye tattooed into Carl's chest by Shi Maria herself, while she had control of his body, so that he could not leave her behind as a card. It blinks once and closes, and its description gives nothing but its name.

Shi Maria is trapped inside Carl now, and the eye on his chest is his to control. He can see through it and keeps it shut on purpose. He can summon her once, and then she may choose to take his body or go back to her own form.
When Vinata, fighting Carl with his shirt open, stares into the eye on his chest, it drives her mad. Shi Maria is still trapped behind it.
The eye has followed Carl into a dog's body, to the middle of his forehead, where he opens it on reflex and freezes a mimic in place. Shi Maria asks to take over, and he says no.
Carl is back in his own body, and he has made sure the Eye of the Bedlam Bride is back in its proper place.
Shi Maria, in control of Carl, burns a sliver of toraline in a beaker and gets a little bubbling black ink, which she pokes into his chest with the stick from a tattoo kit.
Carl has a few thimblefuls of the spider's ink left and a finger-sized slice of toraline, and Rosetta wants both.
Ink mixed with a willing donor's blood lets another crawler borrow their spell or skill as a tattoo; the donor loses levels for a while, not the skill.
Imani borrows Carl's Tripper through a small toraline tattoo, but there is barely any of the vegetable left to make more.
Edgar, with tips from Milk, has learned to make a similar ink that does not need the toraline.
A ghillie suit comes with Donut's new class, a long-range sniper and assassin called Deathbed Hellcat, along with a hat. Donut has no idea what a ghillie suit is. Carl does, and keeps it a surprise.
It is a cat-sized camouflage suit of shredded, colour-changing fabric that covers her whole body, adding Blend into the Background and a Cone of Silence, and Donut is absolutely not wearing it.
Donut wears it after all, invisible at the top of the Nest tower while she shoots magic missiles from it.

The beige, extra-floppy boonie hat that came with Donut's sniper class adds a Targeting skill for examining mobs from afar and stretches the range of all her spells. Worn with the ghillie suit, every benefit is buffed further.
It is the first hat on the tiara's red charge pillow, where it will give up all its magic over ten hours.
Its Targeting skill is in Donut's tiara now.

Revitalize Pet was a Heal Pet potion, Donut says, until Carl set it on the ground before Paz blew Ysalte's head off; now it is purple, full of glitter, and super rare. Mordecai says it will grow Mongo's missing wing back in about an hour.
Mordecai knows the recipe now, though the ingredients are really rare. Carl has smashed the vial on Mongo's backside, and the Healing buff has appeared over his head.
Mongo's wing is starting to grow back.

The Cloak of the Benevolent Champion was Quan Ch's, and it is the first celestial item of this crawl. On Donut it is a shawl. Over the coming days and weeks it raises her lowest stat to match her highest and lifts four spells and a skill to fifteen, as long as she keeps it on.
It is one piece of a matched set of four now. The Crupper of the Benevolent Champion repeats its powers and adds to them.

A platinum box from the Apothecary gives Donut a second charging pillow for her tiara, purple where the first is red. It drains any magical item, not only hats, but a buff passes only to a like item, so a ring's goes into a crystal set in a ring.

MySpace Photo, once called Charisma Cheat, is a two-minute potion of Mordecai's that makes the system think Donut's Charisma is thirty points higher, so that the cloak she puts on lifts her Constitution to match.

entries.name: Enchanted Toe Ring of the Well-Balanced

taglines.text: A Legendary Spicy Box gives Carl a plain silver toe ring for his left pinky toe, and the System insists on the toe. It holds one potion to fire automatically, guards his mind against Enslavement and Conscription, and grants Extra Steady Balance and Walk on Air, a skill the description marks as already obtained.

Its Mind Balance has been blocking hundreds of attempts to cast through Carl that he never made, and it is climbing fast; trained this high, he would keep the skill, less five levels, without the ring.
The treatment meant Imani had to pry it off him while he slept, and that is the moment a teleport invitation was accepted in his name.
Its Mind Balance is level sixteen now, trained past fifteen on the battlefield.

entries.name: Hell-Kissed Celestial Skill Potion of the Prince of Woe

taglines.text: A Celestial skill potion in a bottle shaped like a horned skull, which gives one random combat skill of level 10 to 15 taken from a Sheol mob of level 200 or more. Carl drinks it and comes away with the level-13 Gloom Wraith Phase.

entries.name: Reaper Spider Minion merchant patch
entries.role: Carl's key to the Midnight Market

taglines.text: A small black-and-silver upgrade patch of a Reaper Spider Minion merchant, from a Platinum box. Affixed to a garment, it opens the Midnight Market, warns of traveling merchants nearby and adds five percent to Dexterity; Mordecai calls the market a place Carl needs to stay out of.

Jamal is a seventeen-foot hammerhead shark who breathes air and can only flop, so Carl has built him a voice-controlled harness of eight double-jointed automaton legs. It holds his weight fine, but its joints cannot take the landing when he tells it to hop, which he keeps doing.
Jamal has new legs, and he has broken them again; Justice Light says he can fix them without going into the saferoom.
On his mechanical spider legs, newly enhanced and fortified, Jamal can move terrifyingly fast.
Carl's No Disassemble has wrecked Jamal's legs, the fifth set he has been given, because they were not shielded. Katia has made him another set, and Mordecai has it.
Jamal is bouncing up and down on a new set of legs.
Mordecai has given Jamal's front legs grabbers that look like hands.
Jamal's legs now have new and improved sticky feet, good enough to walk upside down on a ceiling and get stuck there.
Jamal's legs are wrecked and have fallen off him again, though he is alive.

Dazzlers are part alarm, part spotlight trap, one of the few trap modules allowed in a trebuchet. Each strobes coloured light into the eyes of the nearest enemy soldier, and all of them play the same song at the same time.
When every war protection on the field is stripped away, the Dazzlers keep flashing and playing.
War Crime is a spellbook Donut drew from her 1914 box. The book itself is bleeding and crying, and she is not sure she should read it.
War Crime is one of Donut's Atrocity-class spells, which the Nest tower is built to amplify, and it is the part of the plan Carl prays they will not need.

War Crime combines two of Donut's spells in a way most governments would call unconscionable, once a floor and only on the Scolopendra levels, three times in all. Nobody it catches can die of it, so it needs a finisher.
Donut has cast War Crime with Bijanbi and Astral Paw, and thousands of soldiers and a god have been slammed through Li Na's chains. It made her The Oak Fell, Champion of Nekhebit.
Donut has cast War Crime once and cannot cast it again before the twelfth floor; asked which three spells she would combine next, she says nothing is off the table.

A necklace of Indelible Woe trades a random spell of its wearer's for one of a target's, and for one of the target's five highest-level spells if the wearer kills the target. It works only on crawlers and people like Tipid, and Tipid reckons King Rust has one.
King Rust's body is in Carl's inventory, and with it a second Ring of Divine Suffering and the necklace.
Li Na asked about the necklace and decided against it, because it could cost her one of her level-15 dreads. It stays in Carl's inventory.

entries.name: Carl's chain dragon tattoo
entries.role: Li Na's skill, on Carl's arm

taglines.text: Katia is tattooing a chain shaped like a dragon on Carl's right arm. It carries a level-13 skill Li Na gave freely, at the cost of five of her levels for a while, and if it is drawn well it should last him the rest of the floor.
The tattoo's skill is Profane Iron, a once-a-day burst of chains that rip out of Carl's skin for about thirty seconds. He can truly control two of them; Li Na controls ten.

entries.name: Spellbook of Run, Little Günter, Run

taglines.text: A special-edition spellbook from Carl's 1914 box that grows centipede legs, drips black goo and begs not to be read. Its spell summons Little Günter, a one-hit creature who stores whatever attack hits him and carries it to a target.
Carl uses Run, Little Günter, Run to double a bomb: Günter should come through the blast unhurt and carry it down the hallway to the god, and a second, distant explosion follows.
Little Günter carries a mallet blow just as well as a bomb, and he still says hello first.
Carl held a potion of Conscription behind his back when Prepotente landed, the other way of bringing him into the army, and put it away the moment Prepotente asked to be recruited.

The war mages are conscripting gods with hell-kissed versions of it, level 18, five of them bought at the Midnight Market with the Gate of the Feral Gods. One worked on Yarilo, and the war mage who threw it blew up.
Li Na duplicated one taken off a dead war mage and gave Carl the copy, a screaming glass bottle brewed in the Nothing by Krakaren Prime, and he broke it over Lucia Mar's head.
Lucia Mar and Harpocrates are both conscripted into the Princess Posse until the floor ends.

Mordecai brewed this potion for the push into Club Vanquisher. For an hour it closes the drinker off from aura effects, Blessings and Dreads alike, though it does not cancel effects already in place or the drinker's own auras, and it does not work on pets.

The Waffle Maker is Carl's thermobaric bomb: about the punch of the one that needed wheels, minus the Fear, in a device the size of a thermos. It incinerates everything within a hundred meters, and Louis carries fifty of them on Party Planner.

Carl's third celestial item is a hairbrush of shining gold with a jewelled handle that screams like a concert crowd as he brushes. Five minutes through long hair buys thirty hours of Shining Charisma, Speedster, a quarter more constitution and Entourage, so the hair stays long.

entries.name: Enchanted Spiked Kneepads of the Munificent Goddess Kina

aka.name: Enchanted Spiked Knee pads the Munificent Goddess Kina

taglines.text: Katia's celestial award from Club Vanquisher is a pair of divine knee pads made of a sea goddess's eyelashes: melee damage reflected, breathing underwater, swimming, and skills for eating magic items and corpses. Katia has already taken them off and given them away.
Donut wears them now, a celestial gift from Katia, and they fit her.
Penelope the pig wears them now, and they give her the same temporary deity effects as Carl's Scavenger's Daughter patch.

The Engine of Tomorrow is Li Jun's new celestial eye, a swirling black orb that becomes a tiny clockwork engine when it works. It shows him muscles tensing and slows his sense of time in short bursts, so he sees a strike coming.
Li Jun is dead, and his sister has put his eye into herself.

The patch from a Legendary Lucky Bitch Box shows a bare foot crushing four-leaf clovers. Sewn on, it deflects one fatal blow a floor into a party member instead, and Carl has no intention of wearing it.
Carl has sewn the four-leaf-clover patch onto his jacket above the Midnight Epicure patch: once a floor, a blow that would kill him goes into someone in his party.
The Four-Leaf Clover Patch has fired once on this floor, passing a spell meant to kill Carl to his party member, Penelope the pig.

Zhang's Cape of Odds is his celestial prize from the fight at Club Vanquisher, a white cape printed with an archery target. It adds fifteen per cent to every stat and, once an hour, offers a spin of three hundred and thirty-three outcomes, sixty-six of them bad.
Zhang ripped the cape off and threw it on the table when he despaired of stopping Li Na, and pulled it back on to go and tell her the new plan.

Edgar is inking a tattoo onto a shaved patch of Donut's right flank to carry Bijanbi, a Dinner Bell variant taken from a cleric who fell defending the FUPA, and Milk is to etch words of power over it to raise the spell's level. He is drawing a dog.

Edgar inked Donut's dog tattoo on her right flank in a hurry: a simple line drawing of a dog that lifts its leg and licks itself. It holds Bijanbi, a variant of Dinner Bell, and Milk's words of power have pushed it to fifteen until the ink fades.
Donut can cast Bijanbi together with her Astral Paw, and she thinks the stupid dog tattoo has just bitten her.

The adept's fountain pen is the most basic of all the calligrapher's implements, and the System calls it the most versatile item anyone can own. Milk gives it to Carl along with a wineskin of Stayfast Ink.

Stayfast Ink comes in a wineskin, 825 ml, enough for several chonky books, and nothing will ever make it fade. Milk gives it to Carl with an adept's fountain pen, after telling him the recipes she once wrote in a different ink have faded away.
A Mini Tactical Nuke rides on the back half of the biggest Reaver sentry dogs. When Elle froze one solid, Carl hauled the burning block of ice into his inventory before it could go off.
Carl still has his, attached to its dog, and keeps quiet about it; Samantha has one of her own hidden up her neck hole.

entries.name: A Banquet Fit for a Princess

taglines.text: A Banquet Fit for a Princess is Donut's own book from the crawlers leaving the dungeon: pictures and kind words about her, and on each page a skill or spell its painter gave up. Eating a page lends her the spell for a short while.
Every page in it that offered lightning magic has been removed, and Donut carries a dozen lightning spells into Club Scolopendra.

entries.name: Carl's Book of Boom
entries.role: The second volume of the Book of Voodoo

taglines.text: When the Book of Voodoo floods with entries it splits in two, and the second volume is Carl's Book of Boom: pages painted by crawlers leaving the dungeon, each a note of thanks with a skill or spell he can eat to use for a short while.
Every page in it that offered lightning magic has been removed, and Carl has consumed ten different spells for the fight against Scolopendra.

Made human again by Eileithyia, Katia is missing her right arm to the shoulder, her left leg, her right leg up to the knee and an ear. She built cybernetic parts for herself in anticipation, Bautista finished them, and she waves goodbye with her cybernetic right arm.

The Scorpion's Bite is a non-magical quadruped weapon mount from the Apothecary's gold benefactor box, a bandolier that lets Donut carry ranged weapons on her back and fire and load them from her inventory. Katia's crossbow, bigger than Donut herself, forms on it.
Loaded with Katia's Bolt of Ophiotaurus, the mount puts a bolt into one of Emberus's eyes, and a Danforth bolt into the other.

The wheel gives the Royal Court a Big Shot Chicken food truck, about twenty feet long, with a faux-1920s hood, chrome fenders, a brand-new aluminium kitchen in the back and no passenger seat. A giant plastic tommy gun on its roof partly blocks the windshield.
After every race the garage regenerates the food truck to the form it started in. Its first upgrade is a set of retractable spider legs, Hedy's pick, which can climb walls when they are switched on.

The food truck races on spider legs and resizable all-terrain tires, with a gyro that keeps it from flipping, a full Bubble Buddy shield, a heat sink, booster rockets, and Roller Limbo, which lets it race upside down.
Off the tenth floor, the truck's racing rules no longer apply: its consumables are no longer magically refreshed, and all damage has to be repaired by hand.
The food truck is the last float in the Royal Court's procession, with Dwight's looted magic missile launcher on its roof and a crew of sluggalos at the wheel and the deep fryer.
Smashed, stinking of fire and somehow still running, the food truck pulls up beside Carl with about ten sluggalos left inside.
Dwight is a sparkling unicorn, more magical than most, and the System advises that whoever kills him should grab his horn as quickly as possible, because certain parties value such horns.
Dwight's horn is a weapon as well as a treasure: in the Lollipop he stabs the karaoke DJ in the face with it.
Dwight's magical horn is in Donut's inventory, taken from his head before the notification of his death has even arrived.
Oozy Form is a special-edition spell book that ran out of the mailbox on little legs, spewing slime. Carl has read it, and he can turn into a slime and slip through cracks until the spell runs out.
Carl used Oozy Form for the first time in the cul-de-sac, to slide up to Jasha and Radoslav's beers and swap one for a bomb.
In Oozy Form, Carl has carried Penelope through the inside of Scolopendra, the pig made part of him by the backpack on his chest.
An Emergency Gremlin scroll is a heavy green summoning scroll that clanks like metal. It calls up a gremlin who can fix a vehicle that breaks down mid-race, or a biological mount.
A summoned emergency gremlin arrives in overalls with a toolbox, a little different every time, and explodes when its summoning runs out.

The Assassin's Veil is a beaded Egyptian headdress for a female cat, worn in the court of the goddess Sekhmet. It adds ten percent to dexterity and warns its wearer when someone nearby readies a spell or a skill, and the enemies of Sekhmet turn hostile at the sight of it.

entries.name: The Crupper of the Benevolent Champion

taglines.text: The Crupper of the Benevolent Champion is a plain silver crupper of fine chain mail from a celestial box, the matching piece to Donut's champion cloak.

The crupper has the cloak's abilities, and worn together as a set they buff Donut's constitution a further twenty percent, take Find Weakened to level 10 and let her raise Puddle Jumper to 16. A third piece of the set would earn her a fourth.
The Danforth is an enchanted crossbow bolt that does no damage and anchors the part of a body it hits in place, for two seconds per level of the shooter's Crossbow skill. Donut has about ten of them.
Donut puts a Danforth bolt into Emberus's second eye, after Katia's Bolt of Ophiotaurus takes the first, and the god cannot move.

The Nemes of Pestilence is a striped pharaoh's headdress that came with Donut's new class, for Mongo. When he is within three meters of her and her health falls below ten percent, he turns invulnerable and twice as strong for sixty seconds, once a day, and his bites carry a 75 percent chance of Cruel Sepsis.
Donut's new Gurkha class has brought wild clothes for every pet, but Mongo keeps the nemes on for the parade's fight, with kukri claw caps on his feet besides.

The Wrap of Sekhmet's Compassion is a red headband, Rambo-style, that came with Donut's new class, for Rend. When he is within three meters of Carl and Carl's health is below ten percent, Rend turns invulnerable for sixty seconds, once a day, and gains the Heal Party Member skill, and his fatal bites have a 75 percent chance of casting a level 10 Raise Bootlicker on the corpse.
Rend has come back from his sixth death bigger, and the headband from Donut's class has stayed with him, slipped down to half cover his eyes.

Donut's right front claws glow a brilliant blue since her godslayer box, and four red claw caps from the shop, bought by Rosetta, mute the glow to purple. She can take them off and put them back on through her inventory.

Ice Slick is a special-edition spell book, freezing cold to the touch, for a spell that lays an inch-thick sheet of ice over a wide area. It starts at level 5 and trains faster, and Donut calls it an Elle spell.
Donut's Ice Slick normally casts in a cone, but laid along Carl's Gutter Bumper it follows a whole river and runs half as far again.

entries.name: Quadruped baby backpack
entries.role: A chest carrier for a pet

taglines.text: A Gold Adventurer Box has given Carl a pink baby backpack, worn on the chest, that only carries quadrupeds. With a passenger buckled in, his Phase or Oozy spell takes them too, and Donut refuses to get in it.
Mordecai has modified the backpack to fit a giant pig, and Carl wears Penelope strapped against his chest.

entries.name: Enriched Pet Biscuit
entries.role: A pet biscuit with a known result

taglines.text: An Enriched Pet Biscuit is a highly refined pet biscuit with a known result instead of a gamble. Prepotente has three from a celestial box: the Paramour, Nothing Special, and Nothing Special Party Companion.
The Nothing Special Party Companion biscuit has made Penelope the pig a sapient crawler who cannot talk out loud, in a party with Carl because he fed it to her.
Donut, combining in a hurry from Carl's inventory, put the wrong pet biscuit into the bomb for Scolopendra, and the boss comes out of her goo a level-one crawler in Carl's party instead of a pet.

The Enchanted Juvenile Macropus Dominus Skin is a dead joey's hide worn as a costume, with clawed gloves, padded palms and big kangaroo feet. It protects from seeping acid and gives a level-10 Jump, and it is a twelve-hour timed item that will not come off.
In the crash at the end of heat three the kangaroo skin flays off Carl as he slides down the road, and its feet catch fire, but the shredded suit is still on him.
Carl's shredded kangaroo suit has two hours left on its timer, and he still has to move in little hops.

Hobgoblin big boom satchels are explosive satchels Carl keeps ready in his inventory. Two of them, released at the bottom of a demon kangaroo's pouch and set off from outside, blow a level-170 gatekeeper apart.

Denial of Service missiles are Rosetta's idea: a load for Carl's eight-pack launcher, a different recipe from his potion balls but just as insidious, for a race in which every team has a shield and a direct attack will likely do nothing.
A Denial of Service missile does not explode. Its impact sets off a chemical reaction that spreads a thick membrane of green slime over a wide area, blinding a vehicle under its own shield.

The Smart Companion Royal Pet Throne is the passenger seat the audience voted Donut: an ordinary bucket seat until she sits on it, when it grows a fluffy bed, monitors her vitals, feeds her snacks and agrees with everything she says. Donut has named it Dorota and given it a Polish accent.
Dr. Metcalf, whom the chair's very existence has annoyed from the start, has cut Dorota off mid-sentence and put her into diagnostics mode, out of commission for a few hours.

Eris's five-sided coin looks like a plain poker-chip-sized coin with her laughing face on one side and a swirl on the other, until she reveals four fates on it. Carl snatches it out of the air, and it dissolves into a swirl tattoo on his palm that spins on its own.
Eris has told Carl not to forget about the coin: they have until the end of the twelfth floor to figure out how the fifth side lands.
A disintegration trap is a hidden trap module. Carl pulled one off the secret door that Akuma was hiding behind at the back of a diner.
Disintegration traps fire in silence and take a single target. Carl has laid two beside the Tigrans' truck, set to go off only under a Tigran.
Both of Carl's disintegration traps have fired, and team One Fine Pig is out of the race. No notification has come about Penelope.
From this race on, the team that wins a heat is given a key. It opens a single garage of a defeated team, with whatever supplies, items or even vehicle or mount are left inside.
Carl's first garage key opened the house of One Fine Pig, and Penelope the pig was inside.
A garage key can be looted. Donut took Dwight's last two and came back with a bear and a dog for the parade.

Splooge is the crew's name for the secretions the bat dudes sell at the pit stop. Half a potion bottle's worth protects the drinker from most environments for about half an hour; it smells like poop and, Louis says, tastes like Miami swamp ass.
Splooge has carried Carl through toxic air, kept a starfish alive, and calmed a panicking pig, who now craves it.
Splooge does not let anyone breathe where there is no air at all. It is a type of potion, but it is treated more like a food-based buff, so the cooldown rules do not apply to it.

Gelded Choirboy is a scroll that lets Carl physically hit notes his deeper voice cannot, at the cost of sounding squeaky. Mordecai insists the name is not literal, and Carl reads it alongside a few singing potions Mordecai has compounded together to get round the cooldowns.
On the Choirboy scroll and Mordecai's potions, Carl sings Take On Me through a bar brawl and hits the high note, and he is granted permanent access to the Stage Performance Guild.

An XL pet carrier cannot hold a crawler, but it can suck one in who allows it, for about ten seconds before it breaks. Mordecai's has a device fixed to the outside, and it is how the crew means to get Li Na out.
Big-Ass Magnet is a spell on a page of Donut's A Banquet Fit for a Princess, drawn by Mees Koning, a half-orc mage she was once kind to for about a minute. It casts at level 14.

Cast on an object, Big-Ass Magnet activates at once and grows stronger for about fifteen seconds. Donut casts it on Dong's lance, and it pulls every screw within two hundred metres toward him and Corcunda as they charge Grull.

The hidden beer-can bomb is a peach-flavoured Busch Light from Team Free Love's own magical cooler, drilled out in Carl's bomber's studio and refilled with an explosive that only a level-12 Find Traps skill would notice. Carl sets it off himself.

The Tome of Gatekeeper is Donut's spell book from the floor prize, a paperback Advance Reader Copy that can be installed now and works from the twelfth floor. It strips a target of their class skills and abilities for a while, and a deity of most of its spells.

Gurkha hats come with Donut's Elite Gurkha Warrior class: wide-brimmed, camel-coloured hats worn at an angle that reshape to fit whoever wears them. A mercenary's raises several melee skills by three levels, and Donut's raises several skills by five.

Petey Motteux's Little Secret is a large, thick nipple ring from the jewellery Mistress Tiatha set aside from earlier crawlers. It gives its wearer the Oxygenated benefit, marks bars, dance halls and chocolate houses on the map, and is now through one of Penelope's nipples.
A Tracking Tag is a dart Carl finds sticking out of his leg after the last fight in the arena, with no idea when or how it got there. Its text says the Kyryap has claimed him.
At 2:23 in the morning on January 3rd, every building on the planet came down at once, and almost everyone who was indoors died.
The dungeon has eighteen levels, and whoever completes the last one wins the planet back from the Borant Corporation's regency.
Every floor runs on a timer, and when it expires, the floor collapses with everyone still on it.
The crawl is a television programme called Dungeon Crawler World, broadcast across the Syndicate's three billion star systems, and the survivors are its cast.
The recap plays on the safe-room screens, narrated by an orange, four-eyed, lizard-like creature. The premiere is mostly about last season, and it has no time at all for Donut's boss fight.
Carl has been given several of something that sounds a lot like loot boxes. The rat man tells him where they are kept, and then tells him that he cannot get at them yet.
Loot boxes come in six tiers, from bronze to celestial, each far rarer than the last. They open only in a safe room, all of them at once and lowest tier first.

Compensated Anarchist is Carl's class, a unique hybrid of monk and rogue: trapmaker, bomb-maker and social-media dynamo, happy to throw a Molotov through a window one moment and to plead on camera for the violence to stop the next.
Former Child Actor is Donut's class, a hybrid of bard and rogue built on charisma and chance. On every floor she picks a new specialty, and the AI decides how much of it she gets.
The Desperado Club is somewhere a Desperado Pass gets you into, and Carl and Donut both have one now, as tattoos. What the club actually is, the pass does not say.
There is a second door in the safe room with an X over it, and its box says that Personal Spaces are not yet available, as though a crawler could one day buy a place of their own down here.

A personal space is a pocket room that travels with you. Carl, Donut and Katia have each been given coupons for beds, a shower, a crafting studio and a training room, and Donut has installed a cat tree.

The bubbles are not stage sets. Hump Town, the dirigible gnomes' castle in the air and the necropolis underneath were all here and running, with histories of their own, long before any crawler arrived.
On the ninth floor, the rich who come to fight in Faction Wars can really die now, the same as everybody else.

Primal is a race whose preview model is empty, because nobody alive knows what the Primals looked like: the first species to conquer the universe, gone one day without a note. It costs Carl fifteen stat points compared with staying human, and in exchange every skill he trains has a higher ceiling.
Orren has cut into the broadcast to explain what Primal Engines and Macro AIs are, and to admit that the AI running this crawl has taken control away from the showrunners.
The AI has told the galaxy what it is. The Primals never vanished: they closed their society down and kept their minds alive in a collective, and every Macro AI, this one included, is a Primal.
A war mage called Dismember rides the Dismemberment Limited with his fleshers, and Donut's Hole spell takes his head off.
Nobody makes a war mage. Resleeve a symbiote, a skeleton and a flesher a dozen times or more, and the magic left in the body wakes up sapient, hundreds of spells deep and notoriously cruel.
The war mages have left the realm with the Scavenger's Daughter, which was what they came for. The system has ruled their rebellion defeated, and they do not appear to mind.

A Rage Elemental is Borant's penalty for any human-born crawler who relieves themselves outside a designated bathroom. It is plucked from the thirteenth floor, and it kills the offender and everyone in their party.

The rage elemental took Yolanda and hammered on the safe room door for hours. Carl finally destroyed it with bombs, obstacles and a safe room door used as an ejector, with the whole universe watching.
Mordecai was born a skyfowl and became a Changeling on the third floor of his own crawl. Now he changes form every time his guildhall is moved.
A Changeling can take any shape, but Mordecai does not get to choose his. Every time his guildhall moves, the dungeon picks a mob from the current floor, and he wears whatever he is given.
There are Changelings all over this floor, some of them in the uniforms of the dromedarian guards, and one of them has been wearing the faces of a chained gnome's loved ones to break him.
According to the Maestro, nine families fight the Faction Wars on the ninth floor. His Skull Clan has won six of the last ten, and the Blood Sultanate is almost always the first to be eliminated.

Donut's fan club and Princess D'nadia have secured two of the nine places in Faction Wars, and one of those teams belongs to the crawlers. The faction sponsors fight behind safety protocols that the crawlers do not have.

Faction Wars now has ten teams: nine attacking the city and the NPCs defending it. The sponsors' safety protections have been voted away, and the crawlers are fighting inside the war rather than beside it.
The faction sponsors come to the ninth floor inside safety protocols that the crawlers do not have. Removing them is an action item on Carl's list, and the first vote goes two to seven against.
Mordecai asks who their warlord adjutant is, gets a blank look, and puts off explaining.
An adjutant is the referee attached to each team on the ninth floor, and Odette means to ask for the job with Carl's team.
Feral Goose is the name on a dead neighbourhood boss, and Mordecai's rule of thumb is that anything with feral in its name is usually bad news.
The word turns up again in the name of an artifact buried in the necropolis, and Mordecai's advice holds: stay away from anything marked feral.
Feral marks something that has been inside the Nothing. Every time the Gate closes, a feral god comes through, and other gods do not like feral ones.

Every season, the land crabs leave their forests to spawn in the ocean, and the monk seals, who hold those waters sacred, consider it a sacrilege most foul. The System has made it a quest, and the crawlers are getting involved whether they like it or not.

The Recital is a quest that arrived on the day Donut renamed the town Point Mongo. Something is driving the dinosaurs at its fences, and the crawlers must find out what they want, or exterminate them.

CrawlCon is the galaxy's fan convention, held once every other season, with thousands attending in person and billions virtually. Carl's fans have voted him onto the roster, and no active crawler has been on it in more than a century.
The cookbook's twenty-second edition mentions a formal way of attaching separate parties to one another, switched on from the sixth floor, if it still exists.

The guild system is live. A charter costs upward of half a million gold, and a level-one guild joins five parties through a shared common area, with upgrades and experience that can be shared for a fee.
Vengeance of the Daughter is a Syndicate drama shot inside the dungeon, with a circus, a half-naiad who would be tsarina if she were full-blooded, and a guest-star slot for Carl.
The grief in Vengeance of the Daughter is real, but the schedule is not. Someone outside the floor decides when Signet mourns, and counts how many are watching.
The Dream has bought Vengeance of the Daughter, and it means to collect on the third season that Carl's contract guarantees.
A stairwell is an iron staircase wide enough for twenty, with warmth and light rising out of the ground. In a frozen city, it is the only warm place left.
Magic Missile came out of a tome in Donut's loot, and she had taught herself the spell before anyone could tell her how. A tome teaches a spell for good; a scroll casts it only once.
A safe room is always on the map, even under the fog of war, with restrooms, sleeping cubicles and, in some of them, food. There is no time limit, except the floor's own.
Bopca Protectors are magical, gnome-like creatures who exist solely to watch over safe rooms. They scrub the toilets and cook the food, they are surly and smelly, and they never wash their hands.

A Bopca Protector runs every safe room, like Wendita behind the counter of a red-and-white fast-food restaurant here. The good ones, like Tally and Sebastian, are excellent cooks who treat the cat like royalty.
Brindle Grubs are the janitors of the second floor. They eat whatever gets killed, and the more they eat, the bigger they grow.
Clockwork Triplicate splits a pet or minion into three real copies, each with a mind of its own. After about a minute, the copies fall apart into gears and go up in smoke.

Jikininki are the most common ghouls in the Iron Tangle, the best-behaved and the most insatiable. They will generally leave you alone, as long as you are not bleeding, you do not litter, and you stay out of their personal space.
According to a train engineer, the Kravyad handle the rail employees who get off at station 435 and go through the portal home, and anyone who takes that path loses time and memory.
The Kravyad wait at station 435, where the rail employees get off. Madison, who works above them, insists that they are not bosses at all but part of human resources.
Skyfowl are what Mordecai was born as: going by the photograph of his brother, a golden, eagle-like creature with angel's wings folded on its back.

Skyfowl look like eagles, with feet and wings but no arms. On the fifth floor Mordecai is one again, a rock edge skyfowl cleric with clipped wings, in the first body close to his own in a very long time.
A Tummy Acher is one of the caged pets for sale: a meatball with two legs and a mohawk.
A Tummy Acher is a pet-class mob, once a parasite in the guts of titans, that grows stronger every time it dies. This one bonded with Carl over a single bowl of chowder.

Ping is a five-mana spell that marks everything that is neither a crawler nor red-tagged. Everything it finds hears it, and the System calls it a tool for those who do not care if their quarry knows they are coming.
Also known as "Here piggy, piggy" and the Night Dread, Ping finds almost nothing in a castle full of robots, which is exactly how the drake stands out.
Sluggalos are slugs that pour out of infected mercenaries every few minutes, hundreds of them in a room full of blood. Imani calls them punk rock, and Carl corrects her.
The System files them as Pox Slugs, but the Sluggalos come out of the boils of the SlugPox in clown makeup, with hatchets and a rowdy culture of their own, and throw themselves at the demons.
A ManTauR, according to the System, is half human and half human, and bred for strength and dexterity, which here means driving trains.
Where a centaur has a horse, a mantaur has a second human half, and the System calls it one of the weirdest of all the 'taurs.

Protective Shell comes with a pair of enchanted boxers: once every thirty hours, a sphere that no mob can enter, lasting twenty seconds and growing with the wearer's intelligence. It does not move with you.
Protective Shell ignores solid objects and stays exactly where it was cast. Cast it inside a speeding train, and it rolls back through the cars like a bulldozer, pushing every mob before it.
The world froze, heavy metal played, and Carl's face appeared in the air with Death Challenge! stamped across it in blood. The announcer promised the live death of a celebrated crawler.
A Death Challenge is not a boss battle but a pop-up gambling event. The AI put Carl's survival at fifty to one, and Borant has appealed over how slowly it moved the odds.
Pustule once watched her mother bite the head off a vorpal muskrat, and her mother died of it. You cannot bite the head off a vorpal muskrat, she says, without doing a little dying.

Astrid has unleashed the vorpals from behind the Desperado Club's Do Not Enter door, as a last resort against a feral demon loose in the club. She will not say what they are, only that they are going to kill everything.

According to Mordecai, vorpal is a condition, not a species. Vorpals are deputised by the gods and drawn to demons, stronger and angrier the nearer one is, and liable to blow themselves up rather than lose.

T'Ghee is a card game from the home planet of Allister, the thirteenth edition's author: somewhere between chess and go fish, and part of his people's meditation-based religion. His copy of the Cookbook came as a deck of the cards.
Each squad leader has twenty flags. Plant one in a living thing below five percent health, and it becomes a T'Ghee totem card that fights for whoever summons it. Lost flags are not replaced.

A T'Ghee deck holds totems, utility, snare, mystic and special cards. Four are drawn when combat starts and one more every ten seconds, and a squad leader cannot use spells or inventory until the deck is spent.
A squad flag does not check what it is stabbed into, and it works on a dying crawler just as well as on a monster.

entries.name: Containment Interface
entries.role: Bootleg interface upgrade · the AI's failsafe
