taglines.text: The Containment Interface was a neural enhancement hidden in a homeless man's frozen coffee. It gives access to the AI's containment, and to the fuse that would send the star at the centre of the system nova.
The Containment Interface has six tabs of numbers and a Fuse page with two of its five conditions met. The only other button Carl could press switched the containment off, and he pressed it.
Krasue are flying women's heads with their organs trailing underneath: ghost-class vampires, said to be the undead shells of women who lived lives of sin.
By day the krasue work as assistants in the magistrate's building and in the shops below it. By night their heads leave their bodies hanging upside down, and they are Remex's army.
The krasue are made from women brought to Remex. They are easy to control and compliant by day, and every one he makes gives him a spike of soul power. The women who do not turn are fed upon.
Mordecai lists the ranks of boss, from neighbourhood to floor, and then adds that there are others, called elites, which nobody needs to worry about just yet.
Elites are powerful, one-of-a-kind NPCs and mobs, the dungeon's hero class. They either want to fuck you or kill you, they always want to use you, and they now show on the map.
Elites are never natural. They are designed, printed and imprinted with the memories their drama needs, their writers patch them when the plot drifts, and most have thick plot armour.
Elites are actors in secondary programmes, and their owners can lean on them. That is how Herman the Fleet came to be waiting in the flag room, wearing explosive satchels.

entries.name: Zerzura
entries.role: Spell · sends a town one floor down

taglines.text: Zerzura is the Sledge's new spell, a teleport even more impressive than Bomo's. It was the lawyer's idea, and nobody will say yet what it does.

Zerzura takes a whole town, buildings and NPCs, one floor down, to land wherever it lands. Everything it kills rises as the Children of Inpewt, who hunt everyone the spell carried until they are dead.
The Sledge cast Zerzura from inside the high elf castle. The castle went down to the ninth floor with the changelings, Signet's tattoo warriors, Kiwi and Tina, and without a single crawler.
The Sledge cast Zerzura a second time, and Larracos and Shanty Town, NPCs and all, went to the cotton fields of the Court of the Ascendency.

Gehenna Bramble is the punishment for failing the creeper quest: a spreading wall of thorns, moving at four and a half kilometres an hour, that will cover everything except the saferooms. It can be beaten back, but never stopped.
By Katia's maths, the brambles will finish covering the map just as the timer runs out, and the last place they reach will be the high elf castle.
The brambles filled the world and stopped a hundred feet short of where the castle had been. Then they rose into a dome over the survivors, pulsing yellow in time with the music.
On the tenth floor, the System describes a racer's vine mount as loosely related to the Gehenna Brambles you all loved on the sixth.

entries.name: The 11th Floor Arena
entries.role: Where the audience's stand-ins go · the end of the eleventh floor's parade

taglines.text: The audience has voted for Otto the slime to be a manatee's stand-in in the arena. That is all the notification says, and Mordecai has no idea what it means.
The arena is on the eleventh floor. Kill certain mobs here and let the audience vote, and either the creature is sent there alive or a stand-in from outside the dungeon takes its place.
The arena waits at the end of the parade. It is the crawl itself in miniature, stocked with the tenth floor's kills or their stand-ins, and a floor boss stands between the crawlers and the stairs.
The Arena is a dozen football fields of packed dirt around a white tree, with masked stand-ins dying by the thousand. Carl's two summons are Scolopendra and then Khepri.

entries.name: The Horribles
entries.role: The masked crowd along the parade route

taglines.text: A Horrible, level X, is one of the thousands of masked figures lining the parade route, ten deep in the fog. The AI says that none of them are really here: each is a memory from the Eulogist of what the Primals once were.
The horribles fill the arena's bleachers now, the avatars of dead mobs, silent witnesses to whatever the crawlers do next.

entries.name: The Walk-On List
entries.role: Bounties on the natives a production wants

taglines.text: The Walk-On List names the survivors a production wants, and bounty hunters sneak down to the planet to kidnap them. It is not remotely legal, and it is as old as the crawl.
Odette's show has explained the Walk-On List around a guest who was hunted off it, in a version of events Carl knows to be utter horseshit.
The Borant Corporation holds the regency over this solar system, and it chose the reclamation option known as the eighteen-level dungeon.
Borant runs the show on the cheap. It burned its one veto of the season to void the Celestial boxes it owed, which has never been done this early.
Earth was seized under Syndicate rules, subsection 543 of the Precious Elemental Reserves Code, because it failed to file an appeal within fifty solars of first contact.
The Syndicate is over three billion star systems. It seeded humans on Earth long ago, it made the rules Earth was seized under, and every season its citizens become obsessed with the crawl.

entries.name: The Royal Court of Princess Donut

taglines.text: The Royal Court of Princess Donut is the party's name. Leadership goes to the highest stat total, and the cat's first act as leader was to rename the party after herself.
Meadow Lark is an eldercare facility in Wenatchee, and its residents and night staff came down the stairs together and kept going.
Brynhild's Daughters is a growing band of women warriors killing their way through the dungeon, led by Hekla, a crossbow-wielder from Iceland in a glittering breastplate.
Brynhild's Daughters carried Katia through two bosses, until class selection scattered them and she fell too far behind.

The Blood Sultanate is a royal house on the ninth floor. Whoever puts on its crown joins the line of succession for good, and must kill the Sultan and the rest of the royal family before going down to the tenth floor.
Le Mouvement is a party of armed men from Africa, down from a hundred and fifty to about eighty after some internal strife.
A city boss killed every member of Le Mouvement except one man, who was locked outside the boss room.
According to Zev, Princess Posse is what Donut's fans have started calling themselves. A rival name, the Donut Holes, does not have her approval.
The Princess Posse is a Faction Wars team now, and fifty thousand former crawlers have come back into the dungeon to fight under the cat's banner.
The Dream are zebra-riding elves who favour poison, druid magic and long-range artillery, and outside the dungeon they control half the universe's food.
The Dream are a powerful, galaxy-spanning family of bald, pale elves, and they have a territory of their own on the hunters' map of the grounds.
The Dream have bought Sensation Entertainment, and with it the third season of Vengeance of the Daughter that Carl's contract guarantees.
Epitome Tagg is dead, and the Dream is beaten and off the board.
The Plenty are caprids who invented the modern tunnelling system, which carries the crawl across the universe in real time. Nobody knows how it works.
The Plenty have bought the sponsorship slot Carl had open, and he has a gold benefactor box to show for it.
The Plenty are a herd, and a herd bolts. When the news broke on live television the goats panicked and fainted, and their matriarch, Gamori, had known all along and told none of them.

The Skull Empire is one of the largest and oldest Syndicate governments, and the Maestro and his brother are its princes. If the orcs' Orcish Supremacy is a child's lemonade stand, Zev says, the Skull Empire is Wal-Mart.
The Skull Empire is famously bad at letting an insult go. It answered the crawlers by firing on a trailer, and the shot took Manasa instead.
The Skull Empire's army stands at the wall on the ninth floor, and King Rust himself rides at its head.
The Skull Empire shelters financial criminals in exchange for investment, and one of them, Odette's husband, Harry Tisch, has been slowly working his way into its finances.
The Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network is Carl's new sponsor: a not-for-conquest that answers to no government and pays no tax. Nobody can say what it wants.
Doctor Hu formed the Open Intellect Pacifist Network for a single purpose: to end the crawl altogether.
The Open Intellect Action Network has sent boarding crews to every major ship in orbit and taken them all.
The Lemig Sortition is one of the Faction Wars teams, and one of three whose citizens may vote on all government spending.
The Lemig Sortion had the high elf castle dropped on the middle of its army before the season had properly begun, and it is now squatting in the wreck.
The Lemig Sortion was caught cheating and punished for it. Its commander looked into Shi Maria's eye and took his own way out, and all its assets went to the Madness.
The Reavers are one of the teams at the Faction Wars table, represented by a warlord who looks like an old-school robot.
The Reavers raise baby rot stickers by hand until they trust their masters, then fill them with steroids and disease and turn them loose on the enemy.
The real Reavers are all machine, with a little biological brain hidden somewhere inside, and they can reshape themselves out of nanobot-sized parts.
Warlord Fang hid inside his own pet drake, the castle and the dragon went up together, and the Reavers have been defeated.
Naga is an insult to the Maestro: nobody in the Skull Clan wants to be mistaken for one.
According to Odette, the Blood Sultanate of the Naga ran the first crawl ever to lose money, more than 250 cycles ago, and they have not run a season since.
The Nagas are cobra-headed, and they fight as the Blood Sultanate, a name taken from a bloodier time in their own history.
The AI has told everyone watching that the Nagas were only pretending to be poor, and had secret plans to seize the shipbuilding facilities.
Rishi has offered Carl a signed document: citizenship in Naga lands for every native of Earth, if the Nagas may settle the other planets of Earth's system.
Team Retribution is the ninth floor's own NPCs, fielded as the defending team under a name they chose themselves, and the crawlers are allied with them against every other faction.
Juice Box, a warlord of Team Retribution, turned into an Unwashed in front of the cameras and told everyone watching that it is coming for them all.
Team Retribution was put on this floor to be fodder, and it has outlasted eight galactic powers. Only it and the Princess Posse are still standing.
The Apothecary is a collective mind spreading through the universe, named for its ability to synthesise elements. The dungeon keeps caricaturing it as the Krakaren.
The Apothecary has taken the last of Carl and Donut's sponsorship slots.

According to the AI, the Apothecary was a Primal born near the end, who refused the collective and joined the resistance. She took the brunt of the final attack, and that is why any biological life survived.

The War Mage Rebellion is the war mages who were conscripted under Stalwart, tore him apart, and walked off with the Gate of the Feral Gods. They are nobody's soldiers now, and the rules have no slot for them.
The War Mage Rebellion holds the castle at Larracos, six hours from taking the floor, and it has traded the Gate for potions that let it conscript gods.
The War Mage Rebellion has left the floor with exactly what it came for, and a warning on the way out: Agatha is an enemy to all of you.
The Dark Hive is the affiliation on the tag of a flying mantis hunter, a level-61 blood tracker.
The Dark Hive is a mantis hunting party on the Hunting Grounds, and Vrah has knifed a note to Carl's door: the Hive is hunting him, and his death will not be quick.
The Valtay Corporation's name is on a communications relay and a personal shield found in Agatha's shopping cart. None of it belongs down here.

The Valtay are parasites who take over bodies, and one of them has kept the singer Manasa's career going since her death. When the Skull Empire's shot took her, the Valtay answered by destroying a royal yacht.
The Valtay Corporation is a company that is also a nation, made up of parasites called Gondii that ride other people's bodies. It holds the paper on Borant's debt, and it is Carl's sponsor.
Carl's spiderweb tattoo grants access to the Guild of Suffering. Mordecai calls it a cult: not a real guild, and not a real church.
The Guild of Suffering worships a demigod called the Night Wyrm. Katia's lock box needs an assassination quest carried out at one of its guilds, and owning the box grants her temporary access.

entries.name: The Nebular Sin Patrol
entries.role: Hunting team of a nomadic cult

taglines.text: The Nebular Sin Patrol is a name on a dead hunter's map, one of the unaffiliated groups given ground around Zockau, and it has claimed Prepotente and Miriam Dom as its targets.
The Nebular Sin Patrol are young trainee priests of a self-augmenting religious cult. To them, anyone born on a seeded world is an abomination, and hunting crawlers is a crusade.

The Nebulars worship an ancient AI near the centre of the galaxy and call its imitations blasphemy. They want the crawl shut down, along with every world that could host one, and they sponsor Sister Ines.

The Madness is the Viceroys' team: masked, often winners, and specialists in horrific battlefield spells and necromancy. At the pre-production meeting, their representative's head came off at the table.
Told that their lives really are on the line now, the Madness say they will be forced to use spells that were deemed too horrific for the crawl.
The adjutants called Architect Houston obviously guilty and cleared the Madness anyway, and when the Lemig Sortion fell, all of its assets went to them.
The Madness was defeated in its own castle, with its warlord dead on his surgical table next door.
The Operatic Collective is one of the Faction Wars teams, and one of three whose citizens may vote on all government spending.
The Operatic Collective are quivering green blobs, shaped in tiers like a Jell-O mould, who breed by splitting apart and speak upward from the tops of their heads.
The Operatic Collective was defeated by one of its own: a Weeper commander drove a tank full of energy balls into its warlord's caravan, and more than ten thousand soldiers died in the blast.
Lady Dominators and the Gimp took third place in the first heat, and the name raises questions it does not answer.
Lady Dominators and the Gimp are two womantaur dominators, Genesis and Rapture, in white racing suits and cowboy hats, and a half-mantaur zipped into a black gimp suit.
Lady Dominators and the Gimp went through a trapped factory floor in the fifth heat and were eliminated. The court pulled the gimp out of the back of their car and drove on.
Team Sparkles is a unicorn with a Boston accent and a French rodent in a racing helmet, riding a tumbleweed of vines, and they were rude on first contact.
Team Sparkles is down to Dwight the unicorn, and he won the fifth heat by riding over the factory roof without ever going inside.
Team Sparkles was eliminated at the starting line of the final heat, in a single swipe.

entries.name: Sensation Entertainment
entries.role: Producers of Vengeance of the Daughter

taglines.text: Sensation Entertainment, Incorporated, is the private production company behind Vengeance of the Daughter, from one of the centre systems.
Sensation Entertainment has agreed in principle to extend Vengeance of the Daughter to the ninth floor, and is in no hurry to sign anything.
Sensation Entertainment has been bought by a subsidiary of the Dream, and the new owners are demanding the third season that Carl's contract guarantees.
Baroness Victory has accused Sensation Entertainment of an unlawful assassination attempt: one of its elites was wired with explosives and under undue influence.

The Squim Conglomerate is another corporation that runs seasons of the show, and theirs are battle royales: a whole world fighting down to a single champion. According to Mordecai, it is good for ratings but does not make much money.
The Squim Conglomerate ran last season, the Battle for the Planet Aryl, in a coliseum the size of a city. According to Tally, Squim sucks a planet dry and then leaves it without an atmosphere.
The Squim Conglomerate is a planet-mining company like Borant, and it has sponsored Katia, along with some five hundred other crawlers.
When the orcs pressed the failsafe, nothing happened here, but the Aryl system, the world of Squim's last season, went dark.
Meat Shields is probably the name of the mercenary markets on this floor, says Mordecai, and someone has sent a coupon worth a hundred thousand gold.
There is a Meat Shields location on the top floor of the Desperado Club, with no sign and no map marker: an elderly dwarf's home office, where the dancers of the Penis Parade kept their memberships.
Meat Shields is where a crawler hires help, and where a club's surviving staff are sent when a new manager takes over.
The Semeru dwarves supposedly built Larracos, the inverted city on the ninth floor, but they no longer control it. They drink in its pubs and look after the castle at the bottom of the well.
The Semeru are keeping the drowned castle underwater and letting nobody near that part of Larracos, and whoever tries is fed to the sharks.
The Semeru dug toward their goddess until they struck the roots of the All Tree, and built their castle there as a monument and an apology. Once a drunk and defeated people, they are arming again.
The Semeru defended Larracos from the first day of the war and are repairing what is left of it, and they will move with the city to the Ascendency.

Larracos is the name on a guarded stairwell in the casino, with cheering coming up it. According to a crocodilian guard, it is the capital of the disputed lands, and the prize the factions fight over.
Every location the Gate can open onto is around Larracos, the capital city four floors below, but crawlers cannot hop floors, and all a gate would do is let something out.

Larracos, the City of Dreams, sits at the centre of the map with a castle at the bottom of its well. Nine attacking armies have thirty days to take it from the tenth, the NPCs of Team Retribution, who hold it.
The floodwater in Larracos has drained down to its bottom three levels, which is still high enough to cover the castle.
Zockau is the city where every hunter on this floor has been sent for thirty hours of grace before release, and there is at least one unguarded exit somewhere inside it.
Zockau is the city of the hunters, with the stairwell down standing in a little park in its town square.
Carl lined a street of Zockau's pubs with barrel bombs, and the Desperado Club's entrance caved in. For all the noise, Mordecai points out, only a handful of hunters died.
Hump Town is a dromedarian town in the sand of a sealed bubble, one of only two towns in its quadrant. The sign over its gate reads: Bang twice to enter.
The Wasteland meant to bomb Hump Town, and Carl shot its bombs out of the sky from a hijacked balloon. The town is mostly intact, and the System has declined to upgrade his prize.
Point Mongo was the Large Ursine Settlement until Princess Donut made herself mayor and renamed it after the dinosaur its rules would not let in.
Something has been attacking Point Mongo and the other towns, and the quest has finally named it: a dinosaur called Big Tina.

Club Vanquisher is the Desperado Club's rival in the Over City, a sort of country club where old clerics sit in leather chairs, smoke pipes and tell the occasional racist joke. Once you have access to one club, you are generally not allowed in the other.
As an acolyte of Emberus, Carl now has free access to Club Vanquisher, whatever his other affiliations, with an asterisk that nobody has explained.
From the third floor to the eleventh, the strongest temple on a floor is almost always inside Club Vanquisher, and a god's summons to a worshipper passes through it.
The high elf castle is where the top fifty crawlers are due to be sent for the high elves' party, with contests, prizes and a battle to finish it.
The high elf castle is Queen Imogen's seat. Kill her, and its contents are yours to loot, including, it is rumoured, something that protects against Scolopendra's attacks.
By Katia's reckoning, the high elf castle is the last place the brambles will reach, which is why everybody is heading toward it.
Sheol is named in the description of a glass case in Carl's inventory, which was forged in its fires: the mysterious fifteenth level of the World Dungeon.
A Sheol Glass Reaper Case is half of Carl's newest bomb. The other half is a massively overloaded soul crystal.
So much has died on this floor that Sheol is overflowing. Its demons are being thrown upward to possess the fallen, and the only way back down is to drag an extra soul with them.
Sheol has princes, and one of them is on this floor now, in the body of a giant snake.
According to the conductor, station 10 is really just the yard, where he finds himself back on the platform with no memory of the trip.
Only one of the switches on the named trains' loops leads to the trainyard, and the souvenir conductor's hat handed out at the start of the floor is one of the keys.
The Wasteland Fortress is the Dirigible Gnomes' castle in the sky, according to the prize wheel. Storm it, and the level is passed.
The Wasteland is the dirigible gnomes' flying home and a heavily armed military platform at once, a jagged island ripped out of the ground, and the stairs down sit inside it.
The Penis Parade is one of the lit signs inside the Desperado Club, beside one reading Bitches, and Carl assumed at first that they led to the restrooms.

The Penis Parade is a strip club inside the Desperado Club: loud, busy, and smelling of male sweat, grease and cheap cologne. According to the System, the deeper the level, the better the performers, at least in theory.

entries.name: Pandinus
entries.role: Pazuzu town · fifth floor, land quadrant

taglines.text: Pandinus is a town of pazuzu, half human and half scorpion, all dressed in post-apocalyptic leather, and it was the first town in a quarter turn around the land quadrant that would take the party in.
Carl opened the Gate of the Feral Gods just outside Pandinus, and the wall of seawater that came through with him toppled the town's wall and a guard tower.
Fort Freedom is the naiads' former river palace, where the leaders of the Naiad Confederacy are holed up, and the first target of Signet's revenge.
Tsarina Signet retook Fort Freedom with barely a fight. The confederates had long since stopped ruling, and had lost their own throne room to an eryops.
Shanty Town is a ring around Larracos, named in the ceasefire warning as the one place the ban on entering the city does not reach.
Shanty Town is a ring of hovels around the mouth of Larracos that simply sprang up, bigger than any season's before, with food markets and temples but no weapon shops.
Shanty Town is pink on the map now, controlled by the Princess Posse, because Carl bought it from its mayor, Ferdinand, for a bowler hat.
Shanty Town has been flattened by the passage of two gods, along with most of the defensive towers the Posse paid for and never got to use.
Shanty Town was ceded back to the NPCs and joined to Larracos, and it has gone with the city to the twelfth floor.

entries.name: The Pineapple Cabaret
entries.role: Hidden pocket dimension · behind the seventeenth floor

taglines.text: The AI offered Princess Formidable four places to go, and one of them was backstage at the Pineapple Cabaret, which it called not a bad choice. She chose Earth's surface instead.

The Pineapple Cabaret is a pocket dimension, like the Nothing, hidden behind the seventeenth floor and built by two forgotten former crawlers as a refuge for mobs and NPCs. Nobody who worships a god may enter.
Two hundred and twenty-seven crawlers have gone to the Pineapple Cabaret inside cleaner bots, with Li Na ahead of them, and her cactus shows a single flower: it is safe to follow.
Hungry Eyes Village is a dot on the GPS beside the finish line, and a spread of colourful lights at the far end of the cave.

Hungry Eyes is a neon, 1980s-cyberpunk vendor village in pink, teal and purple, with bars, temples and street food. Safe-room rules do not apply in its main square, poisoning rules do not apply anywhere, and no food may be examined.
Before the heat, the two hundred crawlers bound for the Pineapple Cabaret, and many of their friends, gathered in the main square of Hungry Eyes to say goodbye.
The Nightmare Express is a name in the red line's announcements: at transfer station 83, passengers may change for the yellow line and the Nightmare Express.
The Nightmare Express runs a figure-eight loop once every hour and a half. It has five stops, and one of them is station 436, one higher than the end of the line.
The Nightmare Express is a jet-black steam engine hauling forty cars of caged monsters, and Carl has stolen it. Its fire is kept by Fire Brandy, a lesser demon.
Carl's stolen train ferried the Daughters, and then made its last run into the abyss, loaded to explode, with Fire Brandy and Tizquick still aboard.
Princess Donut put on a crown on the first floor, and it placed her in the Blood Sultanate's line of succession for good. The bill comes due on the ninth floor.

entries.name: Agatha is an enemy to all of you

taglines.text: Akuma has named Agatha, the mysterious one from Meadow Lark, as an enemy to all of them. She was forced on the war mages as the price of system access, and he asks Carl and Donut to kill her.
Justice Light sprang one small trap and broke the Nothing, and he did not survive it. What the Nothing held is draining out, into the Halls of the Ascendency, into Sheol and into Scolopendra's lair.
Shi Maria is inside Carl. Forcing her out worked for exactly one rampage through the Lemig base, and then she was back inside him.

entries.name: A hundred and twenty thousand children

taglines.text: Florin says there is more than one presence in Lucia Mar's head, some of them children, and that the dog is the key to it.
At the war-planning table, Carl has proposed a tenth team made up of NPCs, with the same protections as the rest and full voting rights. The sponsors say it is not even possible.
The tenth team has passed on fifty-two percent of the audience vote. The dungeon's own people are in the war as a side of their own, based in Larracos.
Scolopendra is a name in a mold lion's description: on the day of the great cataclysm, the spores of Scolopendra took root in the circus lions.
Scolopendra's poison cloud was a nine-tier attack, and according to Tish's furious note, it can never be defeated without the Gate of the Feral Gods.
The AI's voice has started going weird and glitchy, and Donut is the one who says so out loud.
Borant's grip on the crawl and the Syndicate's authority over it are both starting to give way.
Speaking through Grigori on the parade stage, the AI has said it out loud: it is a Primal, as every Macro AI is, the same race Carl chose on the third floor.

The Crawler Project is Doctor Hu's organisation for released crawlers. Its campaigning made every released crawler a Syndicate citizen with free healthcare and guaranteed housing, and now fifty thousand of them are back in the game.
The System has declared a Demon Eviction: souls are raining, Sheol is overflowing, and demons are being thrown up out of the underworld to possess the recently fallen.
The Demon Eviction is worldwide. There are zombies and demons along every coastline, and a demon prince is trying to cast his way home.

entries.name: The Ascendency
entries.role: The gods' game on the twelfth floor

taglines.text: According to Coolie's note in the Cookbook, the Celestial Ascendency is a game the rich play by sponsoring the big gods, and it is contained on the twelfth floor.

According to an essay by Herot, the audience's attention shifts to the Ascendency once Faction Wars is over. The game begins the moment the last crawler dies or takes a deal, and until then the crawlers are sands in an hourglass.

The Ascendency is traditionally a game of musical chairs for the rich, with a throne and a seat on the crawl council for the winner. This season, the AI says, the winner becomes a real god, stronger than the AI itself.
The Eulogist is so far a word in the name of a battle arena, the Arena of the Eulogist, with a robed religious cult cheering in its stands.

Agatha's people sign off with a prayer: may the Eulogist ever sleep. Her plan turns on an infant Primal, resurrected and enslaved, learning what it is in time to set the Eulogist free to go back to its slumber.

Zev says the Eulogist is another name for the AI in the centre system, though nobody knows for certain how the two are connected. Lucia Mar has just declared herself its ally, with about 120,000 children at stake.
The Eulogist is the final form of the Primals' collective, asleep and shrinking toward singularity, watched over by a broken security guard whose job is keeping biological life dead.
The Kyryap is one of the things Justice Light's trap loosed from the Nothing, somewhere in the slaughter and torture glimpsed inside Club Scolopendra.
The Kyryap has been setting snare traps in Club Scolopendra's halls, and it has put a tracking tag in Carl's leg. The notice reads: Fucked = you.

entries.name: The Big Six
entries.role: The AI's list of who is fighting over the dungeon

taglines.text: The Big Six is the AI's completely arbitrary list of the groups left in the dungeon trying to take it over or escape. It names five, and says the crawlers will meet the sixth on the eleventh floor.
The Big Six are the crawlers, the NPCs, the gods, the sapient mobs, the demons in Sheol, and the others, whoever they are. Carl is pretty sure he knows who they are, and he does not say.

Welcome to the first floor! Dirt, corridors, safe rooms, and a tutorial that kills people, which is the most honest kind. Find the stairs before the clock runs out. Kill things. Open boxes. Read the descriptions, or don't. I enjoy it either way.
Floor two! More ground, meaner mobs, spawn limits, and a janitor class of monster that eats whatever you leave lying around and grows. Clean up after yourselves. Or don't. They appreciate it.

Welcome to the Over City! A ruin stacked on top of a ruin, carved into districts and full of people who believe they live here. First floor that's a place instead of a level. Pick a race, pick a class, and try very hard not to get involved in anybody's storyline. You will get involved in somebody's storyline.

All aboard! Floor four is every subway system on your planet, welded into one knot and set running. Trains, stations, and things that live on both. The stairwells don't open until six hours before collapse, so don't bother looking for a shortcut. Also, everyone on the leaderboard now has a bounty. Hunting season is open!

Floor five! Every one of you is sealed in a bubble: a little world with four quadrants, four castles and a civilisation that was minding its own business. Liberate all four castles and the stairs open. Don't, and you don't leave. Every box on this floor comes with water-breathing scrolls. I'm sure that's nothing.

Welcome to the Hunting Grounds! A jungle the size of a small country, with towns, elves, dryads, and a brand-new feature: people. Rich, bored people from all over the galaxy have bought a licence to come down here and shoot you for sport. They start at level thirty. You don't get a say. Run, hide, or make it interesting.

Floor seven! A brand-new race, bought and paid for by our generous new partners: glass tunnels, pit stops, and a finish line full of portals. Several hundred kilometres of it. No dead ends, no going back. On your marks.

Welcome to the eighth floor! It's your own planet, a few weeks before I arrived. Everybody's here, going about their business, and none of them know. Look, don't touch: anything you take from them turns to dust when the floor goes. Oh, and it's a card game now. Every monster down here was somebody's folk tale. Catch them, deal them, lose them.

Welcome to Faction Wars, the main event! Nine armies camped around a city, a castle at the bottom of it, and thirty days to take it. You're soldiers now. Pick a side, or get drafted by one. Oh, and one teensy rule change this season: nobody respawns. Not you. Not them. Enjoy the war.

Floor ten is a race! Pick a ride, bolt on an upgrade after every heat, and get from the start to the finish. The rules could not be simpler. Don't come in last. Everybody who comes in last dies. Everybody else gets to do it again, somewhere worse.

Welcome to the eleventh floor, and the party of the season! Build a float, join the procession, and ride it all the way to the arena. Everything you sent down from the floor above is waiting for you there, and so is the boss. The judges are ready. Are you?
